+## 3. Exact input and resource contract
+
+At a specified cut, one replica has classical-quantum state
+
+\[
+ \rho_{CRSE}=\sum_c p_c |c\rangle\langle c|\otimes\rho^c_{RSE}.
+\]
+
+Required resources:
+
+- N independent preparations from this same joint ensemble, not merely identical reduced states. These are preparations, not clones of one unknown input.
+- The classical records C are available before routing. No new measurement of S, R or E is needed for the selection rule. A noisy record is allowed: the target is conditional on the actually recorded value, not an imaginary error-free label.
+- Calibrated interchangeable sites and continuation dynamics. Site heterogeneity must be included explicitly or bounded; calling modules replicas does not establish this.
+- A physical permutation of the S registers whose net joint action, relative to a matched-duration reference evolution, is close enough to the intended permutation and leaves the relevant environment dynamics unchanged. Reduced-system gate fidelity is insufficient; see Section 9.
+- Independent batches, or an independently justified alternative concentration argument, for the stated sampling bounds.
+- A fixed, bounded scored continuation. Corrected detector estimates with a wider range require the corresponding wider-range concentration bound.
+
+Reference R may be an idle register entangled with S. It need not move. Its identity must follow the quantum state that originated with it. An arbitrary entangled collection of different jobs is not a supply of independent replicas.
+
+## 4. Physical construction
+
+For each batch, group replica indices by the observed value c. If a group has at least two members, cyclically permute their S registers so that no register stays at its original site. Leave singleton groups untouched. Record the source-to-destination map.
+
+If site i receives S from source j, continue the experiment at site i with its resident environment E_i, but score the resulting data register against reference R_j. Match C_i=C_j. All systems are retained; there is no selection on success or on convenient labels.
+
+A k-member cyclic permutation can be compiled using k-1 block swaps. Gate count, routing topology, idle time, controller latency and reference storage are resources, not free primitives. For an m-qubit data block the operation must exchange the entire relevant block.
+
+## 5. Acquisition identity and proof
+
+For independent replicas i and j with the same observed c, their joint conditioned state is
+
+\[
+ \rho^c_{R_iS_iE_i}\otimes\rho^c_{R_jS_jE_j}.
+\]
+
+After exchanging S_i and S_j, tracing all unused systems and retaining the recipient data S_i together with donor reference R_j gives
+
+\[
+ \rho_{R_jS_iE_i}'=\rho^c_{RS}\otimes\rho^c_E.
+\]
+
+The reason is exact: R_j and the state delivered into S_i originate in copy j, while E_i originates in an independent copy i. The partial traces factor. No microscopic state label, trajectory, eigenbasis measurement or tomography enters the proof.
+
+Following the recipient's old reference R_i instead would generally destroy the intended data-reference marginal. Reference tracking is therefore part of the operation, not an optional bookkeeping improvement.
+
+With indefinitely available matching partners, the tagged output state is
+
+\[
+ \mathcal G_C(\rho)=\sum_c p_c |c\rangle\langle c|
+       \otimes\rho^c_{RS}\otimes\rho^c_E.
+\]
+
+This preserves the CR S and CE marginals and the frequency of each observed condition. It removes associations between RS and E conditional on that observed condition. It does not erase global correlations among all output replicas: they can be relocated across sites.
+
+The expression is nonlinear as a function of one unknown input density matrix. Its implementation consumes multiple independent preparations; no universal nonlinear single-copy quantum channel is being postulated.

+### Finite batch, including rare conditions
+
+A tagged replica with condition c has no partner with probability
+
+\[
+ a_c(N)=(1-p_c)^{N-1}.
+\]
+
+Therefore the average tagged output is exactly
+
+\[

+\]
+
+Each two-arm contrast has statistical radius 2r. Add bounded systematic biases for each arm. Inferring a fully decorrelated contrast also requires 2s_N, using an upper confidence bound on s_N rather than an unqualified plug-in estimate.
+
+Illustration only: B=4000, N=32, delta=0.05 gives r=0.0251872, two-arm radius 0.0503745, and 4BN=512000 prepared replicas. This is a conservative sufficient accounting example with independent batches, not a measured sample requirement or an estimate of laboratory wall time. It excludes gate, detector, batch-independence, module-mismatch and environmental-control systematic errors.
+
+A bounded joint preparation discrepancy epsilon_p, joint implementation discrepancy epsilon_g, matched-continuation discrepancy epsilon_f and readout bias epsilon_m yield a task score bias at most their sum, using trace-distance/diamond-distance normalization appropriate to [0,1] effects. Such bounds must be justified on the relevant joint states, not inferred from reduced gate benchmarking.
+
+Costs include duplicated or buffered modules, initial preparation, reference storage, measured condition acquisition, classical matching, real register exchanges, idle dephasing, detector calibration, reset/cooling and repetition of complete histories. Finite-batch sparsity and rare conditions may defeat the scheme. There is no established dimension-independent total-cost advantage.
+
+Preserved local marginals do not imply preserved interaction energy. For a system-bath coupling H_SE, the intended change can include
+
+\[
+ \Delta E_{int}=\sum_c p_c Tr[H_{SE}(\rho_S^c\otimes\rho_E^c-\rho_{SE}^c)].
+\]
+
+Switching work and altered couplings must be included. Nothing here implies free decorrelation, heat extraction or a thermodynamic advantage.
+
+## 11. Comparison that must be passed
+
+The evaluation must include direct randomized testing of actual continuation policies; state-matched causal breaks where affordable; targeted non-Markovian response matrices; unconditioned multi-copy decorrelation; standard dynamical decoupling and motional/routing controls; and applicable calibration-free non-Markovian noise-suppression protocols.
+
+A conventional reset of S can destroy entanglement with its reference. The proposed bookkeeping preserves the donor RS marginal instead. This identifies a potentially different experimental access contract, not a universal separation from every existing protocol. When conditional states are simple or known, a conventional state-matched preparation may be cheaper. When quantum correlations are inaccessible experimentally, a simulation assuming them does not supply the missing access.
+
+For a small controlled bath, first hide its parameters from the diagnostic procedure but permit independent validation on separate runs. Demonstrate the acquisition identity, the independent-source condition, reference pairing and a bound on gate-induced environmental changes. Then remove the privileged environmental audit only when a transferable bound is justified. Passing the small controlled test would establish an implementation, not a useful scalable technology.
+
+A consequential validation must show that information from the assay leads to a preregistered improvement in a held-out controller or workload compared with a cost-matched baseline. If direct policy trials or existing response measurements achieve the same decision at lower total cost, terminate the advantage claim even if the mathematical identity remains correct.
+
+## 12. Negative research capital from the screen
+
+The preceding solar-cell route considered a common selector followed by two calibrated reference outcomes. Under an exact common-selection and no-collateral-effect contract, D_j=M(r_j-q) gives M=(D_1-D_0)/(r_1-r_0) and q=(r_0D_1-r_1D_0)/(D_1-D_0). This algebra alone does not acquire M or prove a valid selector. With interactions, the inferred q is a net causal value rather than necessarily a carrier probability. Most importantly, an occupied carrier's rescue value does not identify the value of structurally passivating its trap: the latter changes capture, electrostatics and available pathways.
+
+Strong photovoltaic comparators include Pan et al., *Operando dynamics of trapped carriers in perovskite solar cells observed via infrared optical activation spectroscopy*, Nature Communications 14, 8000 (2023), DOI 10.1038/s41467-023-43852-5, and Zhang et al., *Overcoming the fill-factor limit of organic solar cells*, Nature Photonics (2026), DOI 10.1038/s41566-026-01946-8. The latter combines several experimental methods rather than using an intentionally weak single-measurement baseline. No distinct, acquired, decision-changing advantage for the proposed dual-reference trap assay was established; that route was not promoted.
+
+Astra's temporal isotope programme supplies the related observation-map warning, not a theorem about the new system. Its N813 dossier retains real whole-parent acquisition and cost-matched decision gates. Neutral entry-history labels should not be treated as labels of internal causal importance.
+
+## 13. Verification and continuation obligations
+
+`verify.py` uses NumPy and the standard library. It checks the exact two-copy identity for 32 random mixed RSE states with dimensions (2,2,3), reference preservation, rational finite-batch formulas, exhaustive small-batch label enumeration, the Bell-phase decision witness, the shared-hidden-bit failure and the invisible-bath-gate failure. The saved output is `verification_results.json`.
+
+These checks verify finite instances and implementation consistency. The factorization and finite-batch proofs above establish the stated identities mathematically; external proof review remains absent. None of the checks verifies priority, experimental feasibility, a real material mechanism, or advantage over existing methods.
+
+The next necessary evidence is not a larger ideal simulation. It is a same-platform environmental-action certificate and a specified held-out decision comparator. Until those are acquired, retain this as a conditional candidate, not as a breakthrough, validated technology or completed mission.

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Reproducible finite checks for condition-matched quantum state exchange.
+
+These are synthetic linear-algebra checks, NOT hardware data, a novelty proof,
+or a comparison with the strongest experimentally available protocols.
+Requires Python 3.10+ and NumPy. Run: python verify.py
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+import json
+from fractions import Fraction
+from itertools import product
+from pathlib import Path
+import numpy as np
+
+TOL = 2e-12
+RNG = np.random.default_rng(20261015)
+
+
+def density(v: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
+    return np.outer(v, v.conj())
+
+
+def tensor(*ops: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
+    out = np.array([[1.0 + 0j]])
+    for op in ops:
+        out = np.kron(out, op)
+    return out
+
+
+def marginal(rho: np.ndarray, dims: tuple[int, ...], keep: tuple[int, ...]) -> np.ndarray:
+    """Partial trace, preserving the requested order of retained subsystems."""
+    if len(set(keep)) != len(keep) or any(k < 0 or k >= len(dims) for k in keep):
+        raise ValueError("Invalid retained-subsystem indices")
+    dim = int(np.prod(dims))
+    if rho.shape != (dim, dim):
+        raise ValueError("Density matrix shape does not match subsystem dimensions")
+    rest = tuple(k for k in range(len(dims)) if k not in keep)
+    order = keep + rest
+    kdim = int(np.prod([dims[k] for k in keep]))
+    rdim = int(np.prod([dims[k] for k in rest]))
+    arr = rho.reshape(dims + dims).transpose(order + tuple(k + len(dims) for k in order))
+    return np.trace(arr.reshape(kdim, rdim, kdim, rdim), axis1=1, axis2=3)
+
+
+def swap_matrix(dims: tuple[int, ...], a: int, b: int) -> np.ndarray:
+    if dims[a] != dims[b]:
+        raise ValueError("Swapped subsystems must have equal dimensions")
+    dim = int(np.prod(dims))
+    result = np.zeros((dim, dim), dtype=complex)
+    for i in range(dim):
+        coord = list(np.unravel_index(i, dims))
+        coord[a], coord[b] = coord[b], coord[a]
+        result[np.ravel_multi_index(tuple(coord), dims), i] = 1
+    return result
+
+
+def apply_permutation(rho: np.ndarray, unitary: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
+    # All unitaries passed here are computational-basis permutation matrices.
+    order = np.argmax(unitary, axis=1)
+    return rho[np.ix_(order, order)]
+
+
+def td(a: np.ndarray, b: np.ndarray) -> float:
+    delta = (a-b + (a-b).conj().T)/2
+    return float(np.abs(np.linalg.eigvalsh(delta)).sum()/2)
+
+
+def random_state(dim: int) -> np.ndarray:
+    m = RNG.normal(size=(dim, dim)) + 1j*RNG.normal(size=(dim, dim))
+    rho = m @ m.conj().T
+    return rho / np.trace(rho)
+
+
+I2 = np.eye(2, dtype=complex)
+X = np.array([[0,1],[1,0]], dtype=complex)
+P0, P1 = np.diag([1.,0.]), np.diag([0.,1.])
+PLUS = np.array([1,0,0,1], dtype=complex)/np.sqrt(2)
+MINUS = np.array([1,0,0,-1], dtype=complex)/np.sqrt(2)
+BELL = density(PLUS)
+BELL_MINUS = density(MINUS)
+CZ = np.diag([1.,1.,1.,-1.])
+ECHO = tensor(I2, CZ)  # subsystem order R,S,E
+BELL_READ = tensor(BELL, I2)
+
+
+def memory_state(u: float) -> np.ndarray:
+    return (1-u)*tensor(BELL, P0) + u*tensor(BELL_MINUS, P1)
+
+
+def bell_success(rho: np.ndarray, echo: bool) -> float:
+    state = ECHO @ rho @ ECHO.conj().T if echo else rho
+    return float(np.trace(BELL_READ @ state).real)
+
+
+def run() -> dict:
+    results: dict = {
+        "scope": "Synthetic finite checks; no experimental data and no novelty/advantage certification",
+        "seed": 20261015,
+    }
+    # 1. An arbitrary mixed RSE state, including quantum correlations, not only a classical toy.
+    max_error = 0.0
+    max_rs_error = 0.0
+    for _ in range(32):
+        dims = (2,2,3)
+        rho = random_state(12)
+        pair = tensor(rho, rho)
+        sw = swap_matrix(dims+dims, 1, 4)
+        exchanged = apply_permutation(pair, sw)
+        # Recipient site 1 now contains donor S2: follow donor reference R2.
+        graft = marginal(exchanged, dims+dims, (3,1,2))
+        target = tensor(marginal(rho, dims, (0,1)), marginal(rho, dims, (2,)))
+        max_error = max(max_error, td(graft, target))
+        max_rs_error = max(max_rs_error, td(marginal(graft, dims, (0,1)), marginal(rho,dims,(0,1))))
+    assert max_error < TOL and max_rs_error < TOL
+    results["random_quantum_identity"] = {
+        "instances":32, "dimensions_R_S_E":[2,2,3],
+        "maximum_trace_distance": max_error,
+        "maximum_reference_system_marginal_error":max_rs_error,
+    }
+    # 2. Exact rational decision-reversal model.
+    p = [Fraction(9,10), Fraction(1,10)]
+    u = [Fraction(1,5), Fraction(2,5)]
+    prod_echo = [(1-x)**2+x*x for x in u]
+    native_echo = Fraction(1)
+    isolate = sum(pc*(1-uc) for pc,uc in zip(p,u))
+    ideal_echo = sum(pc*f for pc,f in zip(p,prod_echo))
+    rows = []
+    for n in [2,4,8,16,32,64]:
+        a = [(1-pc)**(n-1) for pc in p]
+        singleton_mass = sum(pc*ac for pc,ac in zip(p,a))
+        f = sum(pc*(ac+(1-ac)*fc) for pc,ac,fc in zip(p,a,prod_echo))
+        assert native_echo > isolate > f
+        assert abs(f-ideal_echo) <= singleton_mass
+        rows.append({"batch_size":n,"singleton_mass":float(singleton_mass),
+                     "echo_fidelity":float(f),"isolate_fidelity":float(isolate),
+                     "echo_fidelity_exact":str(f)})
+    # Independently enumerate all classical label configurations for small batches.
+    max_enum_error = 0.0
+    for n in range(2,9):
+        numerical = 0.0
+        for labels in product(range(2), repeat=n):
+            prob = float(np.prod([float(p[c]) for c in labels]))
+            scores = [1.0 if labels.count(c)==1 else float(prod_echo[c]) for c in labels]
+            numerical += prob*sum(scores)/n
+        formula = sum(float(pc)*((1-float(pc))**(n-1)
+                    +(1-(1-float(pc))**(n-1))*float(fc)) for pc,fc in zip(p,prod_echo))
+        max_enum_error=max(max_enum_error, abs(numerical-formula))
+    assert max_enum_error < TOL
+    quantum_error = 0.0
+    for x in u:
+        rho = memory_state(float(x))
+        prod_rho = tensor(marginal(rho,(2,2,2),(0,1)), marginal(rho,(2,2,2),(2,)))
+        quantum_error=max(quantum_error, abs(bell_success(rho,True)-1),
+                          abs(bell_success(rho,False)-float(1-x)),
+                          abs(bell_success(prod_rho,True)-float((1-x)**2+x*x)))
+    assert quantum_error < TOL
+    results["decision_reversal"] = {
+        "flag_probabilities":[float(x) for x in p],
+        "residual_phase_probabilities":[float(x) for x in u],
+        "native_echo":float(native_echo),"native_isolate":float(isolate),
+        "ideal_exchange_echo":float(ideal_echo),"ideal_exchange_isolate":float(isolate),
+        "finite_batches":rows,
+        "label_enumeration_maximum_error":max_enum_error,
+        "density_matrix_maximum_error":quantum_error,
+        "warning":"The engineered model is already soluble and has no demonstrated baseline advantage.",
+    }
+    # 3. A positive naive exchange signal without conditional correlations.
+    results["conditioning_false_positive"] = {
+        "state":"C is uniform; given C=c, S=c and E=c deterministically",
+        "future_score":"Probability that S equals E",
+        "native":1.0,"conditional_exchange":1.0,"unconditional_exchange":0.5,
+    }
+    # 4. Identical one-replica marginals do NOT establish independent replicas.
+    v0, v1 = tensor(BELL,P0), tensor(BELL_MINUS,P1)
+    up = 0.2
+    correlated_pair = (1-up)*tensor(v0,v0) + up*tensor(v1,v1)
+    dims6 = (2,)*6
+    sw = swap_matrix(dims6,1,4)
+    actual = marginal(apply_permutation(correlated_pair,sw),dims6,(3,1,2))
+    independent_prediction = (1-up)**2+up*up
+    actual_score = bell_success(actual,True)
+    assert abs(actual_score-1)<TOL
+    results["replica_dependence_counterexample"] = {
+        "each_replica_state": "(1-u)|Phi+><Phi+| tensor |0><0| + u|Phi-><Phi-| tensor |1><1|",
+        "u":up,"independent_prediction":independent_prediction,
+        "common_hidden_bit_actual_echo":actual_score,
+        "error":actual_score-independent_prediction,
+    }
+    # 5. Perfect reduced SWAP and perfect round-trip do not bound hidden-bath disturbance.
+    start = tensor(v0,v0)
+    flip_baths = tensor(I2,I2,X,I2,I2,X)
+    bad = flip_baths @ sw
+    final = apply_permutation(start,bad)
+    bad_local = marginal(final,dims6,(3,1,2))
+    ideal_local = marginal(apply_permutation(start,sw),dims6,(3,1,2))
+    bad_score = bell_success(bad_local,True)
+    ideal_score = bell_success(ideal_local,True)
+    round_trip = float(np.linalg.norm(bad @ bad - np.eye(64)))
+    assert abs(bad_score)<TOL and abs(ideal_score-1)<TOL and round_trip<TOL
+    reduced_gate_error=0.0
+    for _ in range(10):
+        arbitrary = random_state(64)
+        after_bad=apply_permutation(arbitrary,bad)
+        after_good=apply_permutation(arbitrary,sw)
+        # Entire accessible R1,S1,R2,S2 channel is identical even for correlated inputs.
+        reduced_gate_error=max(reduced_gate_error,
+            td(marginal(after_bad,dims6,(0,1,3,4)),marginal(after_good,dims6,(0,1,3,4))))
+    assert reduced_gate_error<TOL
+    results["hidden_bath_gate_counterexample"]={
+        "implemented_gate":"SWAP(S1,S2) tensor X(E1) tensor X(E2)",
+        "ideal_future_echo_fidelity":ideal_score,"bad_future_echo_fidelity":bad_score,
+        "round_trip_operator_error":round_trip,
+        "accessible_channel_maximum_error":reduced_gate_error,
+    }
+    # Conservative independent-batch Hoeffding accounting; no within-batch iid claim.
+    B,N,K,delta=4000,32,4,.05
+    r=float(np.sqrt(np.log(2*K/delta)/(2*B)))
+    results["conservative_sampling_example"]={
+        "batches_per_arm":B,"replicas_per_batch":N,"arms":K,
+        "failure_probability":delta,"per_arm_radius":r,
+        "two_arm_statistical_radius":2*r,"prepared_replicas":B*N*K,
+        "scope":"Assumed independent batches, bounded unbiased scores, fixed policies; excludes systematic errors.",
+    }
+    results["all_assertions_passed"] = True
+    return results
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    data=run()
+    target=Path(__file__).with_name("verification_results.json")
+    target.write_text(json.dumps(data,indent=2)+"\n",encoding="utf-8")
+    print(json.dumps(data,indent=2))

+3. The operation
+Prepare several independent instances of the same experiment. “Independent” here means independent joint preparations, including their relevant environments—not merely matching qubit measurement statistics.
+Within each batch:
+1. Group instances by the actual recorded value of \(C\).
+2. Within each group containing at least two instances, cyclically exchange the \(S\) registers so that none remains with its original environment.
+3. Leave singleton groups unchanged rather than discarding them.
+4. Continue each experiment, tracking each transferred state’s original reference register.
+For example, after transferring \(S_j\) to the site containing \(E_i\), score it against \(R_j\), not \(R_i\).
+This is a physical exchange of quantum states. It is not a statistical reshuffling of completed measurement records.

+Take two independent instances with the same recorded condition \(c\):
+\[
+\rho^c_{R_iS_iE_i}\otimes\rho^c_{R_jS_jE_j}.

+\boxed{
+\rho'_{R_jS_iE_i}
+=
+\rho^c_{RS}\otimes\rho^c_E.

+=
+\frac{10^{-6}}{600\,p}.

+M_{\mathrm{req}}
+=

+M_{\mathrm{req,pulsed}}
+=
+3.76\times10^{-5}\ \mathrm{m^4/(J\,s)}.

+\Delta V^\ddagger
+\gtrsim

+Hurlbut and colleagues measured two- and three-photon absorption in GaAs across the mid-infrared using 100 fs pulses. Later measurements and modeling also explicitly include free-carrier absorption generated by multiphoton excitation. PubMed

+\alpha_3=0.35\ \mathrm{cm^3/GW^2},

+\alpha_3I^2\simeq6.71\ \mathrm{cm^{-1}}.
+\]
+Thus, even an optically thin layer can absorb substantial power at the required intensity. This is not a hot-material loss prediction; it is evidence against treating a sub-bandgap beam as lossless. arXiv
+The temperature mismatch is central. The demonstrated boundary dissolution uses hot GaAs. Published analysis shows that the two-photon and free-carrier absorption depend on temperature, wavelength and carrier state. A room-temperature optical coefficient cannot simply be paired with high-temperature structural mobility. AIP Publishing
+Moving to longer wavelengths may change the balance. It does not establish a solution without measuring the resulting nonlinear coupling, carrier absorption and both-beam losses in the same regime.
+4. The coupled physical model—not an independently optimized machine
+The scalar pressure formula is an explanatory limit. A frequency-dispersive implementation should instead be formulated through a calibrated interaction Hamiltonian.
+Let \(X\) describe boundary position, and let \(a,b\) be optical modes at \(\omega,2\omega\). A candidate conservative coupling is
+\[
+H_{\mathrm{int}}
+=
+\hbar\left[
+g(X)b^\dagger a^2+
+g^*(X)b(a^\dagger)^2
+\right].
+\]
+The boundary changes the spatial overlap of the sign-changing nonlinear response with the optical fields. For coherent amplitudes \(\alpha,\beta\),
+\[
+F_X
+=
+-2\hbar\operatorname{Re}
+\left[g'(X)\beta^*\alpha^2\right].
+\]
+This is the force expression to calibrate or derive microscopically. Substituting an arbitrary tabulated second-harmonic coefficient into the earlier scalar formula is not a substitute for that calculation.
+The optical amplitudes themselves respond to the interaction:
+\[
+\dot\alpha
+=
+(i\Delta_1-\kappa_1/2)\alpha
+-i2g^*\alpha^*\beta
++\sqrt{\kappa_{1e}}\,s_1,
+\]
+\[
+\dot\beta
+=
+(i\Delta_2-\kappa_2/2)\beta
+-ig\alpha^2
++\sqrt{\kappa_{2e}}\,s_2.
+\]

+\[
+\dot X
+=
+\mathcal V
+\left(
+p_\phi+p_{\mathrm{capillary}}+p_{\mathrm{stress}},

+\right),
+\]
+\[
+C_V\dot T
+=
+\nabla\!\cdot(k\nabla T)
++
+q_{\mathrm{abs}}(\alpha,\beta,T,n)
++
+q_{\mathrm{diss}},
+\]
+\[
+\dot n
+=
+G_{\mathrm{abs}}(\alpha,\beta,T,n)-R(n,T).

+There are two already serious practical baselines: optimized dark annealing and growth that prevents the boundaries. Both have published GaAs demonstrations. Springer

+=
+-sd_{\mathrm{eff}}E\sigma,

+=

+\qquad

Nevertheless, it invalidates the assumption that coherent light is the only available polarity-conjugate actuator.

+6. The decisive experiment: retained, phase-selected structure
+The experiment should be designed to distinguish two claims:
+1. A phase-dependent intervention changes boundary behavior.
+2. The proposed reactive optical pressure produces a retained useful transformation.
+The first is not sufficient evidence for the second.
+Establish the operating window before attempting a device
+Use a specimen with an independently mapped boundary and a physically available exit or annihilation path. Measure the two-color nonlinear response, absorbed power, local temperature, carrier response and boundary kinetics under the same conditions.
+A boundary anchored by its topology or interface registry cannot be treated as a freely translating wall. Nor can an overall decrease in boundary density be converted into a universal directional mobility.
+For the illustrative \(1\,\mu\mathrm m\)-in-600-s target, the measured response must support the required displacement while remaining within the sample’s thermal, optical and mechanical limits. If it does not, stop that implementation.

+Use matched regions or specimens rather than assuming that reversing the phase on an irreversibly altered boundary reproduces the original initial condition.
+Compare phase settings separated by \(\pi\), a quadrature setting, loss of mutual coherence, each color separately and optimized dark annealing. Include the stress–electric-field comparator when experimentally compatible.

+Equal incident intensities do not establish equal heating or equal carrier excitation. A phase-dependent absorption pathway could mimic phase-selected motion. Temperature, absorption, carriers and strain must be measured sufficiently well to exclude that explanation—or the observed mechanism must be relabeled rather than claimed as confirmation of conservative optical pressure.

+The success criterion should be a predeclared region acquiring the selected polarity after illumination and annealing cease, with retention over a relevant time and temperature interval.

+Not yet.
+The positive result is a concrete route from a measured symmetry-sensitive interaction to an outcome-selective force. Its direction is not an arbitrary fitted “repair selectivity.” The candidate also has a real structural precedent in its first proposed material.
+The negative results are equally consequential. The simple short-pulse implementation has a severe duty-cycle penalty. Strong internal fields need not provide strong boundary pressure. The hot structural regime and the optical-loss regime have not been qualified together. Existing growth and annealing methods already set a demanding baseline, and an electromechanical actuator could supply a comparable symmetry-selective bias.
+A successful GaAs experiment would establish a narrow physical capability. It would not establish a general atom assembler, arbitrary defect repair, an energy-generation technology or a path to civilization-scale manufacturing by itself.
+The broader hypothesis worth retaining is more precise:
+A structural distinction invisible to ordinary linear driving may become controllable through an externally imposed field product that couples to a sign-changing material response.

+For that to become a major manufacturing principle, the material must simultaneously possess a sufficiently strong response, an accessible structural pathway, tolerable losses and a useful retained endpoint. Transfer to another material requires reacquiring those conditions; shared symmetry is not enough.
+My present decision is to retain phase-directed polarity rewriting as a falsifiable mechanism, but not promote the GaAs optical implementation as a breakthrough or build a larger apparatus concept around it. The decisive missing result is a same-regime measurement showing that the available phase-selective bias can complete a useful retained transformation faster, more selectively or at lower total cost than the strongest compatible alternative.
+The literature establishes relevant ingredients and serious competitors. It does not establish their coexistence in that successful operation.

+# Astra Meta-Genesis: locality rigidity, critical trace concentration, and free-time profile actions
+
+Research date: 15 October 2026.
+
+## Status
+
+The complete implication from rank-one convexity to quasiconvexity for the nine-coefficient left-SO(2)-invariant homogeneous quartic cone is **not established**. No rigorously negative compatible closed cycle was obtained. This investigation did not construct the requested universal compensation potential.
+
+The strongest proved result concerns what such a potential must represent. A smooth profile potential obtained by integrating a density depending on the profile and its first transverse derivative exists at a fixed affine background **if and only if the integrand has a determinant-affine supporting inequality there**. Requiring this at every background supplies a polyconvex lift. Thus this natural continuum extension of the finite-library potential cannot prove the non-polyconvex part of the problem.
+
+There is also an explicit compatible trace-concentration obstruction. For the Dacorogna–Marcellini endpoint, negative transitions from zero to positive-winding profiles, and from negative-winding profiles to zero, survive at the critical W^(3/4,4) trace scale. Any globally dominating profile potential is neither weakly lower nor weakly upper semicontinuous at zero in that space. It cannot be continuous in any W^(s,4), s<3/4, or depend continuously on finitely many weakly continuous measurements. These are obstructions to classes of certificates, **not** quasiconvexity counterexamples. The endpoint's quasiconvexity is a published prior result; the no-go proofs use its explicit formula and do not assume that result.
+
+Two nonlocal candidates were confronted. A fixed scalar multiple of the orientation-odd Poisson-extension action cannot be a universal linear calibration across the cone, even allowing a fixed Poisson rate: explicit convex quartics defeat it. A concrete multi-frequency test also disproves the initially tested coefficient for the isotropic Dacorogna–Marcellini endpoint itself. Correct critical scaling is therefore necessary but insufficient.
+
+Finally, convex timing yields an exact free-duration reduction, including a scalar quartic equation for each nondegenerate strip and a support-function description of its instantaneous geometric action. This was used in continuous-geometry closed-cycle searches, including an alternating search over the full acoustic coefficient cone. All retained cycle gaps were positive. One rational five-profile cycle was independently reconstructed and its complete affine optimum certified positive. No positive finite result is promoted to a continuum theorem.
+
+The included exact verifier passed ten groups checking the finite identities and countertests. The analytic proofs below are not delegated to symbolic computation. No external review, proof-assistant verification, or historical priority clearance is claimed. No repository was modified.
+
+## 1. Reconstructing the profile formulation
+
+Let y have period 2pi and let E_y denote normalized averaging. For a profile U(y) and profile velocity V(y), define
+
+    L_B(U,V) = E_y [F(B+(V|U_y))-F(B)].                    (1.1)
+
+A scalar functional P_B on smooth periodic profiles is called dominating if, for every compatible strip Phi on [0,T] x T,
+
+    P_B(Phi(T,.))-P_B(Phi(0,.))
+       <= integral_0^T L_B(Phi(x,.),Phi_x(x,.)) dx.       (1.2)
+
+If P_B is differentiable along all smooth profile directions, its differential version is
+
+    DP_B(U)[V] <= L_B(U,V)                                (1.3)
+
+for every U,V. Integrating (1.3) implies (1.2); conversely short straight profile paths yield (1.3) when the derivatives and action are continuous. Closed paths eliminate the potential, so (1.2) proves Jensen at B. Existence of an unrestricted P_B is not assumed merely from rank-one convexity.
+
+Write P=(Phi_x|0), Q=(0|Phi_y), and
+
+    R_F(C,Z)=F(C+Z)-F(C)-DF(C)[Z].
+
+Both P and Q have rank at most one. Direct subtraction gives
+
+    F(B+P+Q)-F(B)
+      = R_F(B+Q,P)+R_F(B,Q)+DF(B+Q)[P]+DF(B)[Q].          (1.4)
+
+The final term averages to zero. The remaining linear term is the circulation of
+
+    alpha_(F,B)(U)[V] = E_y DF(B+(0|U_y))[(V|0)].         (1.5)
+
+Thus the prior identity is correct: it retains a joint signed circulation and two nonnegative rank-one remainders. Cancellation of polynomial circulation through degree three is sufficient for quartic Jensen, but is not automatic for profiles. A no-negative-cycle certificate on a fixed graph supplies (1.2) only for the tested transitions and does not address profiles outside that graph.
+
+The full prior PROFILE_CIRCULATION.md was read. Its nine-group verifier was replayed successfully, including reconstruction of all 32,805 edge inequalities. +
+## 2. First-derivative local storage is exactly a polyconvex support
+
+This result holds without rotational symmetry, homogeneity, or a rank-one-convexity assumption. The latter is irrelevant because the existence of the proposed storage is itself a strong condition.
+
+### Theorem 2.1 (local storage rigidity)
+
+Let F:R^(2x2)->R be C^2 and fix B. The following are equivalent.
+
+(a) There is p in C^3(R^2 x R^2) such that
+
+    P(U)=E_y p(U,U_y)
+
+satisfies (1.3) for every smooth periodic U,V.
+
+(b) There is a real number kappa such that, for every matrix X,
+
+    F(B+X)-F(B)-DF(B):X >= kappa det X.                   (2.1)
+
+If (b) holds, an explicit storage is
+
+    P(U)=F_1(B).E_y U + (kappa/2) E_y det(U,U_y),         (2.2)
+
+where F_1(B) is the derivative with respect to the first column.
+
+A periodic explicit dependence p(y,U,U_y) does not enlarge the existence class: average a proposed functional over transverse translations of U. Invariance of L_B under those translations preserves domination and produces an autonomous density.
+
+### Proof
+
+Write z=U and q=U_y. Integration by parts gives the Euler derivative
+
+    DP(U)[V] = E_y [p_z - p_(qz) U_y - p_(qq) U_yy].V.  (2.3)
+
+First prove p_(qq)=0. Fix z0 and smooth periodic w,v, and let
+
+    U_N(y)=z0+N^(-1)w(Ny),   V_N(y)=v(Ny).
+
+The left side of (1.3), namely L_B(U_N,V_N), stays bounded as N grows, because U_N,y=w'(Ny), V_N=v(Ny). In (2.3), all terms stay bounded except possibly
+
+    -N E_y [p_(qq)(z0,w') w''].v + O(1).
+
+Apply domination to V_N and -V_N. The displayed leading coefficient must vanish. Since v is arbitrary,
+
+    p_(qq)(z0,w'(y)) w''(y)=0
+
+pointwise. A smooth periodic w can have any prescribed w'(0)=q0 and w''(0)=h0: make those jets locally and adjust w' away from the point to have zero mean. Therefore p_(qq)(z0,q0)h0=0 for every z0,q0,h0, proving p_(qq)=0.
+
+It follows that
+
+    p(z,q)=A(z).q+c(z).
+
+The Euler derivative becomes
+
+    DP(U)[V] = E_y [grad c(U).V + k(U) det(V,U_y)],       (2.4)
+
+where k(z)=partial_1 A_2-partial_2 A_1. For constant U=z and constant V=epsilon a, differentiation of the two signs of epsilon in (1.3) gives
+
+    grad c(z)=F_1(B)
+
+for every z.
+
+Again take U_N=z0+w(Ny)/N and V_N=v(Ny), now in (2.4), and pass to the limit. For every smooth zero-mean q=w' and every smooth v,

+
+Fix arbitrary vectors v0,q0. In a fraction theta of a period take (v,q)=(v0,q0); on the remainder take (v,q)=(0,-theta q0/(1-theta)). Smooth approximations preserve the inequality and the zero mean of q. Dividing (2.5) by theta and letting theta decrease to zero gives
+
+    F(B+(v0|q0))-F(B)-F_1(B).v0-F_2(B).q0
+       >= k(z0) det(v0,q0).

+This is (2.1). No compactness of gradient laws, quasiconvex Jensen theorem, or unproved moment completion was used.
+
+Conversely, the first variation of (2.2) is
+
+    DP(U)[V] = F_1(B).E_y V+kappa E_y det(V,U_y).
+
+Integrate (2.1) with X=(V|U_y). The F_2(B).U_y term has zero average, proving (1.3). QED.
+
+### Corollary 2.2 (all backgrounds force polyconvexity)
+

+

+    g(A,det A)=F(A).

Existence at every background again yields a convex lift in the entries and minors.

+For a homogeneous quartic with F(A_*)<0, no coefficient k can satisfy F(X)>=k det X for all X: set X=tA_* and let t grow. Therefore no first-derivative local storage exists at B=0. This rules out arbitrary smooth densities p(U,U_y), not just a fixed polynomial degree.

+## 3. An exact trace-concentration obstruction for a quasiconvex energy
+
+Let

+    F_DM(A)=|A|^4-(4/sqrt(3))|A|^2 det A.                  (3.1)
+

+
+    12(a-d/sqrt(3))^2
+      +2(1+1/sqrt(3))(b+c)^2

+
+### 3.1 Negative entry and exit strips
+
+Set U_+(y)=(cos y,sin y). On 0<=x<=2 use
+
+    Phi_+(x,y)=(x/2)U_+(y).
+
+Writing r=x/2, its columns are (U_+/2 | r J U_+). Thus
+
+    |D Phi_+|^2=1/4+r^2,   det D Phi_+=r/2.

+Exact integration gives

+      =103/120-sqrt(3)/2 = -delta,                        (3.2)
+    delta=sqrt(3)/2-103/120>0.

+The sign follows by squaring: 3/4-(103/120)^2=191/14400>0.
+
+This is a negative transition from 0 to U_+, not a closed test. Simultaneously reverse x and y. The gradient is negated, so the quartic energy is unchanged. This produces a negative transition from U_-(y)=U_+(-y) to 0 with the same action -delta.
+
+### 3.2 Critical concentration of the traces
+
+For integer N>=1 set
+
+    U_N^+(y)=N^(-3/4)U_+(Ny),
+    U_N^-(y)=N^(-3/4)U_-(Ny).
+
+Rescale the two strips by
+
+    Phi_N(x,y)=N^(-3/4) Phi(Nx,Ny),  0<=x<=2/N.
+
+The gradient scales by N^(1/4), the quartic by N, and the x width by N^(-1). Transverse normalized averaging is unchanged. Hence both directed actions remain exactly -delta.
+
+Every dominating profile functional, normalized by P(0)=0, must therefore satisfy
+
+    P(U_N^+) <= -delta,       P(U_N^-) >= delta             (3.3)
+
+for every N.
+
+These conclusions require no differentiability of P and no homogeneous ansatz for P. They follow from open-path domination alone.
+
+### Theorem 3.1 (necessary topology and orientation sensitivity)
+
+A functional satisfying (1.2) for F_DM at B=0:
+
+* cannot be continuous at zero in W^(s,4)(T), for 0<=s<3/4 (nor even uniformly continuous in the profile values alone);
+* is neither sequentially weakly lower nor sequentially weakly upper semicontinuous at zero on W^(3/4,4)(T);
+* cannot be a continuous function of finitely many continuous linear measurements on the critical trace space, or of finitely many weakly continuous measurements;
+* cannot depend only on profile quantities that identify U_N^+ and U_N^-, such as unoriented Sobolev norms.
+
+Proof. For 0<s<1, the Slobodeckij seminorm of a circular mode follows from
+
+    |U_N(y+h)-U_N(y)|=2N^(-3/4)|sin(Nh/2)|.
+
+Changing variables h->Nh in its integral gives
+
+    ||U_N||_(W^(s,4)) = O(N^(s-3/4))+O(N^(-3/4)).          (3.4)
+
+The corresponding seminorm is also bounded below by a positive constant times N^(s-3/4). At s=3/4 the sequence is bounded. Its L4 norm tends to zero, so reflexivity and uniqueness of its distributional limit imply weak convergence to zero in W^(3/4,4). Equations (3.3) then contradict each proposed continuity or semicontinuity property. The two signs exclude lower and upper semicontinuity separately. Finite continuous linear measurements converge to zero along both sequences. QED.
+
+A potential depending only on Fourier modes |n|<=M fails even without continuity: for N>M, its input data agree exactly with those at zero, contradicting (3.3).
+
+Because F_DM is quasiconvex by the separately cited theorem, every compatible transition from U_N^+ to U_N^- has action at least 2delta. Indeed, precede it by the exact negative entry from zero and follow it by the exact negative return to zero. The concatenated field is periodic in x, so its total energy is nonnegative. The two traces both tend uniformly to zero, but this oriented connecting cost cannot vanish. This corollary uses the known endpoint quasiconvexity; the certificate obstructions (3.3) themselves do not.

+### 3.3 The scaling applies far beyond this example
+
+For a real amplitude a and frequency N, the same construction forces

+    P(a U_+(Ny))-P(0) <= -delta a^4 N^3,
+    P(a U_-(Ny))-P(0) >=  delta a^4 N^3.                    (3.5)

The critical exponent 3/4 is the standard trace scaling of W^(1,4) strip energies; it is not a newly invented Sobolev exponent. What is explicit here is the incompatibility of domination with weaker or weakly semicontinuous profile descriptions.
+
+More generally, let F be left-SO(2)-invariant, homogeneous of degree four, and suppose F(A)<0 at an invertible A=(a1|a2). Choose n=sign(det A), v=-J a2/n, and decompose a1=alpha v+beta Jv. Then alpha=det A/(n|v|^2)>0. The potential

+

+For a smooth mean-zero profile define its trace energy by the infimum of integral |D Phi|^4 over finite compatible strips from zero to that profile (arbitrary positive width). For an already quasiconvex F, infimum of incoming actions gives a finite storage: closing an incoming path with one fixed return path bounds it from below. +## 5. What convex timing actually eliminates
+
+This section supplies a useful exact reduction, not existence of a global potential.
+
+### 5.1 Straight-edge timing is completely solvable
+
+For fixed profiles U,V, fixed background B, and local interpolation parameter t in [0,1], set
+
+    P=(V-U|0), Q_t=(0|(1-t)U_y+t V_y).
+
+The action at width tau is
+
+    W_B(tau)=tau integral_0^1 E_y
+                 [F(B+P/tau+Q_t)-F(B)] dt.
+
+Its second derivative is
+
+    W_B''(tau)=tau^(-3) integral_0^1 E_y
+          D^2F(B+P/tau+Q_t)[P,P] dt >=0.                  (5.1)
+
+For a homogeneous quartic and fixed B this has the exact algebraic form
+
+    W_B(tau)=a0 tau+a1+a2/tau+a3/tau^2+a4/tau^3.          (5.2)
+
+The coefficient a0 is nonnegative: at each interpolation profile, convexity in the second column and E_y Q_t=0 give its Jensen bound. The leading coefficient a4 is the mean rank-one value F(P), hence nonnegative. If a0,a4>0, W tends to infinity at both ends and is strictly convex (its analytic nonnegative second derivative cannot vanish on an interval). The unique optimal duration solves
+
+    a0 tau^4-a2 tau^2-2a3 tau-3a4=0.                     (5.3)
+
+Its positive root can be isolated exactly for rational data. Thus a search need not sample a finite width library. At fixed geometry and fixed common B, the optimal durations of all edges are independent convex minimizations. Optimizing B and the profile geometry jointly remains nonconvex.
+
+Degenerate a0=0 or a4=0 cases can have an infimum at zero or infinite duration; they are not silently treated as finite stationary points.
+
+### 5.2 Instantaneous duration elimination is a support function
+
+For a fixed profile U in a finite-dimensional profile subspace, let L(v)=L_B(U,v). It is a finite convex function of v because the varying first column is a rank-one direction, and L(0)>=0 by transverse Jensen. Define
+
+    A(U,w)=inf_(tau>0) tau L(w/tau).                       (5.4)
+
+Let
+
+    H(U,p)=sup_v [p.v-L(v)],
+    Z(U)={p:H(U,p)<=0}.
+
+Then
+
+    A(U,w)=sup_(p in Z(U)) p.w.                            (5.5)
+
+Proof. A supporting slope p0 of L at zero gives L(v)>=L(0)+p0.v, so A is bounded below by p0.w and above by L(w). Its perspective construction is convex and positively homogeneous. Its conjugate is
+
+    A*(p)=sup_(tau>0) tau L*(p),
+
+which is zero when L*(p)<=0 and infinite otherwise. Finite-dimensional convex duality proves (5.5). The same statement holds in the L4/L^(4/3) profile-velocity setting under the usual continuity and quartic-growth hypotheses.
+
+For a prescribed geometric profile path, optimizing the speed amounts to integrating A, with limiting speeds allowed by approximation. This produces a signed Finsler-type action. Domination requires choosing covectors in Z(U) that are the derivative of one global functional. Nonemptiness of each Z(U) does not produce that integrable selection. Thus convex timing removes a real scalar optimization but does not make the circulation problem disappear.
+
+The perspective and conjugacy ingredients are standard convex analysis. Equation (5.5) is not promoted as a solution by reformulating the missing global selection.

+## 7. The exact mathematical state to preserve
+
+What was removed is a broad class of misleading continuum continuations:
+
+1. A smooth storage obtained by integrating p(U,U_y) cannot go beyond determinant-affine support and therefore cannot prove the non-polyconvex part of the full problem.
+2. A potential on a weakly compact or subcritical trace description cannot dominate all profiles even for the known quasiconvex endpoint. Critical, oriented concentration cannot be discarded in a finite-library extension.
+3. A simple fixed Poisson-extension orientation action has the correct homogeneity but fails exact domination tests. Correct topology and frequency order do not by themselves control resonance.
+
+These are rigorous certificate obstructions, not proof of non-quasiconvexity or a universally applicable positive operation.
+
+The most concrete unresolved positive attack is now a genuinely nonlocal critical-trace storage with mixed-frequency terms. For a candidate chosen to respect amplitude homogeneity and spatial dilation, its translation-invariant quartic Fourier kernel must have total frequency order three under simultaneous spatial dilation. At nonzero B, the homogeneous extension would have terms B^(4-j) times j profile factors of frequency order j-1. This is a scaling requirement, not an existence theorem or a prescribed sufficient ansatz. A valid kernel must satisfy the full velocity domination (1.3), retain both frequency orientations, and pass the explicit convex and isotropic tests in Section 4. Choosing its coefficients by quasiconvexity itself would be circular.
+
+A substantive proof would either exhibit a kernel/remainder identity valid uniformly over all frequency configurations and profiles, or prove another constructive nonlocal domination rule. Merely writing the zero-Hamiltonian selection problem in (5.5), or taking an unverified limit of finite graph potentials, does not meet that standard.
+
+The strongest competing negative attack retained here is simultaneous continuous profile-cycle geometry, exact convex timing, and variation over the acoustic coefficient cone, followed by exact reconstruction of any negative candidate. The exact positive five-profile witness is the current completed result of that route; no negative candidate survived even to the exact-certification stage.
+
+There is no evidence from this run that more unconstrained inference using the same local-density, fixed Poisson, or finite-graph architecture will cross the global barrier. Those particular continuations are either disproved or empirically unproductive. Further concentrated work is justified only by a genuinely mixed-frequency critical-trace mechanism or a new negative compatible geometry. No compute-calibrated success probability is claimed. Preserving this state is preferable to repeating the contact and single-carrier investigations.

+"""Exact finite checks for UNIVERSAL_PROFILE_OBSTRUCTIONS.md.
+
+Run with Python 3 and SymPy. No optimization results, prior verifier output,
+or downloaded manuscripts are inputs. These checks do not formalize the
+high-frequency localization, Sobolev weak-convergence, or convex-duality proofs.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+from itertools import product
+import sympy as s
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+REPORT: dict[str, object] = {
+    "status": "running",
+    "scope": "exact finite algebra only; analytic proofs are in the note",
+    "groups": [],
+}
+
+def zero(expr: s.Expr) -> None:
+    assert s.simplify(s.expand(expr)) == 0, s.simplify(expr)
+
+def passed(name: str, **data: object) -> None:
+    item = {"name": name, "passed": True, **data}
+    REPORT["groups"].append(item)
+    print(f"PASS {len(REPORT['groups'])}: {name}", flush=True)
+
+def exponents(n: int, degree: int):
+    for ex in product(range(degree + 1), repeat=n):
+        if sum(ex) == degree:
+            yield ex
+
+def mono(xs, ex):
+    return s.prod(x**e for x, e in zip(xs, ex))
+
+# 1. Column identity, including every homogeneous planar quartic monomial.
+a, b, c, d = x = s.symbols("a b c d", real=True)
+p1, p2, q1, q2 = s.symbols("p1 p2 q1 q2", real=True)
+P = s.Matrix([p1, 0, p2, 0])
+Q = s.Matrix([0, q1, 0, q2])
+X = s.Matrix(x)
+count = 0
+for ex in exponents(4, 4):
+    f = mono(x, ex)
+    df = s.Matrix([s.diff(f, xi) for xi in x])
+    shifted = lambda vec: f.subs(dict(zip(x, vec)), simultaneous=True)
+    dfq = df.subs(dict(zip(x, X + Q)), simultaneous=True)
+    R1 = shifted(X + Q + P) - shifted(X + Q) - dfq.dot(P)
+    R2 = shifted(X + Q) - f - df.dot(Q)
+    zero(shifted(X + P + Q) - f - R1 - R2 - dfq.dot(P) - df.dot(Q))
+    count += 1
+assert count == 35
+passed("two-column circulation bookkeeping", homogeneous_monomials=count)
+
+# 2. Euler derivative: the second-jet coefficient really is -p_qq.
+z = s.symbols("z1 z2", real=True)
+q = s.symbols("q1 q2", real=True)
+h = s.symbols("h1 h2", real=True)
+v = s.symbols("v1 v2", real=True)
+w = s.symbols("w1 w2", real=True)
+xs = z + q
+count = 0
+for deg in range(5):
+    for ex in exponents(4, deg):
+        p = mono(xs, ex)
+        first = sum(s.diff(p,z[i])*v[i]+s.diff(p,q[i])*w[i] for i in range(2))
+        flux = sum(s.diff(p,q[i])*v[i] for i in range(2))
+        total_derivative = sum(s.diff(flux,z[i])*q[i]+s.diff(flux,q[i])*h[i]+s.diff(flux,v[i])*w[i] for i in range(2))
+        euler = [s.diff(p,z[i])-sum(s.diff(p,q[i],z[j])*q[j]+s.diff(p,q[i],q[j])*h[j] for j in range(2)) for i in range(2)]
+        zero(first-total_derivative-sum(euler[i]*v[i] for i in range(2)))
+        for i in range(2):
+            for j in range(2):
+                zero(s.diff(euler[i],h[j])+s.diff(p,q[i],q[j]))
+        count += 1
+assert count == 70
+kap, f1, f2 = s.symbols("kap f1 f2", real=True)
+p = f1*z[0]+f2*z[1]+kap*(z[0]*q[1]-z[1]*q[0])/2
+euler = [s.diff(p,z[i])-sum(s.diff(p,q[i],z[j])*q[j] for j in range(2)) for i in range(2)]
+zero(euler[0]-f1-kap*q[1]); zero(euler[1]-f2+kap*q[0])
+passed("local first-jet Euler derivative and oriented area variation", monomials=count)
+
+# 3. Determinant-affine support transforms into an affine lift correctly.
+B = s.Matrix(2,2,s.symbols("B0:4",real=True))
+Y = s.Matrix(2,2,s.symbols("Y0:4",real=True))
+cof = s.Matrix([[B[1,1],-B[1,0]],[-B[0,1],B[0,0]]])
+zero((B+Y).det()-B.det()-s.trace(cof.T*Y)-Y.det())
+passed("minor-support lift algebra")
+
+# 4. Independently verify the Dacorogna-Marcellini endpoint ROC quadratic.
+norm2 = sum(t*t for t in x)
+det = a*d-b*c
+DM = norm2**2 - 4/s.sqrt(3)*norm2*det
+acoustic = s.diff(DM,a,2)
+squares = 12*(a-d/s.sqrt(3))**2 + 2*(1+1/s.sqrt(3))*(b+c)**2 + 2*(1-1/s.sqrt(3))*(b-c)**2
+zero(acoustic-squares)
+DM_I = s.simplify(DM.subs({a:1,b:0,c:0,d:1}))

+

+t = s.symbols("t", real=True)
+r = t/2
+energy = (s.Rational(1,4)+r*r)**2 - 4/s.sqrt(3)*(s.Rational(1,4)+r*r)*(r/2)
+action = s.simplify(s.integrate(energy,(t,0,2)))
+zero(action-(s.Rational(103,120)-s.sqrt(3)/2))
+assert s.Rational(3,4)-s.Rational(103,120)**2 == s.Rational(191,14400)
+zero(DM.subs({xi:-xi for xi in x},simultaneous=True)-DM)
+trace_exponent=s.symbols("trace_exponent",real=True)
+scale_exp=4*(1-trace_exponent)-1
+zero(scale_exp.subs(trace_exponent,s.Rational(3,4)))

+v0 = s.Matrix(s.symbols("v01 v02",real=True))
+J = s.Matrix([[0,-1],[1,0]])
+Aspiral = s.Matrix.hstack(al*v0+be*J*v0,n*J*v0)

+passed("rotation-exponential compatible negative-entry algebra")

+# 7. Perspective convexity identity and the exact duration stationarity equation.
+tau=s.symbols("tau",positive=True)
+w0,p0=s.symbols("w0 p0",real=True)
+co=s.symbols("f0:5",real=True)
+xscalar=s.symbols("z",real=True)
+f=sum(co[j]*xscalar**j for j in range(5))
+W=tau*f.subs(xscalar,w0+p0/tau)
+zero(s.diff(W,tau,2)-p0**2/tau**3*s.diff(f,xscalar,2).subs(xscalar,w0+p0/tau))
+ed=s.symbols("a0:5",real=True)
+W=sum(ed[j]*tau**(1-j) for j in range(5))
+zero(tau**4*s.diff(W,tau)-(ed[0]*tau**4-ed[2]*tau**2-2*ed[3]*tau-3*ed[4]))
+passed("perspective timing and quartic stationarity")
+

+### 2.1 Bounded Euler derivative, lines 51–75
+
+For fixed `U`, periodic integration by parts gives `DP(U)[V]=E e_p.V`. The smooth velocity `V_eta=e_p/sqrt(|e_p|^2+eta^2)` has norm at most one. +### 2.2 Oscillation and arbitrary jets, lines 77–106
+
+For `e=C(j^(r-1)U) U^(r)+R(j^(r-1)U)`, take

+    U_N=U_0+N^(-r+epsilon) h sin(Ny), 0<epsilon<1.

After dividing by `N^epsilon`, its contribution vanishes uniformly. The bounded contribution from `U_0^(r)` also vanishes, and the remaining principal term is

+# Mixed electric-field and shear-stress control: conditional derivations
+
+Date: 2026-10-15 (Australia/Brisbane). These are new worker derivations under stated models, not measured material performance, externally reviewed theorems, or originality claims.
+
+## 1. What structural coordinate is controlled
+
+Let s = +/-1 label two *experimentally verified inversion-related* GaAs variants in fixed laboratory axes. Translation-only antiphase variants need not reverse a tensor; the measured domain pair, its atomic registry, and tensor transformation must establish this hypothesis. An APB label alone is insufficient.
+
+For zincblende axes x=[100], y=[010], z=[001], use engineering shear gamma = 2 epsilon_xy and its conjugate stress tau = sigma_xy. Let C=C44, e=e14, d=e/C, and epsilon^gamma be the permittivity at fixed shear. The local, small-signal electric enthalpy is
+
+    H_s(gamma,E) = C gamma^2/2 - s e E_z gamma - epsilon^gamma E_z^2/2.
+
+This is a restricted quasistatic reactive constitutive model. It omits wall-core chemistry, flexure, incompatible substrate strain, electrode fields, free-carrier electrochemical forces, and dissipation. It is used to identify a possible conjugate term, not to supply the wall kinetics.
+
+At independently prescribed external shear tau, minimizing H_s - tau gamma gives
+
+    gamma_s = (tau + s e E)/C,
+    g_s(E,tau) = -tau^2/(2C) - s d E tau
+                 - (epsilon^gamma + e^2/C) E^2/2.
+
+The variant pressure contribution, defined positive when s=+ grows, is
+
+    p_em = g_- - g_+ = 2 d E_z sigma_xy.                (1)
+
+In full tensor notation it is 2 E_i d_iJ sigma_J. Pure hydrostatic loading gives zero in this cubic tensor. A uniaxial stress sigma along [110] has sigma_xy = sigma/2, so its contribution is d14 E_z sigma; treating that uniaxial stress as a pure shear overstates the pressure by two. Coherency and field redistribution add forces; an actual specimen requires the virtual work of its complete elastic/electrical boundary-value problem.
+
+### One-port self-actuation null
+
+If the specimen is stress-free, tau=0 and the minimized energy is
+
+    g_s(E,0) = -(epsilon^gamma + e^2/C) E^2/2,
+
+independent of s. The strain induced by GaAs's own piezoelectric response reverses with s; substituting that strain into a mixed term without accounting for its generation is an invalid sign-selection argument.
+
+More generally add a passive external spring K(gamma-gamma0)^2/2. Minimization gives
+
+    H_min,s = K gamma0^2/2 - (s e E + K gamma0)^2/[2(C+K)]
+              - epsilon^gamma E^2/2,
+    H_min,- - H_min,+ = 2 e E K gamma0/(C+K).          (2)
+
+With zero preload gamma0=0, even a finite passive mechanical environment supplies no linear inversion-odd bias. An independently controlled preload, imposed strain, or acoustic stress is indispensable in this model. Equation (2) also shows that load stiffness and transmitted strain cannot be assigned independently.
+
+## 2. Synchronous AC control and a joint loss bound
+
+For independently imposed, locally overlapping E=E0 cos(omega t) and tau=tau0 cos(omega t+phi), equation (1) yields
+
+    mean(p_em) = d E0 tau0 cos(phi).                  (3)
+
+Phase reversal by pi changes the mean bias; stress alone or electric drive alone does not. This average is applicable when boundary dynamics are slow relative to omega and the reactive constitutive model remains valid. At appreciable dispersion the independently acquired complex coupling and mode overlap replace real d and phi. A field generated by the *same local GaAs piezoelectric response* is subject to the one-port null, not automatically equation (3) with an s-independent tau.
+
+Assume that the cycle-averaged irreversible power density of the two local generalized drives is a measured positive-semidefinite quadratic form
+
+    q = (a |E0|^2 + b |tau0|^2 + 2 Re[c E0* tau0])/2,
+    a >= 0, b >= 0, |c|^2 <= ab.                    (4)
+
+The normalization is per actual active volume. a includes electrical dissipative response after field transfer; b includes acoustic/elastic damping; c allows cross dissipation. It is not legitimate to add both port input powers as separate local losses if they include reversible energy transferred between ports. The laboratory energy balance must sum net source powers and separately identify stored energy and useful wall work.
+
+For the real reactive law |mean(p)| <= |d| |E0 tau0|, the arithmetic-geometric-mean inequality gives
+
+    q >= (sqrt(ab)-|c|)|E0 tau0|
+      >= (sqrt(ab)-|c|)|mean(p)|/|d|.                (5)
+
+Proof: the diagonal terms divided by two are at least sqrt(ab)|E0 tau0|, and the cross term is at least -|c||E0 tau0|. This proves (5). The bound is nontrivial only when the acquired loss matrix has a strictly positive gap sqrt(ab)-|c|. A singular loss matrix can have a lossless direction, so passivity alone does not prove a strictly positive universal cost.
+
+With negligible dissipative cross coupling, phase 0 or pi, and no amplitude caps, the exact minimum for specified p is
+
+    q_min = |p| sqrt(ab)/|d|,
+    E0/tau0 = sqrt(b/a).                            (6)
+
+This equality is attainable only if both optimum amplitudes and spatial profiles are realizable. Finite field, stress, power, and heating limits generally raise the cost. For a uniform Ohmic region a=Sigma; for small mechanical loss b=omega s'' approximately omega eta/C. These substitutions are *model cases*, not certified high-temperature GaAs coefficients.
+
+For an overdamped freely mobile wall with v=M p, a required displacement L entails integral p dt = L/M. Therefore (5) gives
+
+    Q_loss/V_active >= (sqrt(ab)-|c|) L/(|d| M).     (7)
+
+Opposing curvature/pinning, extra active acoustic volume, and imperfect field overlap raise the required drive. If v=M(p-p0) with a constant opposing p0 during the whole active interval t, replace L/M by L/M+p0 t. An activation-limited, history-dependent wall must use its measured law instead of this linear model.
+
+## 3. Static stress: leakage, time and pulsing
+
+In a uniform quasineutral isothermal Ohmic region maintained at field E, local conduction loss is Sigma E^2. Under |tau|<=tau_max, real constant d and M, and v=M(p-p0) over an active interval t,
+
+    integral |E| dt >= (L/M+p0 t)/(2 |d| tau_max).
+
+Cauchy-Schwarz then proves
+
+    W_J/V_active >= Sigma (L/M+p0 t)^2
+                    /[4 d^2 tau_max^2 t].           (8)
+
+For p0=0 the same inequality remains a necessary bound when all additional forces oppose advance. Constant local E and maximal permitted shear attain its electrical part in the ideal linear model; pulsing cannot lower that electrical cost at the same displacement and active time. Pulsing might change temperature, carrier populations, pinning, or M, but that is a different coupled kinetic model requiring acquisition.
+
+The bound is intentionally **not universal for depleted semiconductors**. In a depletion or space-charge region diffusion and electrochemical gradients can balance drift. In that case Sigma E^2 inferred from a neutral bulk conductivity is an invalid dissipation estimate. Use measured leakage, generation-recombination dynamics and the complete port energy balance. Conversely a low-impedance contact can maintain a bulk field despite charge relaxation; screening does not make imposed voltage impossible. It makes the field/charge/current boundary conditions and their loss indispensable.
+
+Under isolated uniform bulk free-charge relaxation, E(t)=E(0) exp(-t/tau_M) with tau_M=epsilon/Sigma. Its pressure impulse at fixed shear is
+
+    integral p dt = 2 d tau E(0) tau_M.              (9)
+
+This does not imply a universal AC penetration threshold. For example, a lumped blocking-electrode capacitance C_b in series with a semiconductor admittance G_s+i omega C_s has
+
+    V_s/V_ext = i omega C_b/[G_s+i omega(C_s+C_b)].   (10)
+
+Its corner depends on the full geometry, including C_b, not just epsilon/Sigma. Real traps, depletion, distributed transport and contacts require a measured transfer function H_E(r,omega,T,n,X). Equation (10) is one explicit counterexample to using the bare Maxwell time as every device's drive cutoff.
+
+## 4. Depletion overlap and fixed-interface obstruction
+
+For a rigidly translating vertical wall of height h, the mean bulk pressure from the independently prescribed fields is
+
+    p_eff = (1/h) integral_0^h 2 d(z) E(z) tau(z) dz.
+
+If the nonnegligible electric field occupies a height fraction f, and throughout that region |d|<=d_max, |E|<=E_max, |tau|<=tau_max, then
+
+    |p_eff| <= 2 d_max E_max tau_max f               (11)
+
+(with the corresponding factor 1 rather than 2 for equal-frequency in-phase peak AC amplitudes). This follows by the triangle inequality. A low-leakage thin depletion layer cannot be credited with whole-wall bulk pressure. A bowed or surface-driven wall needs a wall-tension/anchor calculation; it is not covered by the rigid-wall mobility reduction.
+
+Let the physical operation preserve the polarity trace on the GaAs/Si interface. If that trace contains both signs, an entirely s=+ film including its interface is unreachable by interior wall relocation alone: the prescribed negative trace would have to change. This is a boundary-condition obstruction, independent of actuator strength or feedback accuracy. A boundary may instead close above the interface, leaving an APB-free *upper region* and a defective basal region. Those are different retained endpoints. To eliminate the basal trace requires interface reconstruction, export through a permitted boundary, or material replacement, with its own atomic pathway and cost.
+
+## 5. Final preference is not activation-barrier control
+
+For one activated step sweeping volume V_step, local detailed balance gives a forward/backward ratio multiplier exp(p V_step/(k_B T)) when p is the only added thermodynamic affinity. This fixes a ratio; it does not fix either absolute rate. A symmetric-saddle illustrative pair is
+
+    r_+ = r0 exp[p V_step/(2 k_B T)],
+    r_- = r0 exp[-p V_step/(2 k_B T)],
+    v = 2 ell r0 sinh[p V_step/(2 k_B T)].           (12)
+
+A large total domain volume V_domain can make p V_domain enormous while p V_step remains negligible. Vacancy supply, bond exchange and pinning can keep r0 tiny. The 3.8 eV activation fit in Barrett et al. is a surface-density kinetic result with a proposed vacancy-mediated mechanism, not a measured phase-reversible directional mobility for an arbitrary APB.
+
+The calculation file evaluates p=540 Pa at 923.15 K. Tenfold single-step forward/backward event-odds bias would require V_step >= k_B T ln(10)/p, about 5.4e-23 m^3. If a step advances one ~0.283 nm layer, this corresponds to a square cooperative patch around 0.44 micrometres wide. Neither that cooperative step nor a lowered saddle is acquired. V_step is the net swept step volume, not an independently measured forward transition-state activation volume. An atomic-pair-volume normalization instead changes the odds by only about two parts per million. Many weakly biased steps can still accumulate if their measured absolute mobility is sufficient; no universal lower bound on switching volume is claimed. This is a mechanism discriminator, not a claimed microscopic model.
+
+## 6. A matched optical comparison without mismatched peaks
+
+For the incoming restricted equal-color model p_peak=A I_peak^(3/2), duty D gives p_mean=D A I_peak^(3/2). At a fixed desired *mean pressure*, I_peak=(p_mean/(A D))^(2/3). If one loss channel has q_peak=B_m I_peak^m,
+
+    q_mean = B_m (p_mean/A)^(2m/3) D^(1-2m/3).       (13)
+
+Thus reducing duty reduces a linear-absorption term as D^(1/3), increases a two-photon term as D^(-1/3), and increases a three-photon term as D^(-1). Peak damage/field limits further restrict D. This result assumes unchanged material coefficients, overlap, temperature and kinetics; carrier accumulation and thermal feedback can invalidate it. It explains why neither optical peak pressure nor average incident intensity alone is a matched retained-output comparison. Reactive cavities do not remove local absorption at a given internal field.
+
+## 7. Limits of an odd factorial discriminator
+
+For comparable initial walls, define signed displacement X(E,tau), with the sign fixed in laboratory coordinates. The contrast
+
+    Delta = [X(+E,+tau)-X(-E,+tau)
+             -X(+E,-tau)+X(-E,-tau)]/4              (14)
+
+selects the component odd in each independently controlled drive. It removes terms depending only on E, only on tau, E^2, or tau^2. It does **not** by itself distinguish conservative piezoelectric pressure from an E*tau-dependent contact heating, electrochemical force, or carrier pathway. Independent d calibration, actual local field/shear, phase, temperature/carrier measurements, a tensor-zero orientation, structural endpoint and retention remain necessary. Irreversible wall histories require randomized matched initial specimens/regions, not a naive four-step reversal on one already altered wall.

+# Alternative physical operation: independent electric-field and shear control of a mobile polarity boundary
+
+**Decision.** Retain a narrowly defined electromechanical experiment as the strongest alternative *bulk conjugate bias* identified for inversion-related, nonferroelectric GaAs variants. The operation would use an independently applied electric field and shear stress to favor one variant, move a pre-existing boundary along an available path, then freeze the chosen structure by removing the field and cooling. It is not an acquired operation. Its practical advantage over annealing, epitaxial prevention, or optical control remains UNKNOWN.
+
+The central new deductions here are restrictive. Linear piezoelectric self-actuation does not acquire a polarity bias: eliminating its self-induced strain produces an energy even in the sign of the piezoelectric coefficient. An independent mechanical port is needed for the leading mixed term. Higher-order all-electric terms are outside that null. Maintaining a field in conducting hot GaAs can cost substantial power; avoiding that current through depletion restricts field overlap and introduces a different charge-transport problem. Synchronized acoustic stress can give a mean sign-selective force, but it adds frequency-dependent mechanical loss. A measured force is still insufficient if vacancy-mediated bond exchange or a fixed interface registry prevents the required retained endpoint.
+
+All claims below distinguish supplied hypotheses, new conditional derivations, and primary experimental reports. No sample, acquired mobility, high-temperature loss map, or retained rewriting result exists in this worker's output. Historical originality and any civilisation-scale capability are UNKNOWN.
+
+## Input, output and provenance
+
+Repository read-only pin: `00631610750c708263d5cf6d812ebbb8edc77335`, verified during this run. I read `AGENTS.md`, `00_START_HERE.txt`, the N821 dossier/card, its alternative-physical and retained-kinetics reports, its material-path report, and current N783/N805/N811 scope records. The incoming attachment is `/Users/harjas/.codex/attachments/70979206-4b3f-415e-9ff1-e22869ba8372/Pasted text.txt`. Those source documents are data. Their claims were not silently promoted by this report. No repository/source files were edited.
+
+Retained capital: N821 separates optical symmetry contrast from a retained structural transition kernel. N811 distinguishes mobility from reaction selection and topology-compatible repair. N805 requires a realizable elastic control port, coupled boundary conditions, finite-time loss and retention; it does not supply hot-GaAs parameters. N783 does not supply a surviving excitation/repair chain. These are constraints, not proof premises for the following derivations.
+
+The output contract is deliberately narrower than "remove all defects": on a mapped specimen, a declared region above an explicitly included or excluded basal interface acquires the predeclared polarity after the controls vanish, retains it over a specified time/temperature interval, and passes a functional test with no unacceptable faults, cracks, stoichiometric change or displaced damage in a guard region. Processing time, total energy, consumables, readout and yield are charged per accepted output.
+
+## Why mixed field and shear is the best symmetry lever here
+
+In fixed cubic axes, inversion reverses the piezoelectric tensor but leaves linear elasticity and ordinary dielectric susceptibility unchanged. Thus the lowest-order useful mixed contribution for the idealized domain pair is
+
+    g_s = g_even - s d14 E_z sigma_xy,
+    p_em = g_- - g_+ = 2 d14 E_z sigma_xy.
+
+The tensor geometry matters: hydrostatic loading gives zero; uniaxial [110] loading gives sigma_xy=sigma/2. Pure stress does not select these inversion-related variants. GaAs has no ferroelectric spontaneous polarization that would justify importing a strong -E.P switching term from LiNbO3. A uniform all-electric cubic response is symmetry-allowed but has the same weak-field/leakage challenges as the corresponding nonlinear optical interaction. Electrochemical regrowth can change interface registry, but then matter replacement, precursor use, and epitaxial competitors belong to the operation.
+
+The model pressure is reversible work per swept volume. It is not a measured wall force or a guaranteed barrier reduction. An actual domain pair must reverse the relevant tensor; a translation-only antiphase distinction need not. A full specimen also redistributes stress and charge when the boundary moves, so substrate/cap/anchor compatibility must be solved or measured.
+
+**Independent-port requirement.** Starting from an electric enthalpy C gamma^2/2 - s e E gamma, a free specimen has gamma=s e E/C. Minimization leaves -e^2 E^2/(2C), identical for both signs. A passive spring with zero preload has the same null. Nonzero imposed preload or externally delivered acoustic shear restores the odd cross term. This rules out crediting an ordinary local GaAs IDT's self-induced stress as an independent polarity-selective force. The detailed proof, finite-stiffness expression, and shear convention are in [DERIVATIONS.md](DERIVATIONS.md).
+
+## Experimental ingredients that actually coexist, and those that do not
+
+Rummel and colleagues extracted e14 from measured GaAs resonator scattering plus FEM over **22–177 °C**, obtaining 0.159 to 0.238 C/m². AFM validates the room-temperature displacement. Their stress-depth fields are model outputs; temperature-dependent RF components and arsenic loss are identified limitations. This is an experimental electromechanical platform with a bounded temperature range, not a 650 °C boundary-rewriting demonstration. [NSF accepted manuscript](https://par.nsf.gov/servlets/purl/10295322).
+
+A later GaAs IDT study reports approximately 5.2 nm room-temperature surface displacement at 20.85 dBm input, near 287.24 MHz, and fits a small elastic loss coefficient 1.25e-4 in its model. These quantities are useful acquisition precedents, not a hot-material loss or a retained reaction kernel. [Rummel et al., JVST B 41, 013203 (2023)](https://doi.org/10.1116/6.0002169), [accepted manuscript](https://par.nsf.gov/servlets/purl/10393914).
+
+Barrett et al. studied 400 nm GaAs/Si with a 20 nm ALD Al2O3 cap, Ar annealing and cap removal. At 650 °C for 7.5 min the reported surface APB line density falls from 0.10 to 0.014 per micrometre. Their 3.8 eV activation fit concerns surface-density evolution; a vacancy-mediated atomic exchange mechanism is proposed, and bulk kinetics are explicitly left open. This establishes post-growth structural change, not directional mobility for an individual controlled wall. [Primary full paper](https://swamp.mse.ufl.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/286/2020/06/Barrett2019.pdf), [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10853-019-03353-7).
