The accessible transport paper abstract does not supply the needed 923 K numbers for the proposed specimen. [Nichols, Yee and Wolfe, Solid-State Electronics 23, 109–116 (1980)](https://doi.org/10.1016/0038-1101(80)90144-6). The primary interferometric piezoelectric paper also explains why low-impedance converse driving avoids screening of a direct piezoelectric signal. That is not an exemption from source current and heat. [Muensit and Guy, Ferroelectrics 271, 397–401 (2002)](https://doi.org/10.1080/713716205).
+
+## The coupled force, loss and kinetics gate
+
+The incoming normalization |d|=2.7 pm/V, pure shear 100 MPa and local E=1 MV/m gives **540 Pa DC**. Equal-frequency, in-phase AC drives at those *peak* amplitudes give **270 Pa mean**. These are arithmetic screens, not same-regime GaAs performance. Uniaxial 100 MPa along [110] gives half the pure-shear DC value.
+
+For a maintained uniform Ohmic field in a 400 nm film, the DC local conduction power is
+
+    P_J/A = Sigma E^2 h = 40 Sigma W/cm²,
+    W_J/A over 600 s = 24000 Sigma J/cm²,
+
+where Sigma is in S/m. Hypothetical Sigma=1e-5 gives 0.24 J/cm²; Sigma=1 gives 24000 J/cm². Neither is claimed to describe hot GaAs. The point is that field-storage energy, only about 2.3 nJ/cm² at this normalization, does not represent the process's electrical input. The stored shear energy is also small compared with sustained loss; the specimen, cap, substrate and stress fixture need their own ledger.
+
+Screening has two distinct escapes, both charged:
+
+1. Low-impedance contacts can sustain an internal field while conduction dissipates power. Maxwell charge relaxation is not a universal prohibition on applied voltage.
+2. Blocking/depletion geometry can retain field with far lower current, but a neutral-bulk Sigma E² estimate is invalid there. Acquire generation/recombination, traps, electrode electrochemistry, leakage, internal field and depleted volume. If only a fraction f of a rigid wall is exposed to bounded field and shear, its mean pressure is at most 2|d| Emax taumax f. No whole-wall bias follows from a thin surface field.
+
+For AC control, let the measured joint local irreversible response be q=(a|E|²+b|tau|²+2 Re[c E* tau])/2. Passivity gives |c|²<=ab. The derived bound is
+
+    q >= (sqrt(ab)-|c|) |mean(p)|/|d|.
+
+With negligible dissipative cross term, the exact ideal optimum is q_min=|p| sqrt(ab)/|d|, at E/tau=sqrt(b/a). If a=Sigma and b=omega eta/C, it explicitly couples electrical and acoustic losses. At a declared 287.24 MHz, eta=1.25e-4, C=60 GPa and 100 MPa shear, the local mechanical-loss normalization alone is about 0.75 W/cm² for a 400 nm active layer, or 451 J/cm² over 600 s. These room-temperature parameters do not predict the hot process, and an acoustic field extending into substrate increases the active loss volume. A claimed resonator advantage must include measured external RF power, mismatch, electrodes and thermal drift.
+
+A loss bound is still not a switching result. For a freely mobile linear wall, v=Mp, moving L requires integral p dt=L/M. Combining this with the loss inequality gives a necessary acquisition test before spending on the actuator. Opposing curvature and pinning increase the requirement. No directional M or depinning pressure has been acquired here.
+
+Pressure is especially weak as a microscopic barrier rescue. At 650 °C, 540 Pa biases an atomic-pair-volume step by roughly two parts per million in event odds. Tenfold *single-step forward/backward odds* would require a swept step volume around 5.4e-23 m³, corresponding to a ~0.44 micrometre square patch if a step advances half a lattice constant. A whole 1 micrometre³ domain has a large total energy preference, but that does not establish a cooperative saddle. The calculated patch tests that particular single-step odds mechanism; many weakly biased steps might still accumulate if their measured mobility is sufficient. It is not a universal activation-volume lower bound for retained selection.
+
+Cold DFT boundary-energy scales also put a 1 micrometre curved boundary's capillary pressure in the hundreds of kilopascals, much greater than this normalization. That is a scale warning, not a hot-GaAs quantitative exclusion. An almost planar, weakly pinned wall is the sensible assay; adding 540 Pa to already capillary-driven coarsening need not improve its speed. [Rubel and Baranovskii, IJMS 10, 5104–5114 (2009)](https://doi.org/10.3390/ijms10125104).
+
+## What measurement and feedback can actually overcome
+
+The needed acquired state is an individual boundary's polarity pair, plane, anchors, curvature, mobile path, pinning response, carrier/charge state and thermal history. Track signed displacement under independently calibrated positive and negative conjugate biases. Establish whether the same mobile wall reaches an admissible exit or whether it bows while a basal segment remains pinned. SHG phase can locate polarity but must be tied to independent atomic/diffraction endpoint checks; carrier-modified optical contrast alone is insufficient.
+
+Feedback can then choose the sign, spatial overlap and stopping time for a *measured existing pathway*. It can quench after the wall reaches a selected region. It cannot create a missing bond-exchange edge, infer directional mobility from a surface-density fit, or erase a fixed mixed-polarity interface trace. Local vacancy injection, growth-assisted front motion or interface reconstruction could change those edges, but also change defects, stoichiometry, leakage and the comparator. They require a separate acquired operation.
+
+The interface boundary condition is an exact practical distinction. If both signs are fixed at the GaAs/Si interface, interior wall motion cannot yield a single-polarity film including that interface. It may yield a useful APB-free upper layer. Alcotte et al.'s strong published growth comparator illustrates precisely this endpoint: their 150 nm film has an APB-free top region, while cross-section imaging retains a defective basal region and APB planes cease above about 70 nm. Their workflow includes substrate preparation/annealing and two-step MOCVD, and they report improved optical/electrical properties. It must not be compared against a stricter, entire-stack defect-free target without saying so. [Primary AIP article](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.4945586).
+
+## Complete end-to-end comparison
+
+For every route, use the same accepted retained/functional output, tolerance, region, guard volume and retention horizon. Report energy, time, consumables and yield separately, then optionally energy per accepted transformed volume:
+
+    E_good/V_good = (E_prepare + E_heat + E_control + E_cool
+                     + E_feedback + E_verify + E_rejects)/(Y V_good).
+
+Preparation and measurement are not free supplied inputs. Costs inherited from a common starting specimen can cancel in a comparison only when actually common. New growth and post-growth repair need different starting-material ledgers.
+
+| Route | Strongest qualified output | Additional costs needed for a fair comparison | Present decision |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| Optimized dark capped anneal | Published APB-density reduction in GaAs/Si | Cap ALD/removal, furnace/RTA, Ar, heating/cooling, residual defects, depth/functional assay, yield | Leading same-material repair baseline; no prescribed opposite polarity selection established |
+| Epitaxial prevention/template growth | Published APB-free useful top layers; designed polarity patterns are also established | Substrate preparation, high-temperature growth, precursors, vacuum/gas, pattern/template steps, interface residuals, verification and yield | Leading manufacturing baseline when a new layer is acceptable |
+| Incoming omega/2omega optical bias | Conditional reactive pressure; retained phase-selected GaAs wall operation unacquired | Both source wall powers, phase/tensor/overlap control, hot nonlinear absorption/carriers, thermal processing, readout and damage/yield | Requires full retained response; peak pressure is not a throughput comparison |
+| Independent static E × shear | Conditional symmetry-conjugate pressure | Contacts/depletion, leakage and charge management, stress fixture/loading, temperature-compatible cap, same-path M and retention | Best low-frequency alternative if internal field and mobile wall coexist cheaply |
+| Independent synchronous acoustic stress × E | Conditional phase-reversible mean pressure | Two independent ports, RF conversion/mismatch/damping, internal phase/overlap, hot resonance drift, larger acoustic active volume, field loss | Possible screening-management route; no loss or kinetic advantage established |
+
+For optical control, comparing at equal *mean pressure* rather than equal peaks gives a further conditional discriminator. If p_peak=A I^(3/2) and q_peak proportional to I^m, then at duty D and fixed mean pressure, mean loss scales as D^(1-2m/3). Low duty improves a linear-absorption term, worsens two-photon loss, and worsens three-photon loss more severely. Both-color thermal/carrier feedback and damage limits still have to be acquired. This prevents assigning favorable optical duty and independently favorable absorption.
+
+Static E × shear wins only if it produces a desired endpoint unavailable to the optimized dark control, or saves more baseline time/energy/yield than its complete added control cost. A cavity, acoustic resonance, low field-storage energy, or higher cold d alone does not establish that inequality. No numerical ranking of total cost is supportable from the present literature packet.
+
+## Smallest decisive obtainable experiment
+
+1. **Acquire the bridge before a large apparatus.** On the actual capped APB specimen and temperature history, map an initially nearly planar boundary with a reachable exit. Measure local complex electrical field transfer/leakage, shear transmission, reactive piezoelectric coupling, absorbed/dissipated power, temperature/carrier response, and individual wall displacement/pinning. Select compatible contacts and stress geometry by those data. If no safe pressure/kinetics window supports the declared displacement, reject this GaAs implementation.
+2. **Use two independent controls.** Apply externally imposed shear/preload and an independently calibrated electric field. AC is admitted only with measured internal phase and full joint loss. A local self-actuated GaAs resonator is a null comparator, not the required independent stress source.
+3. **Randomize matched starting walls.** Use the four sign combinations (+E,+tau), (-E,+tau), (+E,-tau), (-E,-tau), with stress-only, field-only, optimized dark, tensor-zero and, if AC, quadrature controls. The contrast odd in both controls isolates the predicted symmetry class. Match measured heat/carrier histories; contact thermoelectric or mixed carrier forces can survive the same contrast, so it is not alone proof of reactive pressure.
+4. **Demand endpoint and function.** After drive removal and cooling, independently measure the declared polarity region, residual wall/fault network, basal/interface remnants, stoichiometry, cracks, plastic slip and guard-region damage. Require retention and a predeclared electrical/optical function. Count all preparation, source, heat, cooling, feedback, structural readout, discarded samples and accepted yield against dark anneal and the applicable growth baseline.
+
+The positive elementary result would be independently driven, sign-reversible boundary steering to a retained useful endpoint in a nonferroelectric semiconductor. Failure to observe the odd structural displacement despite an independently calibrated pressure opportunity would constrain the actual wall kernel; failure of the force/heat/kinetics bridge already rejects the proposed implementation. Neither outcome establishes arbitrary repair, atom assembly, net energy generation, or a Kardashev-level manufacturing capability.

+"""Reproduce conditional actuator/kinetic scales. No material performance inferred."""
+from pathlib import Path
+import csv
+import json
+import math
+
+BASE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+k_B = 1.380649e-23
+q_e = 1.602176634e-19
+eps0 = 8.8541878128e-12
+d = 2.7e-12  # incoming room-temperature normalization, NOT hot measurement
+shear = 1e8  # pure shear, NOT uniaxial stress
+E = 1e6
+h = 400e-9  # Barrett specimen film thickness; calculations are hypothetical controls
+t = 600.0
+C = 60e9  # declared normalization, NOT measured same-regime C44
+epsilon = 13*eps0
+T = 650+273.15
+p_dc = 2*d*E*shear
+p_ac = d*E*shear
+frequency = 287.24e6  # room-temperature Rummel2023 platform
+eta = 1.25e-4  # room-temperature fitted elastic loss normalization
+b_ac = 2*math.pi*frequency*eta/C
+
+table = []
+for Sigma in [1e-8, 1e-5, 1e-2, 1, 100]:
+    table.append({
+        'conductivity_S_per_m_hypothetical': Sigma,
+        'isolated_bulk_Maxwell_time_s': epsilon/Sigma,
+        'DC_Joule_W_per_cm2': Sigma*E**2*h/1e4,
+        'DC_Joule_J_per_cm2_600s': Sigma*E**2*h*t/1e4,
+        'AC_Joule_W_per_cm2': Sigma*E**2*h/2e4,
+        'AC_joint_loss_lower_bound_W_per_cm2_for_270Pa':
+            p_ac*math.sqrt(Sigma*b_ac)/abs(d)*h/1e4,
+    })
+
+a0 = 0.5653e-9  # declared lattice-constant normalization
+V_pair = a0**3/4
+V_ten = k_B*T*math.log(10)/p_dc
+step = a0/2
+gamma = 28e-3*q_e/(1e-10)**2  # cold DFT normalization from Rubel family
+
+results = {
+    'status': 'CONDITIONAL_MODEL_ARITHMETIC_ONLY',
+    'base_revision': '00631610750c708263d5cf6d812ebbb8edc77335',
+    'normalizations': {'d_m_per_V':d, 'pure_shear_Pa':shear,
+        'local_E_V_per_m':E, 'film_h_m':h, 'active_time_s':t,
+        'elastic_C_Pa':C, 'relative_permittivity':13, 'temperature_K':T,
+        'AC_frequency_Hz_ROOM_T':frequency,'AC_elastic_eta_ROOM_T':eta},
+    'p_DC_Pa':p_dc,
+    'p_AC_in_phase_Pa':p_ac,
+    'p_DC_for_100MPa_uniaxial_110_Pa':p_dc/2,
+    'electric_stored_J_per_cm2':epsilon*E**2*h/2e4,
+    'elastic_shear_stored_J_per_cm2':shear**2*h/(2*C*1e4),
+    'AC_local_mechanical_loss_W_per_cm2_normalization':b_ac*shear**2*h/2e4,
+    'AC_local_mechanical_loss_J_per_cm2_600s_normalization':b_ac*shear**2*h*t/2e4,
+    'Ohmic_conductivity_ceiling_for_1W_per_cm2_DC_S_per_m':1e4/(E**2*h),
+    'atomic_pair_volume_m3_normalization':V_pair,
+    'atomic_pair_event_odds_multiplier_at_540Pa':math.exp(p_dc*V_pair/(k_B*T)),
+    'tenfold_event_odds_swept_step_volume_m3':V_ten,
+    'tenfold_event_odds_patch_width_m_for_half_lattice_step':math.sqrt(V_ten/step),
+    '1um3_domain_energy_split_eV_at_540Pa':p_dc*1e-18/q_e,
+    'cold_DFT_gamma_J_per_m2_normalization':gamma,
+    'cylindrical_curvature_pressure_Pa_for_R_1um_normalization':gamma/1e-6,
+    'curve_pressure_over_DC_p_normalization':gamma/(1e-6*p_dc),
+    'conditional_3p8eV_Arrhenius_rate_ratio_177C_to_650C':
+        math.exp(-3.8*q_e/k_B*(1/(177+273.15)-1/T)),
+    'overlap_ceiling_DC_Pa':{str(f):p_dc*f for f in [1,0.1,0.01]},
+    'conductivity_table':table,
+    'warning':'No conductivity, hot d, hot C/loss, directional wall mobility, pinning, damage threshold, or retained yield acquired. Cold normalizations are not combined into a claimed hot implementation.'
+}
+
+# Algebraic/model checks that can catch a sign/factor or bound error.
+assert math.isclose(p_dc, 540)
+assert math.isclose(p_ac, 270)
+for a,b in [(1.0,2.0),(1e-8,b_ac),(100,b_ac)]:
+    P = p_ac/abs(d)
+    Ef = math.sqrt(P*math.sqrt(b/a))
+    sf = math.sqrt(P*math.sqrt(a/b))
+    q = (a*Ef**2+b*sf**2)/2
+    assert math.isclose(Ef*sf,P,rel_tol=1e-12)
+    assert math.isclose(q,P*math.sqrt(a*b),rel_tol=1e-12)
+
+(BASE/'calculations.json').write_text(json.dumps(results,indent=2)+'\n')
+with (BASE/'conductivity_thresholds.csv').open('w', newline='') as f:
+    w=csv.DictWriter(f,fieldnames=table[0].keys())
+    w.writeheader(); w.writerows(table)
+print(json.dumps({k:v for k,v in results.items() if k not in
+    ['normalizations','conductivity_table','warning']},indent=2))

+# Scoped proofs for conditional exchange robustness
+
+Worker: exchange_robustness. Date: 2026-10-15. Repository pin:
+`00631610750c708263d5cf6d812ebbb8edc77335`.
+
+These are internal finite-dimensional derivations. No independent external
+mathematical or physical validation and no historical novelty claim is made.
+The wire-cutting identity in Section 5 is established prior art, reconstructed
+here to give an explicit comparator/resource tradeoff.
+
+## 1. Exact reconstruction of the incoming operation
+
+Write the native cq state as
+
+\[
+ \rho_{CRSE}=\sum_c p_c|c\rangle\langle c|\otimes\rho^c_{RSE},
+ \quad \sigma_c=\rho^c_{RS},\quad \tau_c=\rho^c_E.
+\]
+
+For independent joint copies i,j, a local permutation of their S registers
+gives tagged marginal \(\sigma_c\otimes\tau_c\) on donor reference R_j,
+recipient data S_i, recipient environment E_i. This is just the original
+cross marginal \(\rho_{R_jS_jE_i}\), with S_j moved to S_i. Independence
+factorizes that marginal. The donor, rather than recipient, C label follows
+the job and reference.
+
+For N iid copies, cyclically route each condition group of size at least two;
+leave singleton groups native. A tagged condition-c copy is unmatched iff
+the other N-1 records avoid c. Thus exactly
+
+\[
+ \rho_N=\sum_c p_c |c\rangle\langle c|\otimes
+ [ (1-p_c)^{N-1}\rho^c_{RSE}
+  +(1-(1-p_c)^{N-1})\sigma_c\otimes\tau_c].
+\]
+
+With trace distance normalized by 1/2, its distance from complete conditional
+grafting is at most \(s_N(C)=\sum_cp_c(1-p_c)^{N-1}\). Every [0,1] task score
+inherits this bound; a two-policy difference inherits twice the bound.
+None of these statements makes the whole output batch independent.
+
+The source's phase model with hidden bit X~Bernoulli(u), RS Bell phase X,
+and future controlled-Z has native echo success 1 and independent graft
+success \((1-u)^2+u^2\). Sharing X between copies leaves echo success 1.
+An extra bath X gate is invisible to reduced SWAP characterization but can
+change future success from 1 to 0 even on an initially product input.
+
+## 2. Matching on the task-relevant quotient of the record
+
+Let Z=f(C) be a declared deterministic coarsening; \(q_z=\Pr(Z=z)\) and
+\(\bar\tau_z=\sum_{c:f(c)=z}p(c|z)\tau_c\). Draw N iid joint preparations.
+Route S within Z groups by a fixed index-based derangement (e.g. a cycle),
+leaving singleton groups native. Selection may depend on Z and independent
+routing randomness, but not on the fine C values within a group or on any
+unrecorded variable. Attach the full donor C and original donor R to the
+transferred job. Sites and continuation operations are interchangeable.
+
+**Exact finite-batch theorem.** The tagged output is
+
+\[
+ \rho_N^Z=\sum_c p_c|c\rangle\langle c|\otimes
+ [a_{f(c)}\rho^c_{RSE}+(1-a_{f(c)})\sigma_c\otimes\bar\tau_{f(c)}],
+ \qquad a_z=(1-q_z)^{N-1}.                                      \tag{1}
+\]
+
+**Proof.** Condition on the tagged donor's fine record c and all coarse
+records. If its coarse group is a singleton, its joint state is unchanged.
+Otherwise its recipient is a distinct index selected without inspecting
+the fine records. The recipient's fine record has distribution p(c'|z),
+independent of the donor's joint state. The recipient environment marginal
+is therefore \(\bar\tau_z\). Averaging the singleton event proves (1).
+The argument works for any fixed cycle length, and does not require product
+states inside a replica. QED.
+
+If \(\tau_c=\bar\tau_{f(c)}\) for every c, the only difference from complete
+fine-C grafting is singleton mass \(s_N(Z)=\sum_zq_z(1-q_z)^{N-1}\). Both the
+fine CRS and fine CE marginals are then preserved. The condition does not
+require the donor RS states to agree within a coarse group.
+
+There is a weaker, task-only version. Let \(\Lambda_a^\tau\) denote the
+continuation channel S->S' with initial independent environment state tau.
+R is idle; its dimension and its entanglement with S are unrestricted. The
+policy a may include a full predeclared continuation sequence. A finite
+menu may contain the fine-record-dependent policies used in scoring.
+Suppose, for every scored policy and each relevant c,
+
+\[
+ \Lambda_a^{\tau_c}=\Lambda_a^{\bar\tau_{f(c)}}.                 \tag{2}
+\]
+
+Then every tagged reference-inclusive task score equals the full fine-C
+graft score, apart from singleton mass \(s_N(Z)\). Equation (2) follows from
+equality of normalized Choi states, so it can in principle be tested using
+system-only causal-break channel probes on a fixed finite policy menu;
+full bath-state tomography is unnecessary. Such testing still requires
+certified local replacement operations and enough support/precision in C.
+Infinitely many or unique fine records do not come with a free certificate.
+
+For approximate matching put
+\(\eta_{a,c}=\frac12\|\Lambda_a^{\tau_c}-
+\Lambda_a^{\bar\tau_{f(c)}}\|_\diamond\). Then, for a [0,1] effect on RS',
+
+\[
+ |F_a(\rho_N^Z)-F_a(\mathcal G_C(\rho))|
+ \le s_N(Z)+\sum_c p_c(1-a_{f(c)})\eta_{a,c}.                  \tag{3}
+\]
+
+**Proof.** Apply (1). On singleton branches use the [0,1] range. On matched
+branches the diamond definition applies to the arbitrary reference-bearing
+input \(\sigma_c\). Average the bounds. QED.
+
+For d-dimensional S and normalized Choi states J, the sufficient bound
+\(\eta_{a,c}\le(d/2)\|J_a^{\tau_c}-J_a^{\bar\tau_z}\|_1\) gives one finite
+acquisition interface; uncertainty of the Choi estimates must be included.
+Its tomography cost depends on d and output dimension and the policy menu,
+not on a declared bath Hilbert-space size. It is not generally cheap.
+
+Equation (2) preserves selected task response, not the full fine CE
+marginal. If two conditional baths differ only on a spectator that never
+couples during the selected future, they may be task-equivalent and remain
+different physical states. A null task response is not global memorylessness.
+
+**Explicit removal of the rare-record obstruction.** Let C=(Z,U), with Z
+fair and U an independently generated 128-bit nonce. Suppose E's conditional
+marginal depends only on Z. U may select arbitrary genuinely local unitaries
+on S, so the RS states need not coincide. For N=32,
+
+\[
+ s_N(C)=(1-2^{-129})^{31}\ge1-31\,2^{-129},\qquad
+ s_N(Z)=2^{-31}\simeq4.657\times10^{-10}.                       \tag{4}
+\]
+
+Fine-record matching is almost inert; coarse routing realizes the desired
+tagged fine-record graft to the small bound in (4). The nonce's independence
+can be supplied by the actual generation/causal design, rather than guessed
+from bath measurements. With genuinely informative fine records, condition
+coarsening is allowed only when (2) or an explicit error budget is acquired.
+
+### Approximate matching with continuous informative records
+
+The response certificate can be used without coarse bins. Suppose a known
+observed scalar t(c) lies in [a,b], and, uniformly over the scored policy
+menu and all relevant c,c', an acquired bound gives
+
+\[
+ \tfrac12\|\Lambda_a^{\tau_c}-\Lambda_a^{\tau_{c'}}\|_\diamond
+ \le L|t(c)-t(c')|.                                         \tag{4a}
+\]
+
+For even N, sort the batch by t and exchange adjacent pairs. Conditional on
+the complete fine record list, the copies remain independent under the iid
+joint preparation contract. Donor j then sees its recipient's tau rather
+than its own. By the diamond bound, the batch-mean expected score differs
+from the sample average of the ideal fine-C graft scores by at most
+
+\[
+ \frac{2L}{N}\sum_{k=1}^{N/2}(t_{(2k)}-t_{(2k-1)})
+ \le \frac{2L(b-a)}{N}.                                    \tag{4b}
+\]
+
+The paired intervals are disjoint subsets of [a,b], proving the second
+inequality. Averaging over the records gives the same bias bound against
+the population fine-C graft score. Every fine C may be unique almost surely;
+exact matching would be inert, whereas this protocol gives O(1/N) worst-case
+task bias and uses N/2 block SWAPs. For donor-specific policies a(c), the
+Lipschitz certificate must hold for each such policy with both compared bath
+states. For odd N, keeping one singleton adds at most 1/N to the stated
+even-batch upper bound; discarding it changes the target and is not assumed.
+
+The same proof covers simultaneous upper confidence edge costs and a
+minimum-cost permutation, provided the edge certificate is valid for all
+candidate matches and route selection does not inspect hidden replica
+states. This is ordinary assignment optimization, not an algorithmic
+novelty claim. A selected task may admit tighter costs than a full-channel
+diamond certificate.
+
+Equation (4a), its scope/support and its calibration uncertainty are paid
+inputs. A smooth recorded scalar by itself does not establish a smooth
+conditional bath response. Fine CE preservation is not claimed. This is a
+conditional removal of exact-record collision cost, not removal of the
+correlation-safe router or cross-independence premises.
+
+## 3. The exact partial-independence requirement
+
+Let Omega be an arbitrary joint N-replica state with a measured label/routing
+transcript T. On a branch t, donor j(t) routes to recipient i(t). An ideal
+data permutation has tagged state exactly
+
+\[
+ \Omega_{R_jS_jE_i|t}.                                       \tag{5}
+\]
+
+Consequently full N-copy independence can be replaced by the selection-stable
+cross-marginal condition
+
+\[
+ \Omega_{R_jS_jE_i|t}
+ =\Omega_{R_jS_j|t}\otimes\Omega_{E_i|t}.                     \tag{6}
+\]
+
+This is sufficient, and is necessary if equality is required for all future
+channels and all effects. If (6) fails, the difference of the two states has
+a positive spectral projector that separates them by their trace distance.
+For a limited task menu only indistinguishability under that menu is needed.
+For comparison with a specified unselected cq ensemble, the two conditional
+marginals in (6) must additionally equal the intended sigma_c and tau_c (or
+the declared coarse bath mixture). Otherwise selection changes the target
+marginals even when the conditional cross state factorizes. The iid
+finite-singleton formula is not inferred from (6) alone.
+
+With discrepancy epsilon_t equal to that trace distance, the average
+tagged task-score error is at most \(\sum_t\Pr(t)\epsilon_t\). This statement
+includes conditioning on the entire selection transcript: pairwise
+independence before adaptive matching does not automatically survive its
+selection events. Nor do one-copy statistics certify (6).
+
+**Non-iid success example.** Three fair hidden phase bits conditioned on even
+parity are globally dependent but every pair is independent. Constant C and
+a deterministic 3-cycle satisfy (6), so tagged grafting works exactly. This
+strictly weakens the source's full-iid requirement for the mean. It does not
+supply independent endpoints or a free concentration bound.
+
+## 4. A bath-marginal and reset-probe certificate is insufficient
+
+Take two independent copies of any correlated state \(\rho_{RSE}\), with
+identical bath marginal tau. Compare ideal \(U_0=SWAP_{S_1S_2}\) with
+
+\[
+ U_1=SWAP_{S_1S_2}\otimes SWAP_{E_1E_2}.                     \tag{7}
+\]
+
+Both have exactly the same reduced action on every accessible-register
+input, including arbitrary initial correlations. Both square to identity.
+The complete bath marginal is tau tensor tau before and after (7); even
+complete bath-state tomography sees no change in this marginal.
+
+More strongly, prepare ANY accessible-register probe state xi, possibly
+entangled across the copies and with external references, independently of
+the baths. Because bath SWAP fixes tau tensor tau,
+
+\[
+ U_0(\xi\otimes\tau\otimes\tau)U_0^\dagger
+ =U_1(\xi\otimes\tau\otimes\tau)U_1^\dagger.                 \tag{8}
+\]
+
+Thus every subsequent probe, even a joint bath-and-system measurement,
+has identical calibration data on this reset-input class. Arbitrarily many
+such product-probe process tomographies cannot resolve the ambiguity.
+
+Nevertheless on the native correlated input, U_1 delivers the donor bath
+with the donor state, so the intended conditional decorrelation fails. In
+the u=0.2 phase model the ideal tagged echo score is 0.68; U_1's score is 1.
+The unmatched mass is zero, all local and joint bath marginals agree, and
+the reset-probe certificate is perfect. The error is still 0.32.
+
+This falsifies a proposed acquisition shortcut, not every system-only
+certification protocol. A router audit must constrain action on relevant
+correlations, or use justified locality/no-cross-bath-transfer premises, or
+an adequate family of independently auditable correlated calibration
+states. Merely showing that the bath's state or its product-input channel
+is unchanged cannot furnish that contract.
+
+**Reference-pairing boundary, invented by quantum_information_operation,
+relayed by root and independently checked here.** Let
+\(\rho_{RSE}=|0\rangle\langle0|_S\otimes\Phi_{RE}\). Data SWAP between two
+copies leaves the entire physical state unchanged. A later local SWAP_SE
+returns a Bell pair to each resident reference, scoring 1. Pairing each
+output with the other, donor-tracked reference instead scores 1/4. The
+tagged acquisition identity remains correct: the operational estimand
+includes routing/job/reference assignment. It is not by itself a measure
+of changed resident processor dynamics. Any held-out decision must specify
+this assignment and justify its relevance to the physical job.
+
+## 5. A known virtual alternative trades routing for sampling
+
+Suppose actual local measurement and replacement primitives at the cut are
+certified to act on S alone. Take two independent same-condition copies.
+Measure donor S; send its classical outcome to the recipient; discard the
+recipient S nonselectively and prepare a state determined by that outcome.
+Retain donor R. The recipient environment marginal is tau, independently of
+the donor's conditional reference state. No data-register transport or
+coherent intermodule SWAP is required. This is a score estimator, not an
+entanglement-preserving physical output state.
+
+For d-dimensional S choose a Haar-random orthonormal basis or an appropriate
+finite 2-design/MUB implementation. Define D+ by measuring and preparing
+the observed basis vector. Define D- by measuring and preparing a uniformly
+chosen orthogonal vector in that basis. Averaging gives
+
+\[
+ D_+(A)=\frac{A+I\operatorname{Tr}A}{d+1},\qquad
+ D_-(A)=\frac{dI\operatorname{Tr}A-A}{d^2-1},
+ \qquad \operatorname{id}=dD_+-(d-1)D_-.                     \tag{9}
+\]
+
+For a qubit only the X,Y,Z measurement bases are needed: prepare the same
+eigenstate for D+, the opposite eigenstate for D-. Each branch is a physical
+measure-and-prepare channel. Equation (9), including its extension by an
+arbitrary untouched reference, follows directly by substitution. Its signed
+combination reconstructs \(\sigma_{RS}\otimes\tau_E\) before continuation.
+
+Let gamma=2d-1. Sample + with probability d/gamma and - with probability
+(d-1)/gamma. For an available raw score m in [0,1], the centered estimator
+
+\[
+ Y=\frac12+\gamma\operatorname{sign}(t)(m-\tfrac12)           \tag{10}
+\]
+
+has mean equal to the ideal tagged graft score. Its range has length gamma,
+so independent trials/batches need gamma squared times the ordinary bounded
+score Hoeffding budget. For one qubit the multiplier is 9. For m qubits
+collectively it is \((2^{m+1}-1)^2\), in addition to local basis synthesis,
+reference measurement, full-history preparation, record matching, feedforward,
+readout calibration and bath-safe local-operation costs. Measuring Bell
+fidelity by separate Pauli correlators gives raw range [-1/2,1], whose width
+1.5 must also be charged if comparing with a direct binary Bell projection.
+
+The coefficient norm gamma is optimal among signed decompositions of the
+identity into deterministic entanglement-breaking channels. Indeed, their
+normalized Choi states are separable, with overlap with the maximally
+entangled state at most 1/d. If positive coefficients total a and negative
+coefficients total b, trace preservation gives a-b=1. Unit Choi overlap
+requires 1<=a/d, so a>=d and a+b>=2d-1. Equation (9) attains this. This is
+not a universal lower bound for a particular easy task functional, and it is
+not a new wire-cutting result.
+
+The conditional/coarse matching and selection-stable cross-independence
+conditions of Sections 2-3 apply unchanged to this estimator. Local
+measure-and-prepare bath disturbance does NOT disappear by algebra; a real
+local-operation certificate is still required. System-only benchmarking of
+those primitives does not automatically supply such a certificate.

+# Conditional exchange: a matching extension and a stronger acquisition obstruction
+
+**Status:** internally derived conditional results and exact counterexamples;
+synthetic finite checks passed. No new physical implementation, independent
+validation, historical novelty, cost advantage, or civilization-scale
+capability is established.
+
+The most useful positive result removes a genuine record-matching cost:
+matching need only preserve the environment's response to the selected future
+tasks. If a certified coarse record Z captures that response, quantum states
+can be exchanged within Z while their full fine records C and original
+references remain attached to the jobs. The finite unmatched mass then
+depends on Z, not on the potentially enormous alphabet of C.
+
+The strongest negative result concerns the more important physical gate.
+A hidden exchange of the two baths, accompanying the desired data SWAP,
+passes accessible gate tests, double-SWAP tests, complete bath-marginal
+tomography, and every reset-input continuation-channel test. It nevertheless
+undoes the intended decorrelation. A task-specific audit of bath marginals
+or independent probe responses is therefore insufficient to certify the
+router's action on native correlations.
+
+## Exact input/output/cost contract
+
+Input is a specified cq preparation \(\rho_{CRSE}\), the actually observed
+record C, a predeclared menu of bounded scored continuations, independent
+preparations or a weaker selection-stable cross-independence certificate,
+and a physical routing/instrument implementation. No unknown conditional
+state, bath model, reset independence, decoder, or environmental action
+certificate is supplied by notation alone.
+
+Output is a tagged job/reference score comparison under an actual finite
+batch operation, or a bounded inference of the ideal conditional product
+functional. Tagged reference reassignment is part of the estimand. Its
+effect need not imply changed resident processor dynamics.
+
+Preparation histories, environment reset/mixing, condition acquisition,
+reference storage/readout, matching, physical routing, local measurement
+and reset, calibration trials, latency, within-batch dependence, loss,
+switching work and readout cost are charged. Replicas are preparations, not
+copies cloned from an unknown quantum input. All error bounds refer to
+predeclared tasks and the stated condition/support interface.
+
+## Retained theorem: certified coarse matching
+
+Let \(Z=f(C)\), \(q_z=\Pr(Z=z)\), and
+\(\bar\tau_z=\mathbb E[\rho_E^C|Z=z]\). Within coarse classes cycle the S
+registers, keep singletons native, and follow each donor's full C and R.
+For N iid preparations the exact tagged output is
+
+\[
+ \rho_N^Z=\sum_c p_c|c\rangle\langle c|\otimes
+ \left[(1-q_{f(c)})^{N-1}\rho_{RSE}^c+
+ \bigl(1-(1-q_{f(c)})^{N-1}\bigr)
+ \rho_{RS}^c\otimes\bar\tau_{f(c)}\right].
+\]
+
+If the selected continuation channels induced by \(\rho_E^c\) and
+\(\bar\tau_{f(c)}\) agree, every reference-inclusive scored task agrees with
+ideal fine-C decorrelation up to coarse singleton mass
+\(s_N(Z)=\sum_zq_z(1-q_z)^{N-1}\). Approximate channel differences add their
+probability-weighted half-diamond distances; two-policy contrasts add the
+two per-policy bounds. If the environment states themselves agree, the
+full fine CE marginal also stays fixed. Task equivalence alone does not
+preserve that physical marginal.
+
+The exact cost removal is large in a supplied sufficient-record family.
+For C=(Z,U), fair Z and an independent 128-bit nonce U, with bath marginal
+depending only on Z, N=32 fine matching leaves at least
+\(1-31\,2^{-129}\) of jobs untouched. Coarse matching leaves only
+\(2^{-31}=4.657\times10^{-10}\) unmatched. Fine U may change the donor RS
+state through genuinely local controls. The operation preserves that state
+by tracking its donor, rather than demanding identical RS states within Z.
+
+This is a conditional mechanism, not a universal discovery algorithm for Z.
+Equality of selected bath-induced channels can be calibrated using an
+adequate system-only causal-break probe frame when those primitives and
+conditional preparations are available. For unique informative records,
+neither learning Z nor uniform/average channel equivalence is free.
+
+A stronger conditional corollary handles continuously varying informative
+labels with no exact repeats. Suppose an observed scalar t(c) lies in a
+known interval of width R, with a paid uniform response bound
+\(\frac12\|\Lambda_a^{\tau_c}-\Lambda_a^{\tau_{c'}}\|_\diamond
+\le L|t(c)-t(c')|\) for every scored donor-specific policy. Sort an even
+batch by t and swap adjacent pairs. The expected tagged batch score differs
+from the sample ideal fine-C graft mean by at most \(2LR/N\), since the
+paired gaps are disjoint subsets of the interval. This gives O(1/N) task
+bias even when exact fine-label collisions have probability zero. For odd
+N, retaining one singleton adds at most 1/N. Conditional joint-source
+independence given the full fine record list, the response certificate and
+the router operation certificate remain necessary. Fine CE preservation is
+not claimed. The Lipschitz bound must be acquired; ordinary smooth record
+values do not supply it.
+
+## Partial independence and what it buys
+
+The exact tagged state after an ideal permutation is the original cross
+marginal \(\Omega_{R_jS_jE_i|T}\), conditional on the full selection
+transcript T. Full N-replica iid can therefore be weakened to factorization
+of that cross marginal, with the correct intended one-body marginals.
+Global high-order correlations can remain. Three fair hidden phase bits
+conditioned on even parity give an explicit non-iid success example: every
+routed pair is independent, so a fixed 3-cycle has the desired mean.
+
+This weakens the mathematical premise but does not acquire it from local
+statistics, supply the iid singleton formula for arbitrary labels, or make
+endpoints independent. Confidence statements still use independent batches
+or a separately justified dependence model. Adaptive selection must retain
+the condition after its full transcript is revealed.
+
+## Decisive stronger falsifier
+
+Compare ideal \(SWAP_S\) with \(SWAP_S\otimes SWAP_E\) on two independently
+prepared identical native states. The entire bath marginal is
+\(\tau_E\otimes\tau_E\), invariant under bath exchange. For every accessible
+probe xi initially independent of these baths, both operations produce
+the same complete joint output state. No amount of calibration restricted
+to this reset-input class can distinguish them.
+
+On native correlated phase states with u=0.2, the ideal tagged echo score
+is 0.68; the hidden bath exchange gives 1.00. All stated audits have zero
+error. The extra bath exchange carries each state's old environmental
+association along with it. Environmental state preservation is strictly
+weaker than a correlation-safe operation certificate.
+
+The quantum_information_operation worker invented an additional interpretive
+falsifier, relayed by root and independently checked here:
+\(\rho_{RSE}=|0\rangle\langle0|_S\otimes\Phi_{RE}\). Exchanging blank
+S registers changes no physical state. A subsequent local SWAP_SE gives
+Bell score 1 with resident references but 1/4 with donor references. Thus a
+tagged contrast of 3/4 can be reference/job reassignment alone. The algebra
+is correct; a causal claim about altered physical processor behavior needs
+a separately justified workload interpretation.
+
+## A lower-hardware comparator: known wire cutting
+
+An exact signed estimator can replace coherent intermodule exchange by
+local donor measurements, classical communication and local recipient
+replacement, provided those local instruments have the required bath-action
+certificate. For one qubit, randomly measure X,Y or Z. Let D+ prepare the
+same outcome eigenstate at the recipient and D- the opposite eigenstate.
+Then \(id=2D_+-D_-\), including an arbitrary donor reference. Applying the
+future and scoring gives an unbiased ideal tagged product-state score.
+
+The centered estimator has coefficient norm 3 and a factor-9 bounded-score
+sampling budget. For an m-qubit collective cut the known optimum is
+\((2^{m+1}-1)^2\); local collective-basis synthesis and readout are additional
+costs. Uniform per-branch task bias epsilon can amplify to
+\((2^{m+1}-1)\epsilon\). This procedure estimates a scalar and never
+prepares a reference-preserving entangled routed state. Local reset/bath
+collateral action remains a physical premise, so it does not solve the
+arbitrary black-box environment problem.
+
+This is established wire-cutting machinery, reconstructed as a compulsory
+competitor to the exchange proposal. For a one-qubit assay whose coherent
+transport takes more than nine times the complete local protocol cost, the
+virtual estimator can win under equal error/bias conditions. That is a
+conditional resource threshold, not a measured platform advantage. Bell
+fidelity obtained from separate Pauli correlators has raw score range
+[-1/2,1], which changes the absolute concentration budget if the coherent
+baseline has a binary Bell projection.
+
+## Capital and primary-literature comparison
+

+interface, rather than assuming its resolution. N820's sharp target/response
+row-space criterion motivates task-specific coarse response, but supplies
+no quantum operation or physical calibration premise. P-q-d-mem concerns
+density-state reconstruction and cannot replace entangled donor reference
+preservation; N710 supplies a classical supplied-noise model, not an
+acquired quantum-bath independence certificate.

+| [Coeuret Cauquil et al., cavity-QED decorrelation](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.07011v2) | Already recombines subsystems from two atom-cavity preparations. Uses controlled cavity access and quantum-state reconstruction. Count full preparations, second cavity, switching, postselection and readout; do not claim replica recombination is new. |

Local instrument validation and synthesis remain paid. |
+| Direct randomized policy trials | Already select between executable policies on the tested distribution. Any exchange assay must improve a further held-out routing, scheduling or controller-design decision after its extra cost. |
+
+These comparisons identify necessary costs and existing methods. No matched
+hardware experiment or numerical cost advantage over them was acquired.
+
+## Strongest missing premise and next decisive test
+
+The strongest missing physical premise is an operation-on-correlations
+certificate: the router must not transport, recreate or change the relevant
+environmental association while passing marginal tests. This is stronger
+than unchanged bath density matrices. A universal system-only reset-probe
+shortcut is ruled out by the explicit bath-exchange counterexample.

+Y = np.array([[0,-1j],[1j,0]], dtype=complex)

+    out = np.zeros_like(sigma)

+# Strict heat certificates control full critical-trace storage

+Research date: 15 October 2026. Worker: external_machinery.

+## Result and limits
+

+## 2. Exact contract and removal of the affine mean term
+
+Use normalized transverse averaging on `T=R/(2 pi Z)`. Let `F:R^(m x 2)->R` be a homogeneous quartic polynomial. Let
+
+    H(A)=|A|^4,
+    F-epsilon H be quasiconvex for some epsilon>0.           (2.1)
+
+Quasiconvexity is global at every affine matrix, with all zero-boundary perturbations. Polynomial growth passes it to `W^(1,4)` tests and, by periodic extension or tiling/cutoff, to periodic compatible tests. No rotational invariance is required for this theorem.
+
+Fix `B` and define the relative integrand
+
+    f_B(A)=F(B+A)-F(B)-DF(B):A.                             (2.2)
+
+For a finite strip `Phi in W^(1,4)([0,T0] x T;R^m)`, periodic in y and with endpoint values understood as Sobolev traces, put
+
+    J_B(Phi)=integral_0^T0 E_y f_B(D Phi) dx.               (2.3)
+
+All incoming paths are allowed: `T0>0`, `Phi(0,. )=0`, and `Phi(T0,. )=U`. Their transverse means may move along the strip. Define
+
+    p_B(U)=inf {J_B(Phi): Phi is such an incoming path}.    (2.4)
+
+The infimum is over these `W^(1,4)` strips and finite widths, with no width upper bound and no asserted minimizer. This definition is necessary for rough critical traces; a smooth-only incoming class would be empty for a general `U in W^(3/4,4)`. Finiteness and continuity will be proved, not assumed.
+
+For smooth endpoint data, this infimum agrees with the infimum over smooth strips with those exact endpoints. At a fixed finite width, subtract a smooth extension of the boundary data, approximate the resulting zero-trace function in `W^(1,4)` by smooth functions vanishing on the two x faces and periodic in y, and restore the extension. Polynomial growth makes the actions converge. The same argument applies to strips between two smooth traces. No smoothing of a rough trace while claiming its endpoint is unchanged is used.
+
+The adjusted value is invariant under addition of an output constant. To see this, prepend a ramp from zero to a constant `c`, then translate any incoming path by `c`. The ramp of width `L` has gradient `(c/L|0)` and adjusted action
+
+    L f_B((c/L|0)) = O_B(|c|^2/L+|c|^3/L^2+|c|^4/L^3),
+
+which tends to zero. Thus `p_B(U+c)<=p_B(U)`; applying the same argument with `-c` gives equality. This argument retains paths with moving means rather than projecting them away.

+The storage for the **original** action is therefore

+    P_B(U)=F_1(B).E_y U+p_B(U-E_y U),                      (2.5)

+on a strip from `U` to `W`; the second-column integral vanishes.

+## 3. An explicit bounded trace extension

+
+    E:X -> W^(1,4)([-1,0] x T;R^m),
+    (EU)(-1,. )=0, (EU)(0,. )=U.                          (3.1)

+Write

+    e_p(U)=||D(EU)||_(L^p([-1,0] x T)), p=2,4.             (3.2)
+
+The measure uses normalized y averaging, so `e_2<=e_4` on this unit slab. The norm `e_4` is equivalent to the usual norm on `X`, with fixed extension/trace constants. All constants below refer to this supplied choice of extension; no claim of optimal constants is made.
+
+A concrete construction is useful. Set `t=-x`. Choose a smooth periodic mollifier `eta_t`, obtained by periodizing a compactly supported real-line mollifier at scale `t`, and a smooth cutoff `chi` with `chi(0)=1`, `chi(1)=0`, identically one near zero. Put

+    (EU)(-t,y)=chi(t)(eta_t*U)(y).                         (3.3)

+The zero integral of differentiated kernels gives, for the derivative terms near `t=0`,
+
+    ||D(eta_t*U)||_4^4
+      <= C t^(-5) integral_(|h|<=t) ||U(.+h)-U||_4^4 dh.

+After integrating in `t`, Tonelli gives a bound by

+    C integral_(|h|<=1) ||U(.+h)-U||_4^4 / |h|^4 dh,
+
+which is the critical Slobodeckij seminorm (`1+4*(3/4)=4`). The cutoff terms are bounded by `C||U||_4^4`, controlled by the same norm on mean-zero profiles. The extension has no finite frequency cutoff and keeps all interactions in the bulk action.

+## 4. Strict quasiconvexity gives duration-independent coercivity

+The elementary quartic remainder satisfies
+
+    H(B+A)-H(B)-DH(B):A
+      >= (1/4)(|B|^2|A|^2+|A|^4).                        (4.1)
+
+For a direct proof, normalize `|A|=1`, write `B=t A+Bperp` with `Bperp:A=0`, and put `s^2=|Bperp|^2`. The left side is

+Subtracting the right side gives

+    (23/4)(t+8/23)^2+(7/4)s^2+5/92 >=0.                 (4.2)

+Restoring homogeneity proves (4.1). At `B=0` the exact remainder is `H(A)`, and this sharper fact is used later.
+
+Because `F` is a quartic polynomial, choose finite constants `C0,C1` such that
+
+    |f_B(A)| <= C0(|B|^2|A|^2+|A|^4),                    (4.3)
+    |D f_B(A)| <= C1(|B|^2|A|+|A|^3).                    (4.4)

+These bounds require no positivity of `F`. For example if `||D^2F(A)||<=C2|A|^2`, Taylor's formula permits `C0=C2`, `C1=2C2`.

+Take any incoming path `Phi` ending at a mean-zero `U`. Follow it with the reversed fixed extension `RU` from `U` to zero. The concatenated potential is continuous, belongs to `W^(1,4)`, and has equal zero profiles at its two ends; it may be extended periodically in x. No matching of first derivatives across the seam is needed for `W^(1,4)` compatibility.

+Applying (2.1), subtracting the zero total linear term, and using (4.1) yields

+    J_B(Phi)+J_B(RU)
+      >= (epsilon/4) integral_closed

+                                      +||D Phi||_4^4]

+
+    |integral [f_B(A+Z)-f_B(A)]|
+      <= C1[|B|^2 (||A||_2+||Z||_2)||Z||_2
+                     +(||A||_4+||Z||_4)^3||Z||_4].       (5.1)

+    K=max{K_B(U),K_B(W)}.

+Apply (4.8), let `eta` tend to zero, and then exchange `U,W`. One obtains

+                            +(K^(1/4)+e_4(delta))^3 e_4(delta)].  (5.2)

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Exact finite checks; analytic proofs are in HEAT_TO_CRITICAL_TRACE.md."""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import hashlib
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+import subprocess
+import sys
+
+import sympy as sp
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+ASTRA = Path('/Users/harjas/Documents/ChatGPT/ultra/work/astra-capital-compensation-exchange')
+EXPECTED_PIN = '00631610750c708263d5cf6d812ebbb8edc77335'
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    actual_pin = subprocess.check_output(['git', 'rev-parse', 'HEAD'], cwd=ASTRA, text=True).strip()
+    assert actual_pin == EXPECTED_PIN
+    a, b, c, d, w, q, s, t, h = sp.symbols('a b c d w q s t h', real=True)
+    A = sp.Matrix([[a, b], [c, d]])
+    u, v = a*a+c*c, b*b+d*d
+    ww, qq = a*b+c*d, A.det()
+    f = u*u+v*v+4*ww*ww+sp.Rational(7, 2)*qq*qq-sp.Rational(29, 10)*qq*(u+v)
+    assert sp.expand(u*v-ww*ww-qq*qq) == 0
+    rewrite = (u+v)**2+2*ww**2+sp.Rational(3, 2)*qq**2-sp.Rational(29, 10)*qq*(u+v)
+    assert sp.expand(f-rewrite) == 0
+    assert f.subs({a:1,b:0,c:0,d:1}) == -sp.Rational(3, 10)
+    assert sp.expand(f.subs({a:-a,b:-b,c:-c,d:-d})-f) == 0
+
+    # Envelope signs hold on -1/2 <= t <= 1/2 because the factors below
+    # are nonnegative there. They do not rely on sampled eigenvalues.
+    lower = 1+sp.Rational(3,2)*t*t-sp.Rational(29,10)*t
+    upper = sp.Rational(3,2)-sp.Rational(1,2)*t*t-sp.Rational(29,10)*t
+    assert sp.expand(lower+sp.Rational(3,40)-(sp.Rational(1,2)-t)*(sp.Rational(43,20)-sp.Rational(3,2)*t)) == 0
+    assert sp.expand(sp.Rational(113,40)-upper-(t+sp.Rational(1,2))*(sp.Rational(53,20)+sp.Rational(1,2)*t)) == 0
+
+    # R_H(B,A) with |A|=1, B=t A+Bperp and |Bperp|=h.
+    rem = 6*t*t+2*h*h+4*t+1
+    completion = sp.Rational(23,4)*(t+sp.Rational(8,23))**2+sp.Rational(7,4)*h*h+sp.Rational(5,92)
+    assert sp.expand(rem-sp.Rational(1,4)*(t*t+h*h+1)-completion) == 0
+
+    # Circular profile: the y average is already constant pointwise.
+    x, r, p = sp.symbols('x r p', real=True)
+    radial = p**4+r**4+sp.Rational(7,2)*p*p*r*r-sp.Rational(29,10)*p*r*(p*p+r*r)
+    ramp = sp.integrate(radial.subs({r:x/2,p:sp.Rational(1,2)}), (x,0,1))
+    assert ramp == sp.Rational(23,1920)
+    exponential = sp.integrate(radial.subs(p,r)/r, (r,sp.Rational(1,2),1))
+    assert exponential == -sp.Rational(9,128)
+    entry = ramp+exponential
+    assert entry == -sp.Rational(7,120)
+    assert sp.expand(radial.subs({p:-p,r:-r})-radial) == 0
+
+    rho = sp.Rational(1,500)
+    epsilon = rho/24
+    assert epsilon == sp.Rational(1,12000)
+    M = sp.Rational(113,40)
+    K1 = sp.Rational(4)+4+sp.Rational(7,2)+sp.Rational(29,5)
+    assert K1 == sp.Rational(173,10)
+    assert 2*M/epsilon == 67800
+    assert sp.Rational(1,1000)/24 == sp.Rational(1,24000)
+
+    # Critical profile/strip scaling and vanishing background terms.
+    amplitude = -sp.Rational(3,4)
+    gradient = amplitude+1
+    assert 4*gradient-1 == 0
+    assert 3*gradient-1 == -sp.Rational(1,4)
+    assert 2*gradient-1 == -sp.Rational(1,2)
+    # In the Hardy-BMO disjoint-bump obstruction in 2D, bulk quartic
+    # energy is invariant and the squared-gradient BMO norm grows 1/r.
+    assert 4*(sp.Rational(1,2)-1)+2 == 0
+    assert 2*(sp.Rational(1,2)-1) == -1
+
+    source_verifier = ASTRA/'updates/FE/synthesis/quartic/checks/verify_closed_heat.py'

+    (ROOT/'source_heat_replay.stdout.json').write_text(source.stdout)
+    (ROOT/'source_heat_replay.stderr.txt').write_text(source.stderr)
+    source_result=json.loads(source.stdout)

+        'status':'PASS',

+        'full_nine_coefficient_cone':'OPEN',
+        'finite_evaluation_algorithm':'NOT SUPPLIED',
+        'historical_novelty':'UNKNOWN',
+        'external_mathematical_review':'UNKNOWN',
+    }
+    (ROOT/'verification.json').write_text(json.dumps(result,indent=2)+'\n')

+
+

+

+This note extends incoming Theorem 2.1 from first transverse derivatives to
+every fixed finite derivative order. It also checks the critical-trace and
+concatenation arguments. No repository or supplied original was changed.
+
+All profiles U,V are arbitrary C-infinity periodic maps T -> R^2, where T has
+period 2*pi. Their means are NOT constrained. E denotes normalized y-average.
+F:R^(2x2)->R is continuous and differentiable at the fixed background B. No
+growth bound, rotational symmetry, homogeneity, convexity, or rank-one
+convexity is required for the rigidity theorem. Smoothness of the storage
+density means C-infinity on the whole finite-dimensional jet space.
+
+The action and domination condition are
+
+  L_B(U,V) = E [F(B+(V|U'))-F(B)],
+  DP(U)[V] <= L_B(U,V)                         for every smooth U,V.  (D)
+
+Equivalently, when the density is smooth, (D) is domination on all positive
+duration smooth compatible strips, by the chain rule and short straight
+profile paths. No limiting regularity of P on nonsmooth profiles is assumed.
+
+THEOREM A: EVERY SMOOTH FINITE-JET DENSITY REDUCES TO FIRST ORDER
+
+Fix an integer k>=1 and suppose
+
+  P(U) = E p(U,U',...,U^(k)),
+
+where p is smooth and satisfies (D). Then there are smooth A:R^2->R^2,
+c:R^2->R and a smooth finite-jet H of order at most k-1 such that, identically
+on the jet space,
+
+  p(j^k U) = A(U).U' + c(U) + D_y H(j^(k-1)U).              (A1)
+
+The last term integrates to zero for every smooth periodic U. Thus finite
+higher derivatives do not enlarge the set of possible smooth local storage
+functionals under universal domination.
+
+Proof, step 1: a uniform L1 bound on the Euler derivative.
+
+Write q_j=U^(j), with q_0=U, and let D be total y differentiation. The Euler
+derivative of p is the smooth vector-valued differential expression
+
+  e_p(j^(2k)U) = sum_(j=0)^k (-D)^j p_(q_j)(j^k U),
+  DP(U)[V] = E e_p(j^(2k)U).V.                              (A2)
+
+For R<infinity put
+
+  M_R = max_(|q|<=R, |v|<=1) |F(B+(v|q))-F(B)| < infinity.
+
+If ||U'||_infinity<=R, use the smooth test velocity
+
+  V_eta(y) = e_p(y) / sqrt(|e_p(y)|^2+eta^2).
+
+Its pointwise norm is <=1. Condition (D) gives E e_p.V_eta <= M_R. Let eta
+decrease to zero, using dominated convergence for this fixed smooth U:
+
+  E |e_p(j^(2k)U)| <= M_R.                                  (A3)
+
+This is the crucial bound. It controls the Euler derivative independently
+of every profile derivative above first order. It uses only local
+boundedness of F. In particular, there is no hidden polynomial growth
+assumption on either F or p.
+
+Proof, step 2: an oscillation lemma.
+
+Suppose a smooth differential expression has the form
+
+  e(j^r U) = C(j^(r-1)U) U^(r) + R_0(j^(r-1)U),  r>=2,     (A4)
+
+and has a uniform L1 bound on every set ||U'||_infinity<=R. Then C=0 at
+every jet. Indeed, choose any fixed smooth periodic U_0, any h in R^2,
+0<epsilon<1, and integers N tending to infinity, and set
+
+  U_N(y)=U_0(y)+N^(-r+epsilon) h sin(Ny).
+
+All jets through order r-1 converge uniformly to those of U_0. In
+particular ||U_N'||_infinity is uniformly bounded. Dividing (A4) by
+N^epsilon gives, uniformly in y,
+
+  N^(-epsilon)e(j^r U_N)
+    = C(j^(r-1)U_0(y)) h sin(Ny+r*pi/2) + o(1).
+
+Periodic averaging of |sin| against the continuous coefficient yields
+
+  lim_N N^(-epsilon) E|e(j^r U_N)|
+    = (2/pi) E|C(j^(r-1)U_0)h|.                            (A5)
+
+The uniform L1 bound makes the left side zero. Thus C(j^(r-1)U_0)h is
+identically zero. Every finite jet at any point is realizable by a smooth
+periodic map: multiply its local Taylor polynomial by a bump supported
+in a coordinate interval. Hence C=0 on the whole jet space. This also
+explains why the same argument cannot remove an order-one skew term:
+r>=2 is needed to keep U_N' bounded.
+
+Proof, step 3: eliminate the highest-jet Hessian.
+
+The highest derivative in the Euler expression (A2) is linear, with
+
+  e_p = (-1)^k p_(q_k q_k)(j^k U) U^(2k)
+          + R_1(j^(2k-1)U).                               (A6)
+
+For j<k the summand (-D)^j p_(q_j) has order at most k+j<=2k-1.
+In the last summand, the only order-2k term comes from differentiating
+p_(q_k) once with respect to q_k and then applying all k total derivatives
+to that argument. This proves (A6), including for nonlinear smooth p.
+
+The oscillation lemma with r=2k and (A3) gives p_(q_k q_k)=0 everywhere.
+Consequently
+
+  p(q_0,...,q_k) = a(q_0,...,q_(k-1)).q_k
+                     + b(q_0,...,q_(k-1)).                (A7)
+
+Proof, step 4: eliminate the highest affine curvature when k>=2.
+
+Let D_(q_(k-1))a denote the matrix with entries
+partial a_i / partial(q_(k-1))_j. Directly from (A2) and (A7),
+
+  e_p = (-1)^k [D_(q_(k-1))a - (D_(q_(k-1))a)^T]
+                    U^(2k-1) + R_2(j^(2k-2)U).             (A8)
+
+Only (-D)^k a and the q_(k-1) derivative of a.q_k contribute at order
+2k-1. Their coefficients are respectively (-1)^k Da and
+(-1)^(k-1) Da^T, proving (A8). When k>=2, r=2k-1>=3, so the same
+oscillation lemma makes the bracket zero.
+
+For fixed lower jets q_0,...,q_(k-2), the one-form a.dq_(k-1) is therefore
+closed on the entire Euclidean q_(k-1) space. A global smooth primitive is
+
+  h(q_0,...,q_(k-1))
+    = integral_0^1 a(q_0,...,q_(k-2),t q_(k-1)).q_(k-1) dt.
+
+It satisfies h_(q_(k-1))=a. Therefore p-D_y h depends only on jets through
+order k-1. The integral of D_y h is zero on each periodic profile, so the
+reduced density defines exactly the same functional and still obeys (D).
+Repeat this reduction until k=1. Step 3 at k=1 makes the resulting density
+affine in q_1, giving (A1). QED.
+
+THEOREM B: FIXED-BACKGROUND EXISTENCE IS EXACTLY DETERMINANT-AFFINE SUPPORT
+
+Under the hypotheses above, the following are equivalent:
+
+  (i) There is a dominating smooth local storage of some finite order.
+ (ii) There is a real kappa such that for every X in R^(2x2),
+
+  F(B+X)-F(B)-DF(B):X >= kappa det X.                       (B1)
+
+If (ii) holds, a first-order storage is
+
+  P(U)=F_1(B).E U + (kappa/2) E det(U,U').                  (B2)
+
+Here F_1(B),F_2(B) are the derivatives with respect to the first and second
+matrix columns. Thus permitting ANY fixed finite number of transverse
+derivatives cannot go beyond the incoming first-order theorem.
+
+Proof of necessity and the complete surviving first-order structure.
+
+By Theorem A we may use p=A(z).q+c(z). Put
+
+  kappa(z)=partial_1 A_2(z)-partial_2 A_1(z).
+
+Integration by parts gives
+
+  DP(U)[V] = E [grad c(U).V + kappa(U) det(V,U')].          (B3)
+
+For U=z constant and V=t v constant, domination and differentiability of
+F at B, with both signs of t, give grad c(z)=F_1(B). Thus c is affine.
+
+Fix z_0 and arbitrary smooth v and smooth mean-zero q. Write q=w' with
+w periodic, use U_N=z_0+w(Ny)/N and V_N=v(Ny), and let N tend to infinity.
+The left side of (B3) converges by uniform convergence of U_N to z_0,
+while the action's average is exactly unchanged by integer dilation. Hence
+
+  E [F(B+(v|q))-F(B)-F_1(B).v-kappa(z_0)det(v,q)] >=0.     (B4)
+
+For arbitrary v_0,q_0, choose (v,q)=(v_0,q_0) on a fraction theta of the
+period and (v,q)=(0,-theta q_0/(1-theta)) on the rest. Periodic smoothing
+preserves mean(q)=0 and has uniformly bounded values; continuity of F
+therefore justifies this piecewise-constant test. Divide (B4) by theta and
+let theta decrease to zero. Differentiability of F at B handles the small
+compensating transverse column and gives
+
+  F(B+(v_0|q_0))-F(B)-F_1(B).v_0-F_2(B).q_0
+      >= kappa(z_0)det(v_0,q_0).
+
+This is (B1). It holds for EVERY frozen z_0. In particular one may choose
+one such z_0 and replace the original functional by the constant-curvature
+area storage (B2).
+
+Conversely, the first variation of (B2) is
+
+  F_1(B).E V + kappa E det(V,U').
+
+Apply (B1) pointwise with X=(V|U') and average. The F_2(B).U' term has
+zero average. This proves domination.
+
+A qualification that must be retained: the original surviving curvature
+kappa(z) need NOT be constant. Precisely, a first-order density is
+dominating if and only if grad c=F_1(B) and each value kappa(z) belongs to
+the set of global coefficients allowed by (B1). Sufficiency follows by
+using the appropriate coefficient pointwise at z=U(y). For example at
+B=0 and F(X)=|X|^2, all |kappa|<=2 are allowed because
+2|det X|<=|X|^2. Taking A_1=0, A_2=-cos(z_1) gives
+kappa(z)=sin(z_1), a nonconstant valid curvature. Rigidity concerns the
+existence class, not uniqueness or constancy of every supplied density.
+
+Explicit periodic y-dependence does not enlarge the EXISTENCE class:
+average P(U(.+s)) over s. Translation invariance of L_B preserves (D), and
+Fubini gives an autonomous density p_bar(j)=E_y p(y,j). Theorem A then
+applies to the averaged density. This does not assert that every original
+y-dependent density itself equals an autonomous density plus a derivative.
+
+COROLLARY C: ALL BACKGROUNDS ARE EQUIVALENT TO POLYCONVEXITY
+
+Suppose F is C1 on all matrices. A dominating smooth finite-order local
+storage exists at EVERY B if and only if F is polyconvex.
+
+For the forward direction select kappa_B from (B1), and put
+
+  ell_B(A,t)=F(B)+(DF(B)-kappa_B cof B):(A-B)
+                        +kappa_B(t-det B),
+  g(A,t)=sup_B ell_B(A,t).
+
+The determinant identity det(B+X)=det B+cof B:X+det X shows
+ell_B(A,det A)<=F(A); the B=A term gives equality for g on the graph.
+The supremum is convex. It is also FINITE everywhere, so no extended-value
+domain issue is hidden: given (A,t), choose X with det X=t-det A, for
+example diag(t-det A,1). Then
+
+  (A,t)=1/2 (A+X,det(A+X)) + 1/2 (A-X,det(A-X)).
+
+Every ell_B is bounded above there by [F(A+X)+F(A-X)]/2. A fixed ell_B
+also gives a finite lower bound. Thus g is a finite convex lift with
+g(A,det A)=F(A).
+
+Conversely, any convex lift finite on the determinant graph is finite on
+its convex hull, which is the whole (A,t) space by the same two-point
+construction. Choose a subgradient (M,kappa) of g at (B,det B).
+Differentiability of F and the determinant expansion, tested with both
+signs of a small displacement, give M+kappa cof B=DF(B).
+The subgradient inequality then yields (B1), and (B2) supplies the storage.

+For a homogeneous quartic with F(A_*)<0, no (B1) is possible at B=0:
+t^4 F(A_*) >= kappa t^2 det A_* fails for sufficiently large positive t.
+Hence NO smooth finite-jet local storage exists even at zero for the
+negative-valued examples in the incoming packet.

+The incoming trace obstruction is sound under its stated arbitrary-width
+strip domination. It does not require the endpoint quasiconvexity theorem.
+For F_DM(A)=|A|^4-(4/sqrt(3))|A|^2 det A, the entry strip
+
+  Phi(x,y)=(x/2)(cos y,sin y),  0<=x<=2,

+has action 103/120-sqrt(3)/2=-delta<0. Its simultaneous x,y reversal is a
+negative return from U_-(y)=(cos y,-sin y) to zero. Both are smooth on
+their closed cylinders. Integer dilation and amplitude N^(-3/4) leave
+these directed actions exactly equal to -delta. Thus any dominating P,
+normalized by P(0)=0, satisfies

+  P(U_N^+)<=-delta,  P(U_N^-)>=delta,
+  U_N^+(y)=N^(-3/4)(cos Ny,sin Ny),
+  U_N^-(y)=N^(-3/4)(cos Ny,-sin Ny).
+
+For definiteness take the periodic Slobodeckij norm W^(s,4)=B^s_(4,4),
+0<s<1, with circular difference h in [-pi,pi]. Up to the fixed norm
+normalization its seminorm to the fourth power is EXACTLY
+
+  16 N^(4s-3) integral_(-N*pi)^(N*pi)
+                 sin^4(t/2)/|t|^(1+4s) dt.                (T1)
+
+The integral is bounded above and below by positive constants depending
+only on s: near zero its integrand is O(|t|^(3-4s)); at infinity it is
+O(|t|^(-1-4s)); a fixed interval away from zero gives the positive lower
+bound. Consequently the seminorm is comparable to N^(s-3/4).
+
+For s<3/4 the sequence tends strongly to zero. At s=3/4 it is bounded and
+has a nonzero seminorm scale, but its L4 norm tends to zero. The critical
+space is reflexive: its difference-quotient embedding is a closed
+subspace of a product of L4 spaces. Every weak subsequential limit is
+zero by the strong L4 convergence. Weak sequential compactness then
+gives weak convergence of the WHOLE sequence to zero. The positive and
+negative bounds separately contradict weak upper and weak lower
+semicontinuity at zero. No claim of strong critical discontinuity follows.

+Using the different Bessel-potential convention H^(3/4,4) without further
+qualification is unnecessary. The incoming notation is correct when
+W^(s,4) has its stated Slobodeckij meaning.

+# FQ integration generator handoff
+
+`build_fq_integration.py` is a standard-library, scratch-only curation generator. It consumes finalized, root-authored data and creates public records using the existing Astra architecture. It never derives a scientific claim from filenames, topics, numerical output, or indexing. No mutation or export has been run against the real repository by this worker.
+
+The exact input template is `CURATION_INPUT.fq.template.json`; optional notice, paired-bridge, gate and scoped-relation shapes are in `OPTIONAL_FQ_RECORD_TEMPLATES.json`. Copy the filled input to `updates/FQ/CURATION_INPUT.json` after freezing the proofs. All `REPLACE_` strings must be replaced.
+
+## Mandatory input
+
+- Top-level: `schema="astra.fq-curation-input.v1"`, `intake_id="FQ"`, full `base_revision`, `date_version`, nonempty `evidence` object and `cards` array. `sources` identifies the selected new files to index. Optional `checkpoint_path` is propagated to every FQ `CLAIMS.json` record; the generator does not create, validate or publish that checkpoint.
+- Each new source: repository-relative `path` under `updates/FQ/`, full original-byte `sha256`, `title`, and actual per-file `read_depth`. Bytes must already exist. Optional `source_id` must be in the `src-FQ-` namespace; otherwise it is deterministically derived from the path. No files are copied and no tree-wide source inventory is inferred.
+- Each named evidence object: `path`, full `sha256`, inclusive one-based `lines=[first,last]`, and `range_scope`. Optional `read_path`, `hash_kind`, `source_id`, `source_revision` and `status` preserve existing public-source conventions. Exact UTF-8 bytes must be recoverable directly or from an explicitly identified HTML `pre` block. A PDF/binary source may be indexed, but cannot substitute for an exact proof text range.
+- Each card: full `id`, `title`, nonempty `topics`, `scientific_scope`, `statement`, nonempty `assumptions`, nonempty `proof_spine`, `costs`, `information_acquisition`, `obstruction`, `comparator`, `missing_lemma`, `next_decisive_step`, `read_review_depth`, and nonempty `proof_refs` (evidence keys). The allowed numeric routes are the reserved N822, N823 and N824, with one full card per route. A card proof must resolve to source metadata. Explicit `UNKNOWN` is valid; empty strings and template placeholders are not.
+- Optional card fields: additional `paragraphs`, `inventory_refs`, `aliases`, `reported_failed_attempts`, `missing_artifacts`, and scoped relation arrays `depends_on`, `supersedes`, `invalidates`, `material_updates`, `contrasting_blockers`. Each supplied relation has `target`, `scope`, `relation_status`, and `ref_ids`. This intake forbids `whole_claim_invalidated=true`.
+
+The source metadata is limited to the files explicitly listed in `sources`. A card's provenance and proof arrays are limited to its selected `proof_refs`; listing forty preserved files does not attach forty proof pointers to every card. Existing proof references can be reused when their exact path/hash resolves to an existing metadata record. Supply `source_id` explicitly if multiple historical metadata IDs match the same path/hash.
+
+## Optional records
+
+- A notice needs `notice_id` in the `SN-FQ-` namespace, full `card_ids`, `issue`, exact `clarification`, and `ref_ids`. It appends a new semantic notice with scoped reciprocal material-update text. Existing older cards/status sidecars remain byte-identical.
+- A paired bridge needs `id` in the `FQ_` namespace, one of the five composition `state` values, full `cards`, `source_interface`, `destination_interface`, `alignment`, `missing_lemma`, `falsifier`, and `ref_ids`. Both interfaces require exactly the eight FO contract fields: `objects`, `regime_and_quantifiers`, `supplied_information`, `acquired_information`, `legal_access`, `guarantee`, `units_norm_and_precision`, `costs`. Optional `reciprocity` supplies explicit `forward` and `reverse` scopes. Incompatible/refuted records append to `rejected_transfers`; other states append to `bridges`. A bridge state preserves the supplied claim; it grants no external scientific validation.
+- An additional gate needs `gate_id` in the `G-FQ-` namespace, full `card_ids`, `title`, `question`, `pass_condition`, and `ref_ids`. Two default open gates per card retain independent review and the supplied next consequential operation. Every generated gate has `status="open"` and `completion_evidence=[]`.
+
+## Generated files and append behavior
+
+New immutable files are raw cards, matching review wrappers, current-status sidecars, source/card HTML pages, paired-bridge sidecars, and FQ `CURATION.json`, `CLAIMS.json`, `INDEXED_SOURCES.json`, `EVIDENCE_REFS.json`, `SCOPED_NOTICES.json`, `BRIDGES.json`, `INTEGRATION_GENERATOR_RECEIPT.json`.
+
+JSONL ledgers retain their exact existing byte prefix: claims, current statuses, source metadata, proof gates, semantic notices and web documents. Catalog/graph/web-catalog/bridge-registry arrays retain every existing record in order and append selected records only. Existing aliases are unchanged. JSON containers may be reformatted, but no historical record value is changed. Graph additions are provenance edges only; paired bridge semantics remain in the existing bridge registry.
+
+Every new claim is `source_derived_unreviewed`; correctness, novelty, formal/empirical confirmation and physical capability remain `UNKNOWN` in generated validation metadata. The input must accurately state actual internal work in its per-file/card reading and proof fields. Historical checkpoint failures and prior receipts are neither modified nor reinterpreted.
+
+## Root commands after freeze
+
+First run a read-only plan, optionally saving the full plan outside the repository:
+
+```text
+python3 /Users/harjas/Documents/ChatGPT/ultra/research/2026-10-15-capital-mining-v1/workers/integration_builder/build_fq_integration.py --repo /Users/harjas/Documents/ChatGPT/ultra/work/astra-capital-compensation-exchange --input /Users/harjas/Documents/ChatGPT/ultra/work/astra-capital-compensation-exchange/updates/FQ/CURATION_INPUT.json --dry-run --report /Users/harjas/Documents/ChatGPT/ultra/research/2026-10-15-capital-mining-v1/workers/integration_builder/FQ_FINAL_DRY_RUN.json
+```
+
+The plan reports the finalized input SHA256. After the root authorizes that exact input, use the same command with `--apply --expect-input-sha256 <that-full-sha256>`. Apply refuses unless current HEAD and freshly read `origin/main` both equal `base_revision`; this forces a fresh remote-collision/reconciliation check before real authority is appended. It uses a transient Git lock and preflights every read registry/source byte before any write. An identical rerun produces zero changes. A changed immutable output or conflicting existing identifier fails closed.
+
+Then the root runs the existing public projection:
+
+```text
+python3 frontier/build_access.py build --base-revision <full-base-revision>
+python3 frontier/build_access.py check --base-revision <full-base-revision>
+```
+
+The generator deliberately does not run these commands, commit, push, merge, publish a checkpoint, rebuild private SQLite views, or create technology records. It does not modify inherited legacy topic inventories; current generated concept/dossier/connection/proof/gate routes and the navigation manifest are refreshed by `build_access.py`. Legacy topic inventories already omit FO cards on this baseline; expanding that older architecture is outside this minimal tooling task.
+
+## Verification and current limitations
+
+`test_fq_disposable_fixture.py` tests software safeguards entirely in a temporary directory and imports the real current `frontier/build_access.py` only for a fixture projection. `FQ_FIXTURE_TEST_RECEIPT.json` records thirteen passing checks: no-write planning, apply, identical rerun, actual public projection acceptance, open gates, checkpoint-pointer propagation, explicit FQ namespace assertions, immutable collision, source-hash mismatch, invalid line range, numeric-route collision, concurrent source change and conflicting ledger identifier.
+
+No finalized root curation input has been consumed. The final real dry run and public checks remain root work after freezing the selected evidence. Remote main drift or an N822–N824 collision requires reconciliation before apply; the script intentionally does not guess replacement scientific IDs. Existing global checkpoint-schema failures remain outside this generator and must be preserved and reported separately.
+
+## Namespace correction
+
+The root final overlap audit reported that active PR85 already owns `updates/FP` and `src-FP`, although remote main does not yet contain that directory. This derivative therefore uses the fresh FQ intake/source/notice/gate/bridge/checkpoint namespace. N822, N823 and N824 and all scientific content remain unchanged. Original FP tooling is frozen and retained alongside this derivative; see `FQ_NAMESPACE_DERIVATION_RECEIPT.json` for hashes and provenance. No repository content was renamed or mutated by this worker.

+New immutable files are raw cards, matching review wrappers, current-status sidecars, source/card HTML pages, paired-bridge sidecars, and FP `CURATION.json`, `CLAIMS.json`, `INDEXED_SOURCES.json`, `EVIDENCE_REFS.json`, `SCOPED_NOTICES.json`, `BRIDGES.json`, `INTEGRATION_GENERATOR_RECEIPT.json`.
+
+JSONL ledgers retain their exact existing byte prefix: claims, current statuses, source metadata, proof gates, semantic notices and web documents. Catalog/graph/web-catalog/bridge-registry arrays retain every existing record in order and append selected records only. Existing aliases are unchanged. JSON containers may be reformatted, but no historical record value is changed. Graph additions are provenance edges only; paired bridge semantics remain in the existing bridge registry.
+
+Every new claim is `source_derived_unreviewed`; correctness, novelty, formal/empirical confirmation and physical capability remain `UNKNOWN` in generated validation metadata. The input must accurately state actual internal work in its per-file/card reading and proof fields. Historical checkpoint failures and prior receipts are neither modified nor reinterpreted.
+
+## Root commands after freeze
+
+First run a read-only plan, optionally saving the full plan outside the repository:
+
+```text
+python3 /Users/harjas/Documents/ChatGPT/ultra/research/2026-10-15-capital-mining-v1/workers/integration_builder/build_fp_integration.py --repo /Users/harjas/Documents/ChatGPT/ultra/work/astra-capital-compensation-exchange --input /Users/harjas/Documents/ChatGPT/ultra/work/astra-capital-compensation-exchange/updates/FP/CURATION_INPUT.json --dry-run --report /Users/harjas/Documents/ChatGPT/ultra/research/2026-10-15-capital-mining-v1/workers/integration_builder/FINAL_DRY_RUN.json
+```
+
+The plan reports the finalized input SHA256. After the root authorizes that exact input, use the same command with `--apply --expect-input-sha256 <that-full-sha256>`. Apply refuses unless current HEAD and freshly read `origin/main` both equal `base_revision`; this forces a fresh remote-collision/reconciliation check before real authority is appended. It uses a transient Git lock and preflights every read registry/source byte before any write. An identical rerun produces zero changes. A changed immutable output or conflicting existing identifier fails closed.
+
+Then the root runs the existing public projection:
+
+```text
+python3 frontier/build_access.py build --base-revision <full-base-revision>
+python3 frontier/build_access.py check --base-revision <full-base-revision>
+```
+
+The generator deliberately does not run these commands, commit, push, merge, publish a checkpoint, rebuild private SQLite views, or create technology records. It does not modify inherited legacy topic inventories; current generated concept/dossier/connection/proof/gate routes and the navigation manifest are refreshed by `build_access.py`. Legacy topic inventories already omit FO cards on this baseline; expanding that older architecture is outside this minimal tooling task.
+
+## Verification and current limitations
+
+`test_disposable_fixture.py` tests software safeguards entirely in a temporary directory and imports the real current `frontier/build_access.py` only for a fixture projection. `FIXTURE_TEST_RECEIPT.json` records twelve passing checks: no-write planning, apply, identical rerun, actual public projection acceptance, open gates, checkpoint-pointer propagation, immutable collision, source-hash mismatch, invalid line range, numeric-route collision, concurrent source change and conflicting ledger identifier.
+
+No finalized root curation input has been consumed. The final real dry run and public checks remain root work after freezing the selected evidence. Remote main drift or an N822–N824 collision requires reconciliation before apply; the script intentionally does not guess replacement scientific IDs. Existing global checkpoint-schema failures remain outside this generator and must be preserved and reported separately.
