+# Exact oriented free-time actions for the convex complex-tilt family
+
+Date: 15 October 2026. Supplement to NO_LINEAR_SELECTOR.md.
+
+## Result and scope
+
+For real t and rho>0, consider the convex, left-SO(2)-invariant quartic
+
+    C_(t,rho)(X|Y)=|X+(t+i rho)Y|^4.
+
+Let k be any integer and a any complex number. Minimize the action on a strip of width T>0 joining zero to the profile U(y)=a exp(iky), allowing arbitrary smooth multi-frequency strip interiors. Define lambda=rho k and
+
+    I_(lambda,T)=integral_0^T exp((4lambda/3)(T-s)) ds
+      =3(exp(4lambda T/3)-1)/(4lambda),  lambda !=0,
+      =T,                                      lambda =0.
+
+Then the exact fixed-width minimum is
+
+    Incoming_T(0,U)=|a|^4 I_(lambda,T)^(-3).             (1)
+
+The exact return minimum, with the same arbitrary-interior allowance, is
+
+    Return_T(U,0)=exp(4lambda T)|a|^4 I_(lambda,T)^(-3). (2)
+
+Taking the infimum over all positive widths gives
+
+    Incoming(0,U)=(64/27)rho^3(-k)_+^3 |a|^4,
+    Return(U,0)  =(64/27)rho^3( k)_+^3 |a|^4.           (3)
+
+The shear t changes only an optimal phase, not the value. For nonzero a, every fixed-width minimum is attained by a smooth strip. None of the free-width infima in (3) is attained at a finite width: all are limits as T tends to infinity. The trivial profile a=0 has zero action attained at any width.
+
+This is an exact convex-family value calculation, including all compatible interior frequencies. It is not a quasiconvexity advance for negative-valued energies, a solution of the universal left-invariant problem, or a historical novelty claim. Originality remains UNKNOWN.
+
+## 1. Averaging eliminates all interior frequencies except k
+
+Let Phi(x,y) be any smooth competitor with the stated boundary profiles. For theta in the transverse circle, set
+
+    (G_theta Phi)(x,y)=exp(-ik theta) Phi(x,y+theta).
+
+Both boundary profiles are fixed by G_theta. The complex multiplier is a constant output rotation, and the shift is a transverse translation. Therefore C_(t,rho) has the same action on every G_theta Phi.
+
+Average these competitors:
+
+    Psi(x,y)=(1/(2pi))integral_0^(2pi) G_theta Phi(x,y) dtheta
+            =r(x)exp(iky).
+
+Convexity of C_(t,rho), applied pointwise to the gradient and then integrated, gives action(Psi)<=action(Phi). Thus restricting to this single transverse mode does not change the global fixed-width infimum. The reverse inequality holds because single-mode strips are admissible competitors.
+
+This is an energy-decreasing symmetry projection justified by convexity. The same argument cannot be imported for a general rank-one-convex nonconvex quartic.
+
+## 2. Phase gauge and exact Holder bound
+
+For Psi=r(x)exp(iky), the complex quantity inside the fourth power is
+
+    (r'+ikt r-rho k r)exp(iky).
+
+Write r(x)=exp(-ikt x)z(x). The action becomes
+
+    integral_0^T |z'-lambda z|^4 dx,
+    z(0)=0, z(T)=exp(ikt T)a
+
+for an incoming path. Put v=z'-lambda z and A=exp(ikt T)a. The endpoint equation is
+
+    A=integral_0^T exp(lambda(T-s))v(s) ds.
+
+Holder's inequality with exponents 4 and 4/3 gives
+
+    |A| <= (integral_0^T |v|^4 ds)^(1/4)
+             I_(lambda,T)^(3/4).
+
+Therefore the action is at least |a|^4 I_(lambda,T)^(-3).
+
+Equality is achieved by the explicit smooth control
+
+    v(s)=A exp(lambda(T-s)/3)/I_(lambda,T).              (4)
+
+Indeed its endpoint integral equals A and its fourth-power integral equals |A|^4 I^(-3). Solving z'=lambda z+v with z(0)=0 produces a smooth minimizer with exactly the prescribed endpoint. This proves (1).
+
+For a return path z(0)=a and z(T)=0, the endpoint equation instead requires
+
+    integral_0^T exp(lambda(T-s))v(s) ds=-exp(lambda T)a.
+
+The same Holder bound and equality control give (2).
+
+## 3. Free-width limits and attainment
+
+If lambda>0, I increases without bound, so the incoming infimum is zero. For the return value,
+
+    exp(4lambda T) I^(-3)
+      =(4lambda/3)^3(1-exp(-4lambda T/3))^(-3),
+
+which decreases strictly to (4lambda/3)^3.
+
+If lambda<0, I increases strictly to 3/(4|lambda|), so the incoming value decreases strictly to (4|lambda|/3)^3. The return value tends to zero.
+
+If lambda=0, both values are |a|^4/T^3 and tend to zero.
+
+For nonzero a the relevant fixed-width formulas are strictly above their limiting values at every finite T. This proves the nonattainment assertion and (3). The formal controls on an infinite strip explain the limits, but finite-strip limiting sequences suffice for the proof.
+
+## 4. An actual nonlocal nonlinear model, and its limitation
+
+For this convex family define the required supply on an arbitrary smooth profile U by the infimum of incoming actions over all finite widths and compatible strips from zero to U. Pointwise nonnegativity gives a lower bound zero. A unit-width straight strip gives a finite upper bound. Thus the value is finite without invoking quasiconvexity.
+
+Concatenating an almost minimizing incoming strip with any prescribed transition proves that this value is a dominating profile functional. Piecewise smooth concatenations can be smoothed near their joins while keeping the outer traces fixed and approximating the quartic action in W^(1,4). This is the established required-supply construction; its existence here is independently secured by pointwise nonnegativity.
+
+Equation (3) computes its value on every individual circular Fourier mode even though its definition allows arbitrary-frequency interiors. It has quartic amplitude scaling, cubic frequency scaling, orientation sensitivity and cubic dependence on the ellipticity parameter rho.
+
+This is a useful exact model for a genuinely nonlocal, nonlinearly coefficient-dependent construction. It does not solve the hard part of extending it to negative-valued rank-one-convex energies: there the required-supply lower bound is not automatic. The supplement is not offered as a renamed no-negative-cycle solution.
+
+Any normalized dominating functional for C_(t,rho) must lie between negative return cost and incoming cost. Therefore on a mode,
+
+    -(64/27)rho^3(k)_+^3|a|^4
+       <= P_C(a exp(iky))
+       <= (64/27)rho^3(-k)_+^3|a|^4.                    (5)
+
+Both sides are the sharp extremal-storage bounds: incoming required supply dominates, and negative return cost also dominates by concatenation. They give an exact calibration test for nonlinear proposals.
+
+## Verification and provenance
+
+The proof is analytic, based on convex group averaging, a scalar linear ODE and Holder equality. The accompanying verify_no_linear_selector.py additionally checks the finite-T equality-control integrals and free-width constants by exact symbolic calculation. +# Electrodynamic and structural derivations
+
+15 October 2026. Independent internal audit, not external validation. Historical originality UNKNOWN. These are conditional results with explicitly specified optical and structural models. No laboratory response, hot material parameters, useful transformation, or industrial advantage was acquired.
+
+## 1. What the source pressure actually assumes
+
+Let true inversion-related variants have bulk response `chi_s^(2)=s chi_0^(2)`, `s=±1`, in the same laboratory axes. This relation must be checked for the actual APB; the name “antiphase domain” alone does not establish it. The linear responses can agree while the third-rank response changes sign. Let a scalar contraction of that tensor be real, local, instantaneous and weak enough for perturbation theory. At a prescribed electric field the nonlinear contribution to the effective material potential is
+
+\[
+f_s(E)=-\epsilon_0s\chi_{\rm eff}^{(2)}E^3/3.
+\]
+
+This is a fixed-field effective potential, not the complete stored electromagnetic/material energy of a driven dispersive system. With peak fields `E1,E2`,
+
+\[
+E(t)=E_1\cos\omega t+E_2\cos(2\omega t+\phi),\qquad
+\overline{E^3}=\tfrac34E_1^2E_2\cos\phi,
+\]
+
+so
+
+\[
+f_s=-s h\cos\phi,\quad h=\epsilon_0\chi_{\rm eff}^{(2)}E_1^2E_2/4,
+\quad p_0=2h.
+\]
+
+Positive pressure is defined to expand `s=+1`. The source's prefactor is consistent with these assumptions; this audit does **not** identify an algebraic error in it. An absorption/injection coefficient alone does not supply this conservative potential. Nor does an arbitrarily chosen real room-temperature SHG coefficient certify a hot, carrier-loaded, moving-wall force.
+
+For dispersive transparent normal modes the safe reduced model is a calibrated Hermitian interaction
+
+\[
+H_{\rm int}=\hbar[g(X)b^\dagger a^2+g(X)^*b(a^\dagger)^2],\qquad
+F_X=-2\hbar\operatorname{Re}[g'(X)\beta^*\alpha^2].
+\]
+
+The modes must be normalized by their full dispersive field-plus-material energy, with their actual hot optical boundary conditions. The force is a partial derivative at fixed canonical optical state; it is not the total derivative of the energy after replacing the amplitudes by arbitrary steady-state functions of `X`. Driving, damping and changes of the optical state must then be evolved separately. If linear mode frequencies also depend on wall position, the ordinary term `-hbar sum_j omega_j'(X) Nj` and any dissipative-coordinate forces must be included; equality of the ideal bulk variants' linear response does not remove an APB's own localized response. Quesada–Sipe's nonlinear quantization analysis is a relevant warning about canonical variables, not a proof that this fixed-field source formula is wrong. [Primary paper](https://opg.optica.org/ol/abstract.cfm?uri=ol-42-17-3443).
+
+## 2. Exact wall-overlap pressure and thickness cancellation
+
+Assume prescribed, undepleted forward fields. Absorb the real tensor contraction and amplitude product into `h(r)≥0`; write the relative phase as `Phi+q·r`, with `q=2k_omega-k_2omega` (changing this convention only reverses phase signs). The interaction is
+
+\[
+U[s]=-\int s(\mathbf r)h(\mathbf r)
+       \cos(\Phi+\mathbf q\!\cdot\!\mathbf r)\,dV.
+\]
+
+For a wall whose positive-variant side expands with normal displacement `delta X`, its virtual-work pressure is
+
+\[
+p(\mathbf r)=2h(\mathbf r)\cos(\Phi+\mathbf q\!\cdot\!\mathbf r).
+\]
+
+The generalized force on **rigid translation of the entire wall** is the surface integral of this pressure. For a rectangular uniform wall of tangent lengths `L1,L2` and normal position `X`,
+
+\[
+\frac{F_X}{A}=p_0\prod_{j=1}^2
+\operatorname{sinc}(q_{tj}L_j/2)
+\cos(\Phi+q_nX+\mathbf q_t\!\cdot\!\mathbf r_c),
+\quad \operatorname{sinc}x=\sin x/x.
+\]
+
+**Consequences.** A tangent direction spanning an integer beat length `2pi/|q_t|` has exactly zero net force in this uniform lossless model, for every externally set phase. An infinite flat wall has zero mean pressure if there is any nonzero tangent mismatch. A finite thin wall can survive this restriction. Net-force cancellation does not imply every patch of a flexible wall is stationary: opposite local pressures can bow it or write different polarities at different depths.
+
+In a film, if the wall spans `0<z<d`, the two internal intensity attenuation coefficients are `alpha1,alpha2`, and no reflections or depletion occur, the normalized overlap is
+
+\[
+W(d)=\frac1d\int_0^d e^{-az+iq_zz}dz
+=\frac{1-e^{-(a-iq_z)d}}{d(a-iq_z)},\qquad
+a=\alpha_1+\alpha_2/2,
+\]
+
+\[
+\bar p=p_0\operatorname{Re}[e^{i\Phi}W(d)],\qquad
+|\bar p|\le p_0|W(d)|\le p_0\frac{1-e^{-ad}}{ad}\le p_0.
+\]
+
+At `a=0`, `W=exp(i q_z d/2) sinc(q_z d/2)`. At nonzero attenuation the exact sinc zeros generally lift; that does not restore a uniformly driven thick volume. Standing waves, multiple reflections, changing tensor projections and pump depletion require their measured complex overlap instead of this forward-wave formula.
+
+Using **only** Skauli et al.'s original 22 °C dispersion fit, the fundamental/SH pair 2.3/1.15 µm has `Lc=pi/|q|≈5.01 µm`, while 4.6/2.3 µm has `Lc≈40.97 µm`. The corresponding uniform 400 nm overlap magnitudes are 0.99738 and 0.99996. Therefore this propagation theorem is **not** a demonstrated cancellation of the proposed 400 nm film. The fit's temperature measurements extend only to 95 °C; no 650 °C refractive index is extrapolated here. [Original author-uploaded paper, Eq.13/Table II](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/241151797_Improved_dispersion_relations_for_GaAs_and_applications_to_nonlinear_optics).
+
+For common external propagation directions on a planar film, tangential wavevector conservation can make the in-plane components of `q` zero even when the internal normal components differ. A lateral wall can then see position-independent average pressure while the phase varies through its thickness. The theorem must be applied using the wall orientation, not simply the optical path length.
+
+## 3. Fixed-phase drift obstruction and a conditional moving-phase alternative
+
+If mismatch projects onto the direction of wall motion, `q_n!=0`, and the tangent overlap remains fixed, write
+
+\[
+p(X)=P\cos(q_nX+\Phi),\qquad
+U(X)/A=-P\sin(q_nX+\Phi)/q_n.
+\]
+
+Then
+
+\[
+\int_X^{X+2\pi/|q_n|}p(x)dx=0.
+\]
+
+A static optical phase thus creates a periodic potential, not an indefinitely directed bulk pressure. Under deterministic isothermal gradient motion `Xdot=M p(X)`, with positive mobility and no other force, the wall approaches a stable zero of the force rather than traversing repeated cells. Thermal detailed balance in this static periodic potential likewise gives no stationary directed current. Depletion, spatial temperature variation, nonthermal carriers, radiation recoil or moving phases can escape this narrow result and must be accounted for as different driven mechanisms.
+
+A useful mechanism mutation is to translate the phase pattern: `Phi(t)=-q_n v t`. With `eta=q_n(X-vt)`,
+
+\[
+\dot\eta=q_n[MP\cos\eta-v].
+\]
+
+For positive `q_n`, a stable locked solution exists if `|v|<MP`; choose the root with `sin eta>0`. It advances a **freely moving** wall at the programmed speed. The input sources supply power `F v` and all loss. The experiment would compare positive/negative phase-ramp velocity and zero-ramp controls, with independently measured optical overlap and temperature/carriers. This is a conditional optical conveyor interpretation; moving optical potentials are established physics and historical originality of this APB application is UNKNOWN. It removes the static-phase travel restriction, not pinning, absorption, tensor zeros, duty-cycle limits or retention obligations. It is unnecessary when `q_n=0` and a uniform pressure is already available.
+
+For an ideal thick one-dimensional system with `f=-h s(z) cos(qz)`, minimizing local optical energy instead favors `s(z)=sign cos(qz)`. Over an integer number of periods this pattern gains `2h/pi` energy per volume but introduces `|q|/pi` walls per length. With constant wall energy `gamma`, it beats a uniform variant only when
+
+\[
+p_0=2h>\gamma |q|.
+\]
+
+Hence domain inversion used to quasi-phase-match the optical coupling is not an independent free resource while those same domains are being removed. A static mismatched field can favor a periodic polarity pattern rather than a uniform selected bulk polarity. This comparison assumes sharp freely creatable walls, fixed field and isotropic wall energy; it is not a hot-GaAs nucleation prediction.
+
+## 4. SHG backaction, no-seed symmetry and energy balance
+
+For the closed resonant three-wave interaction,
+
+\[
+\dot\alpha=-i2g^*\alpha^*\beta,\qquad
+\dot\beta=-ig\alpha^2.
+\]
+
+Set `Z=g beta* alpha^2`. Direct calculation yields
+
+\[
+\dot N_a=-4\operatorname{Im}Z,\qquad
+\dot N_b=2\operatorname{Im}Z,\qquad
+\frac d{dt}(N_a+2N_b)=0.
+\]
+
+Conservative force samples a real quadrature; frequency conversion samples an imaginary quadrature. Zero **instantaneous** conversion is therefore compatible with nonzero force. It does not provide sustained uncharged work: amplitudes/phases or coupling energy change, and a driven steady state must supply mechanical work and dissipation. For a stationary apparatus a complete energy boundary is
+
+\[
+\frac d{dt}(U_{\rm optical+material}+E_{\rm mechanical})
+=P_{\rm drive}-P_{\rm outgoing}-P_{\rm absorbed}.
+\]
+
+For a closed cycle returning both mechanics and all optical/material states, net delivered work is bounded by supplied work minus losses. There is no new energy source.
+
+For a cavity with an undepleted fundamental and **no independent SH seed**,
+
+\[
+\beta=-ig\alpha^2/(K-i\Delta_2),\qquad K=\kappa_2/2.
+\]
+
+For real `g,g'`,
+
+\[
+F_X^{\rm self}=-\frac{\hbar|\alpha|^4\Delta_2}
+{K^2+\Delta_2^2}\,\partial_X|g|^2.
+\]
+
+This force is zero on SH resonance in this real-overlap limit and is invariant under global inversion `g,g' -> -g,-g'`. More generally the full unseeded equations are covariant under `g -> -g, beta -> -beta`, leaving the force unchanged even with pump depletion. Complex overlaps can carry recoil forces, but the same global parity remains. A target crystal's **own** generated harmonic cannot by itself supply an independently chosen polarity reference. A separately phase-locked injected SH field can do so; its cross term is odd under seed phase reversal while the self-generated contribution is even. This is a design restriction, not a falsifier of the source, which explicitly supplies both colors.
+
+## 5. Same-temperature spectral compatibility
+
+Panish–Casey's published absorption measurements cover GaAs from 300 to 973 K and give
+
+\[
+E_g(T)=1.522-5.8\times10^{-4}T^2/(T+300)\quad{\rm eV}.
+\]
+
+At `T=923.15 K` (650 °C), `Eg≈1.11790 eV`. This is within their measured range, though it is an old bulk fit rather than a calibrated capped-film gap. The publisher-deposited abstract was fetched through Crossref; the full paper could not be fetched. [Primary DOI](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.1657024).
+
+Let `epsilon=hc/lambda_omega`. For a two-color actuator the relevant electronic thresholds include:
+
+| Channel | Minimum final photon energy | To be below the direct-gap threshold at 650 °C |
+|---|---:|---:|
+| SH linear absorption; fundamental 2PA | `2 epsilon` | `lambda_omega > 2.218 µm` |
+| Mixed-color 2PA; fundamental 3PA | `3 epsilon` | `lambda_omega > 3.327 µm` |
+| SH 2PA | `4 epsilon` | `lambda_omega > 4.436 µm` |
+| SH 3PA | `6 epsilon` | `lambda_omega > 6.655 µm` |
+
+These are **kinematic channel screens**, not absorption coefficients, selection-rule proofs or measured hot attenuation. Being below threshold does not remove defect, free-carrier, phonon-assisted or higher-order absorption. Being above it does not give a rate without matrix elements and material populations.
+
+The room-temperature 1.8/0.9 µm cavity precedent's SH crosses this fitted gap around 151.6 °C, so its cold “below-gap SH” premise cannot be used at 650 °C. For 2.3/1.15 µm, the SH is only about 39.8 meV below the fitted hot gap, while mixed-color 2PA and SH 2PA remain energetically open. Considering only the fundamental's room-temperature 3PA coefficient leaves those lower-order two-beam channels unqualified. Experimental nondegenerate 2PA in GaAs is established independently; its hot coefficients are not imported from a different diode or quantum well. [Cold cavity paper](https://doi.org/10.1021/ph500054u), [primary GaAs nondegenerate 2PA experiment](https://photonics.umd.edu/pubs/ja-30/).
+
+## 6. Root topology, capillarity and why surface disappearance can mislead
+
+Suppose a film-spanning wall has fixed substrate root `X(0)=0`, free top at `z=d`, isotropic positive wall tension `gamma`, uniform pressure `p`, and no interface registry change. Its energy per transverse length is
+
+\[
+\mathcal E[X]=\gamma\int_0^d\sqrt{1+X'(z)^2}\,dz
+-p\int_0^d X(z)\,dz.
+\]
+
+The Euler–Lagrange equation and natural free-top condition give
+
+\[
+\frac{X'}{\sqrt{1+X'^2}}=\frac p\gamma(d-z),\quad X'(d)=0.
+\]
+
+For `r=|p|d/gamma<1`,
+
+\[
+X(d)=\frac\gamma p[1-\sqrt{1-(pd/\gamma)^2}]
+=\frac{pd^2/\gamma}{1+\sqrt{1-r^2}}
+\simeq\frac{pd^2}{2\gamma}.
+\]
+
+The last rationalized form is numerically stable. The root remains present regardless of apparent surface progress. At `|p|d/gamma>=1` this graph-equilibrium solution fails; that failure alone neither proves depinning nor authorizes an interface reconstruction. A rooted APB cannot be erased through the whole film while its root boundary condition is held fixed. Contact-line motion, root release or an annihilation path is an additional structural process.
+
+Rubel–Baranovskii's relaxed static DFT result `gamma_{110}=28 meV/Å²≈0.44861 J/m²` supplies a **normalization**, not a measured 650 °C wall tension/stiffness. With it, source pressure 442.7 Pa in a 400 nm film gives only 0.07895 nm of free-top bow; the source's largest example 11.95 kPa gives 2.132 nm. An anisotropic wall uses its orientation stiffness, which must be measured in the operating regime. [Primary paper, Table 1](https://www.mdpi.com/1422-0067/10/12/5104).
+
+For a cylindrical selected-polarity island spanning a film, curvature competes as
+
+\[
+\mathcal E(R)=2\pi R d\gamma-\pi R^2d p,\qquad
+\dot R=M(p-\gamma/R).
+\]
+
+Phase reversal cannot reverse the direction of radius drift if `|p|<gamma/R`; both phases still shrink the island. The same static DFT normalization and middle source pressure give `Rc=gamma/p≈1.013 mm`, far above a micrometer island. This is not an acquired hot critical radius; the exact same-regime falsifier is the **measured** inequality `p_max R < gamma_hot` in this model. A flat unrooted wall avoids this capillary threshold but still needs acquired mobility/pinning and retained exit behavior.
+
+## 7. Coupled loss, carriers, timing and a constrained beam ratio
+
+At a fixed measured state, the phase-even channel contributions can be organized as
+
+\[
+q_{\rm even}=a_1 I_1+a_2 I_2+b_{11}I_1^2+b_{12}I_1I_2+b_{22}I_2^2
++\sum c_{ijk}I_1^iI_2^j+q_{\rm FCA}.
+\]
+
+The full loss can additionally contain coherent interference terms such as `q_Phi=2 Re[D E2* E1²]`, plus propagation-mediated changes of absorption. Those signed terms must be combined with their underlying pathways so the total passive absorption remains nonnegative; they must not be assigned independent favorable values. Coefficients depend on temperature, carrier populations, optical polarization, spectrum, defect state and the boundary. Carrier generation must be computed channel by channel using the corresponding absorbed photon energy, rather than equating a carrier percentage with a lattice-heat percentage. Temperature, carriers, detuning, optical overlap and wall kinetics must all evolve together.
+
+Even in a linear-loss-only comparison at a fixed state, equal beams are not generally optimal. Since `p=A I1 sqrt(I2)`, maximizing pressure for prescribed `a1 I1+a2 I2=Q` gives
+
+\[
+a_1 I_1=2a_2 I_2,\qquad I_2/I_1=a_1/(2a_2).
+\]
+
+The optimal split depends on measured losses; it does not allow assigning each beam a favorable coefficient. Nonlinear or mixed absorption changes the optimum and the carrier/thermal state changes with the split.
+
+For time-varying illumination in the simplest overdamped wall law,
+
+\[
+\Delta X=\int M[T(t),n(t),X(t),\ldots],p(t)\,dt.
+\]
+
+Only constant mobility and temperature permit replacing this by `M D p_peak t`. The source's 100 fs/1 MHz duty penalty is correct in that specified linear regime. Pulsed thermal activation can alter the weighting but must be measured in the same specimen.
+
+If phase jitter is independent and Gaussian with variance `sigma_Phi²`, the mean conservative drive is reduced by `exp(-sigma_Phi²/2)`. Group-velocity walkoff changes the pulse product itself: for field-amplitude Gaussian widths `tau1,tau2`, the normalized time overlap at differential delay `delta` is `exp[-delta²/(tau1²+2 tau2²)]`. Optical phase lock, pulse overlap and hot phase matching are separate obligations.
+
+All calculations in `calculate.py` verify these explicit identities/normalizations only. They do not close N821's physical acquisition gates.

+## The reconstructed operation

+The source proposes an externally phase-locked `omega/2omega` drive acting on verified inversion-related GaAs variants, followed by signed APB movement and a useful polarity pattern retained after light and annealing cease. In its local transparent scalar limit,

+\[
+f_s=-s\frac{\epsilon_0\chi_{\rm eff}^{(2)}}4E_1^2E_2\cos\Phi,

+## 1. Spatial averaging turns the scalar pressure into a wall-overlap law
+
+For a rectangular rigid wall, tangent dimensions `L1,L2`, normal position `X`, and relative wavevector `q`,
+
+\[
+F_X/A=p_0\prod_j\operatorname{sinc}(q_{tj}L_j/2)
+\cos(\Phi+q_nX+\mathbf q_t\!\cdot\!\mathbf r_c).
+\]
+
+An integer beat length along a uniform lossless tangent dimension cancels the net force **at every phase**. If mismatch lies along the travel direction, fixed phase instead produces a periodic potential with exactly zero work per beat. Static isothermal gradient motion approaches a potential minimum; it does not supply indefinitely directed pressure.

In fact, the cold 22 °C dispersion example gives overlap magnitude 0.99738 across 400 nm at 2.3/1.15 µm and 0.99996 at 4.6/2.3 µm. +def gap_panish_casey(T: float) -> float:
+    """GaAs direct gap; published absorption data cover 300 <= T <= 973 K."""
+    if not 300.0 <= T <= 973.0:
+        raise ValueError("Panish-Casey measured temperature range exceeded")
+    return 1.522 - 5.8e-4 * T * T / (T + 300.0)
+
+
+def index_skauli_22C(wavelength_um: float) -> float:
+    """Original paper Eq.13/Table II, at 22 C ONLY; 0.97--17 um."""
+    if not 0.97 <= wavelength_um <= 17.0:
+        raise ValueError("Skauli wavelength range exceeded")
+    poles = (0.4431307, 0.8746453, 36.9166)
+    strengths = (27.83972, 0.031764, 0.00143636)
+    inv_l2 = 1.0 / wavelength_um**2
+    n2 = 5.372514 + sum(g / (1.0 / pole**2 - inv_l2)
+                              for pole, g in zip(poles, strengths))
+    return math.sqrt(n2)
+
+
+def sinc(x: float) -> float:
+    return 1.0 if x == 0.0 else math.sin(x) / x
+
+
+def overlap(q: float, d: float, attenuation: float = 0.0) -> complex:
+    r = complex(-attenuation, q) * d
+    return 1.0 + 0j if abs(r) < 1e-12 else (cmath.exp(r) - 1.0) / r
+
+
+def simpson(f, lo: float, hi: float, n: int = 4000):
+    assert n % 2 == 0
+    h = (hi - lo) / n
+    result = f(lo) + f(hi)
+    result += 4 * sum(f(lo + i * h) for i in range(1, n, 2))
+    result += 2 * sum(f(lo + i * h) for i in range(2, n, 2))
+    return result * h / 3
+
+
+def check_analytic_identities() -> dict:
+    checks = {}
+    # Independent cycle integration checks the cubic prefactor.
+    e1, e2, phase = 1.7, 0.8, 0.46
+    avg_cubic = simpson(lambda t: (e1 * math.cos(t) +
+                         e2 * math.cos(2 * t + phase))**3,
+                         0, 2 * math.pi) / (2 * math.pi)
+    cubic_exact = 0.75 * e1**2 * e2 * math.cos(phase)
+    assert abs(avg_cubic - cubic_exact) < 1e-12
+    checks["cycle_average_E_cubed_abs_error"] = abs(avg_cubic-cubic_exact)
+
+    rng = random.Random(821)
+    overlap_err = 0.0
+    invariant_err = 0.0
+    parity_err = 0.0
+    for _ in range(30):
+        qd = rng.uniform(-12, 12)
+        ad = rng.uniform(0, 4)
+        direct = simpson(lambda z: cmath.exp(complex(-ad, qd) * z), 0, 1)
+        overlap_err = max(overlap_err, abs(direct - overlap(qd, 1, ad)))
+        a = complex(rng.uniform(-2, 2), rng.uniform(-2, 2))
+        b = complex(rng.uniform(-2, 2), rng.uniform(-2, 2))
+        g = complex(rng.uniform(-1, 1), rng.uniform(-1, 1))
+        gp = complex(rng.uniform(-1, 1), rng.uniform(-1, 1))
+        adot = -2j * g.conjugate() * a.conjugate() * b
+        bdot = -1j * g * a**2
+        dna = 2 * (a.conjugate() * adot).real
+        dnb = 2 * (b.conjugate() * bdot).real
+        invariant_err = max(invariant_err, abs(dna + 2 * dnb))
+        K, delta = 0.4, 0.6
+        bself = -1j * g * a**2 / complex(K, -delta)
+        bself_inv = -1j * (-g) * a**2 / complex(K, -delta)
+        force = -2 * (gp * bself.conjugate() * a**2).real
+        force_inv = -2 * ((-gp) * bself_inv.conjugate() * a**2).real
+        parity_err = max(parity_err, abs(force-force_inv))
+    assert overlap_err < 1e-10
+    assert invariant_err < 1e-12
+    assert parity_err < 1e-12
+    checks["complex_overlap_quadrature_max_abs_error"] = overlap_err
+    checks["Manley_Rowe_max_abs_residual"] = invariant_err
+    checks["unseeded_global_inversion_force_max_abs_residual"] = parity_err
+
+    q, p0, phi, x = 2.3, 1.7, 0.9, 0.43
+    dx = 1e-5
+    potential = lambda z: -p0 * math.sin(q*z + phi) / q
+    fd_force = -(potential(x+dx)-potential(x-dx))/(2*dx)
+    assert abs(fd_force-p0*math.cos(q*x+phi)) < 1e-9
+    cycle_work = simpson(lambda z: p0*math.cos(q*z+phi), 0, 2*math.pi/q)
+    assert abs(cycle_work) < 1e-12
+    checks["force_potential_finite_difference_abs_error"] = abs(fd_force-p0*math.cos(q*x+phi))
+    checks["static_pressure_work_per_beat_abs_residual"] = abs(cycle_work)
+
+    # Elastica equation and free-tip condition tested without a small-slope approximation.
+    gamma, thickness, pressure = 1.3, 0.7, 0.8
+    a = pressure / gamma
+    slope = lambda z: a*(thickness-z) / math.sqrt(1-(a*(thickness-z))**2)
+    top_numeric = simpson(slope, 0, thickness)
+    r = pressure*thickness/gamma
+    top_exact = (pressure*thickness**2/gamma)/(1+math.sqrt(1-r*r))
+    assert abs(top_numeric-top_exact) < 1e-12
+    assert slope(thickness) == 0
+    checks["pinned_elastica_top_quadrature_abs_error"] = abs(top_numeric-top_exact)
+    checks["status"] = "passed_internal_conditional_identity_checks_only"
+    return checks

+

The exact checks in `verify_transfers.py` check arithmetic and finite witnesses; they do not formalize the analytic arguments. Nothing here establishes a physical capability or the universal quartic implication.

+## 1. The incoming trace obstruction applies explicitly to the heat-certified Fstar
+
+Use precisely the FE definition, with A's columns x,y:
+
+    u=|x|², v=|y|², w=x·y, q=det A,
+    Fstar(A)=u²+v²+4w²+(7/2)q²−(29/10)q(u+v).
+
+Thus Fstar(I)=−3/10. The main FO correction to this value is correct. An early message from this audit mistakenly gave −13/10; that arithmetic error was corrected before any saved theorem or verification. The final constants below are exact.
+
+Identify R² with C. On an open strip of width T=1+log 2 define
+
+    φ(x,y)=r(x)e^{iy},
+    r(x)=x/2                      for 0≤x≤1,
+    r(x)=(1/2)e^{x−1}             for 1≤x≤1+log 2.
+
+This is an actual compatible potential, from zero to U+(y)=e^{iy}. It is piecewise smooth and in W^{1,4}. Interior corners may be smoothed while retaining the endpoints and taking the action limit.
+
+On the first segment, left SO(2) invariance gives Fstar(Dφ)=2^{-4}Fstar(diag(1,x)). Direct integration yields
+
+    ∫₀¹ Fstar(diag(1,x)) dx
+      = ∫₀¹ [1+x⁴+(7/2)x²−(29/10)x(1+x²)] dx
+      =23/120.
+
+On the exponential segment, Dφ=r(x)R_y I, so its action is
+
+    Fstar(I)·(1−2^{-4})/4.
+
+Consequently the whole entry action and fourth-power gradient energy are
+
+    W_entry = −3/40 + (4/15)·2^{-4} = −7/120,
+    E_entry = 2^{-4}·(28/15)+(1−2^{-4}) =253/240.
+
+The return potential ψ(x,y)=φ(T−x,−y) goes from U−(y)=e^{-iy} to zero. Its gradient is −Dφ(T−x,−y); even quartic homogeneity therefore gives the same action and norm energy. These are two different oriented endpoints, not a negative closed cycle.
+
+For every positive integer N rescale
+
+    φ_N(x,y)=N^{-3/4}φ(Nx,Ny),   0≤x≤T/N.
+
+The gradients scale by N^{1/4}, their fourth powers by N, and strip width by 1/N. The action is still −7/120. Thus every dominating storage P on complete profiles must satisfy
+
+    P(N^{-3/4}e^{iNy})−P(0) ≤−7/120,
+    P(N^{-3/4}e^{-iNy})−P(0) ≥+7/120.
+
+These profile sequences tend strongly to zero in subcritical W^{s,4}, s<3/4, and weakly to zero in critical W^{3/4,4}. Hence no such P can be subcritical continuous, or weakly lower or upper semicontinuous at zero in the critical topology. The same incoming theorem also excludes smooth first-derivative local densities at B=0: Fstar(tI)=−3t⁴/10 cannot be bounded below by κ det(tI)=κt² for all t. This does not exclude nonlocal, orientation-sensitive, strongly critical storage.

+
+    ∫Fstar(Dφ) ≥(1/36000)∫|Dφ|⁴.
+
+A strip bridge from U+ to U−, with action W_bridge and norm energy E_bridge, closes the two negative strips into a compatible cycle. Therefore
+
+    W_bridge ≥7/60+(253/120+E_bridge)/36000
+             =504253/4320000+E_bridge/36000.
+
+This lower bound explains precisely which missing oriented transition prevents the negative open strips from contradicting the heat-certified quasiconvex result. It does not prove that margin independently. It does not transfer the FO one-frequency G storage to Fstar or to arbitrary-frequency profiles.

+## 2. A general bath-spoof theorem for the incoming exchange assay
+
+Let A denote the followed data-reference register RS and E the resident environment. Fold a fixed continuation and its bounded score into an effect 0≤K≤I on A⊗E. For a prepared A state σ define the conditional bath effect
+
+    K_σ=Tr_A[(σ⊗I_E)K],
+    β(K)=sup_σ [λ_max(K_σ)−λ_min(K_σ)].
+
+K_σ is a Hermitian effect. For the ideal decorrelated product σ⊗τ, an otherwise perfect exchange followed by an unobserved bath unitary V changes the score by Tr[K_σ(VτV†−τ)]. The sharp worst-case absolute change, over τ and bath unitaries V, is the spectral diameter of K_σ. It is attained with τ an extremal eigenstate and V an involution swapping the maximum and minimum eigenvectors. Thus the universal worst-case score spoof is exactly β(K), with 0≤β(K)≤1.
+
+Every implemented two-copy gate
+
+    W=SWAP_{S1,S2}⊗V_{E1}⊗V_{E2},   V²=I,
+
+has exactly the ideal reduced action on all accessible R/S registers, even for arbitrary joint inputs. It also satisfies W²=I. Reduced-register process tomography and a perfect double-swap echo therefore cannot distinguish all gates achieving that sharp spoof. The example can begin with independent, completely uncorrelated A/E replicas; no true conditional correlation is needed for the false signal.
+
+Moreover,
+
+    β(K)=0  iff  K=K_A⊗I_E.
+
+If β=0, every K_σ is scalar. Pairing with every traceless Hermitian E operator, and using the linear span of density matrices on A, implies that K has only the identity bath component. The converse is immediate. Such an effect has identical expectation on any ρ_AE and ρ_A⊗ρ_E, so it cannot measure the correlation-removal effect. Therefore a nontrivial correlation-sensitive continuation cannot also be universally insensitive to every hidden bath operation invisible to a reduced gate audit. This is a general identifiability obstruction, extending the incoming single Bell-state counterexample. It is not an assertion of historical novelty.

+## 3. Explicit source current for the open PR85 remote-response family
+
+PR85's one-excitation factor is
+
+    J=Σ_{i=1}^{m−1} c_i q_i* q_i+e e_m e_m*,
+    q_i=e_i*−[i/(i+1)]e_{i+1}*,   c_i=(i+1)/i,
+    b=e_1.
+
+The weighted Thomson current can be written without an inverse:
+
+    f_i=1/i  (1≤i<m),   f_terminal=1/m.
+
+It satisfies Σ q_i* f_i+e_m f_terminal=e_1 exactly: the internal coefficients telescope. Its dual energy is
+
+    Σ_{i=1}^{m−1}|f_i|²/c_i+|f_terminal|²/e
+      =Σ1/[i(i+1)]+1/(m²e)
+      =(m−1)/m+1/(m²e).
+
+This equals the source response, so it is the exact minimum-energy completion. In N816's Euclidean physical-row notation the same witness has w_i=1/sqrt(i(i+1)) and w_terminal=1/(m sqrt(e)). It supplies a concrete source current beyond the late FO adjudication's abstract J=LH^+b recipe. Its O(m) arithmetic cost matches the tridiagonal incumbent, so no algorithmic advantage follows.
+
+With e known only in [e_minus,e_plus]⊂(0,∞), the sharp response interval is
+
+    [(m−1)/m+1/(m²e_plus), (m−1)/m+1/(m²e_minus)].
+
+Feasibility of the weighted current is independent of e, but its energy requires a positive acquired lower endpoint. If e_minus=0, no finite uniform response upper endpoint exists. Exact gap-free completion therefore moves the unresolved physical requirement to a source-specific terminal coefficient; it does not erase acquisition precision. PR85's evolution-only Ω(1/e) interrogation lower bound remains compatible with this exact symbolic completion.

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Exact finite checks for the overlap audit's explicit new constructions.
+
+These checks establish arithmetic and finite examples. They do not independently
+validate analytic source theorems, universal claims, historical novelty, or
+physical acquisition. No source package is imported or modified.
+"""
+from fractions import Fraction as Q
+from pathlib import Path
+import json
+
+
+def mm(a, b):
+    return [[sum((a[i][k]*b[k][j] for k in range(len(b))), Q(0))
+             for j in range(len(b[0]))] for i in range(len(a))]
+
+
+def kron(a, b):
+    return [[x*y for x in rowa for y in rowb] for rowa in a for rowb in b]
+
+
+def eye(n):
+    return [[Q(i == j) for j in range(n)] for i in range(n)]
+
+
+def tr(a):
+    return sum((a[i][i] for i in range(len(a))), Q(0))
+
+
+def partial_e(a, da=4, de=2):
+    return [[sum((a[i*de+k][j*de+k] for k in range(de)), Q(0))
+             for j in range(da)] for i in range(da)]
+
+
+def fstar_ramp():
+    # Fstar(diag(1,x)); definitions are those of FE, not a normalized surrogate.
+    co = [Q(1), -Q(29, 10), Q(7, 2), -Q(29, 10), Q(1)]
+    at_i = sum(co)
+    linear_unit_action = sum(c/Q(i+1) for i, c in enumerate(co))
+    assert at_i == -Q(3, 10)
+    assert linear_unit_action == Q(23, 120)
+    eps = Q(1, 2)
+    ramp_action = eps**4 * linear_unit_action
+    exponential_action = at_i * (1-eps**4)/4
+    total_action = ramp_action + exponential_action
+    assert total_action == -Q(7, 120)
+    norm_ramp = eps**4 * (1 + Q(2, 3) + Q(1, 5))
+    norm_exponential = 1-eps**4
+    total_norm = norm_ramp + norm_exponential
+    assert total_norm == Q(253, 240)
+    eta = Q(1, 36000)
+    bridge_lower_constant = -2*total_action + 2*eta*total_norm
+    assert bridge_lower_constant == Q(504253, 4320000)
+    assert 4*(1-Q(3, 4))-1 == 0
+    return dict(fstar_at_identity=str(at_i), linear_ramp_unit_action=str(linear_unit_action),
+                entry_action=str(total_action), entry_norm4_energy=str(total_norm),
+                bridge_lower_constant_if_FE_margin_valid=str(bridge_lower_constant),
+                additional_bridge_term="E_bridge/36000", critical_trace_exponent="3/4")
+
+
+def explicit_response_current():
+    cases=[]
+    for m in (2, 3, 5, 8, 25):
+        flux=[Q(1,i) for i in range(1,m)] + [Q(1,m)]
+        source=[Q(0)]*m
+        for i in range(1,m):
+            source[i-1] += flux[i-1]
+            source[i] -= Q(i,i+1)*flux[i-1]
+        source[-1] += flux[-1]
+        assert source == [Q(1)] + [Q(0)]*(m-1)
+        for e in (Q(1,10**6), Q(1,3), Q(2)):
+            energy=sum((flux[i-1]**2/Q(i+1,i) for i in range(1,m)),Q(0)) + flux[-1]**2/e
+            exact=Q(m-1,m)+1/(m*m*e)
+            assert energy==exact
+            cases.append(dict(m=m,e=str(e),source_current_energy=str(energy)))
+    return dict(cases=cases, interior_flux="f_i=1/i", terminal_flux="f_m=1/m",
+                robust_uncertainty_interval="[(m-1)/m+1/(m^2*e_plus),(m-1)/m+1/(m^2*e_minus)]",
+                zero_lower_endpoint="unbounded upper response if e_minus=0")
+
+
+def invisible_bath_reflection():
+    bell=[[Q(0) for _ in range(4)] for _ in range(4)]
+    for i in (0,3):
+        for j in (0,3): bell[i][j]=Q(1,2)
+    z0=[[Q(1),Q(0)],[Q(0),Q(0)]]
+    flip=[[Q(0),Q(1)],[Q(1),Q(0)]]
+    bath_flip=kron(eye(4),flip)
+    cz=eye(8)
+    for i in range(8):
+        if ((i>>1)&1) and (i&1): cz[i][i]=-Q(1)
+    effect=mm(mm(cz,kron(bell,eye(2))),cz)
+    rho=kron(bell,z0)
+    altered=mm(mm(bath_flip,rho),bath_flip)
+    assert mm(bath_flip,bath_flip)==eye(8)
+    assert partial_e(rho)==partial_e(altered)==bell
+    scores=(tr(mm(effect,rho)),tr(mm(effect,altered)))
+    assert scores==(Q(1),Q(0))
+    conditional_effect=[[sum((bell[a][b]*effect[b*2+e][a*2+f]
+                                      for a in range(4) for b in range(4)),Q(0))
+                         for f in range(2)] for e in range(2)]
+    assert conditional_effect==[[Q(1),Q(0)],[Q(0),Q(0)]]
+    return dict(ideal_score=str(scores[0]),hidden_bath_score=str(scores[1]),
+                reduced_data_reference_identical=True,bath_reflection_square_identity=True,
+                conditional_effect_eigenvalues=["1","0"],sharp_score_spoof_radius="1")
+
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    result=dict(status="PASS",scope="exact arithmetic and finite witnesses only",

+\[
+ (\rho_A\otimes\rho_E)^{\otimes m}

+**Proof.** Take constant `C`, trivial `R`, and
+
+\[
+ \rho_t=t|00\rangle\langle00|+(1-t)|11\rangle\langle11|,
+ \qquad 0<t<1.
+\]
+
+The input `rho_t^{tensor N}` is an operator-valued polynomial in `t` of degree at most `N`. A fixed quantum channel is linear in that operator. Equality for every `t` in an interval forces a polynomial of degree `2m` to have degree at most `N`. Hence `N >= 2m`. QED.
+
+For heralded operation, collect the designated successful branches into a trace-nonincreasing completely positive map. Its success probability `q(t)` is a polynomial of degree at most `N`. If the successful normalized output equals the target wherever `q(t)>0`, the unnormalized all-zero probability is
+
+\[
+ q(t)t^{2m}.
+\]
+
+A nonzero polynomial `q` gives degree `deg(q)+2m`; this is at most `N` only if `N >= 2m`. It is enough to require exactness on an open interval of nonzero success; the polynomial identity extends from that interval. This does not grant a zero-success protocol any capability.

+Adaptive protocols that use at most `N` preparations fit the same proof: pad unused preparations and combine measurement branches into one CP instrument. +## 6. Quantum Markov and recoverability interpretation
+
+For classical `C`, define
+
+\[
+ \gamma_{CAE}=\sum_c p_c|c\rangle\langle c|\otimes\rho_A^c\otimes\rho_E^c.
+\]
+
+It is the unique maximum-entropy classical-block extension with the same `CA` and `CE` marginals. Per block, subadditivity gives `H(AE)<=H(A)+H(E)`, with equality only for the product state. Consequently,
+
+\[
+ D_{\rm rel}(\rho_{CAE}\Vert\gamma_{CAE})
+ =H(\gamma)-H(\rho)=I(A:E\mid C)_\rho,
+\]
+
+where logarithms are base two. Also, `I(A:E|C)=0` if and only if `rho=gamma`. Recovery from the classical record can be written explicitly: read `c` and append `rho_E^c` to the `CA` marginal. This is a state-dependent mathematical recovery channel; acquiring and physically preparing an inaccessible `rho_E^c` is a separate resource. The swap construction realizes a tagged product state using independent preparations instead of a marginal-state description.
+
+The general quantum conditional-information setting is broader. Approximate recovery is related to small conditional mutual information by [Fawzi and Renner, *Quantum conditional mutual information and approximate Markov chains*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1410.0664). For quantum conditioning registers, exact Markov states have a direct-sum tensor-factor structure on the conditioning register, as characterized by [Hayden, Jozsa, Petz and Winter](https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/0304007). A generic quantum register cannot be read and used to sort copies like a classical label without disturbance. No coherent-`C` extension, universal recovery implementation, or quantum-condition tomography advantage is proved by the checkpoint.

+Consider a past controlled classical history bit `h` stored in `E`. At the cut, `S` has been reset to `|0>` and `R` is constant. The present state is

+ |0\rangle\langle0|_{RS}\otimes\sum_h p_h|h\rangle\langle h|_E.

+Thus `I(RS:E)=0` and exchange produces no tagged-state change. A future CNOT from `E` to `S` nevertheless reveals `h`. The future remains dependent on the past after the system reset. This is precisely the type of dependence tested by the operational process criterion of [Pollock et al., *Operational Markov condition for quantum processes*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.09811).

+Expanding `R` to contain the history can make the association visible, but changes the acquired input/reference contract. Conditioning on a larger actual `C` changes the estimand and the matching cost. Neither operation happens automatically. +
+[Berta, Brandao, Majenz and Wilde, *Conditional Decoupling of Quantum Information*](https://arxiv.org/html/1808.00135), defines deconstruction and conditional erasure using randomizing channels with ancillary resources, negligible disturbance of a specified other marginal, and recoverability or decoupling conditions. Its asymptotic noise rate is conditional mutual information. Conditional erasure permits a maximally mixed output on an appropriate subspace rather than preserving an arbitrary unknown `RS` marginal. In their notation the accessible conditioning subsystem is also part of the allowed control.

Deterministic exchange with zero randomization bits does not violate an erasure-cost theorem: the complete exchange output has not been decoupled. Discarding complementary modules removes their correlations from the retained description and pays a preparation/disposal cost. No heat or work claim follows from the local entropy increase alone.

+ N\ge1+\frac{\log\epsilon}{\log(1-1/K)}\approx1+K\log(1/\epsilon).

+

The expected number of moved records of that type in a batch is exactly `Np[1-(1-p)^(N-1)]`; when `Np` is small it is about `N(N-1)p^2`. These costs cannot be eliminated by not estimating `p` explicitly.

+There is also a basic score-estimation lower bound already in classical diagonal inputs. Suppose a single informative prepared experiment returns a Bernoulli bit with parameter `p_+=(1+gamma)/2` or `p_-=(1-gamma)/2`, with `0<gamma<=1/2`. +
+\[
+ n\,d(p_+\Vert p_-)
+ \ge (1-2\delta)\log\frac{1-\delta}{\delta}.
+\]
+
+Since `d(p_+||p_-)=gamma log((1+gamma)/(1-gamma)) <= 4gamma^2`,
+
+\[
+ n\ge\frac{(1-2\delta)\log((1-\delta)/\delta)}{4\gamma^2}.
+\]
+
+The relative-entropy calculation uses natural logarithms. The decision margin from `1/2` is `gamma/2`. Collective quantum processing cannot circumvent this classical iid subfamily: the states commute and the input already exposes its full classical information. +# Scope correction: deterministic finite-error bound versus exact heralded theorem
+
+Date: 15 October 2026. Applies to Section 4 of the frozen `REPORT.md`, specifically the paragraph beginning “An elementary finite-error obstruction is also available.” The original report, checks, and inventory are preserved unchanged.
+
+The displayed finite-error bound
+
+\[
+ \epsilon\ge\frac{(2m)!}{2^{2m}(2m)^{2m}},\qquad N=2m-1,
+\]
+
+is proved here **for deterministic CPTP outputs only**, with uniform trace-distance error
+
+\[
+ \frac12\|\Lambda(\rho_t^{\otimes N})-
+       (\rho_A(t)\otimes\rho_E(t))^{\otimes m}\|_1\le\epsilon
+ \quad\text{for every }t\in[0,1].
+\]
+
+Under this normalization, the error of every effect probability is at most `epsilon`. A deterministic output effect probability is a degree-at-most-`N` polynomial in `t`; its order-`2m` finite difference vanishes. This is the premise used in the original finite-error calculation.
+
+For a heralded trace-nonincreasing CP map, the unnormalized all-zero effect probability `f(t)` and success probability `q(t)` are polynomials of degree at most `N`. The normalized successful output has effect probability `f(t)/q(t)`, which is generally rational, not polynomial. Its order-`N+1` finite difference need not vanish. The displayed approximate-output bound has therefore **not** been established for normalized heralded outputs. No approximate heralded lower bound is supplied by this correction.
+
+For example, with one classical correlated-bit preparation, accept input bit zero with probability one and bit one with probability `alpha`, where the fixed parameter `0 < alpha < 1` is independent of the unknown `t`. On success, output the original classical pair. Then
+
+\[
+ q(t)=t+\alpha(1-t),\qquad f(t)=t,
+ \qquad\Pr(00\mid\mathrm{success})
+ =\frac{t}{\alpha+(1-\alpha)t}.
+\]
+
+At `alpha=1/2`, the normalized all-zero probabilities on the grid `t=0,1/2,1` are `0,2/3,1`, whose second finite difference is `-1/3`. This explicitly shows why a degree-one input does not force the normalized successful probability to have zero second finite difference. It is a rationality example, not a protocol that achieves the decorrelated target or a counterexample to a stated approximate bound.
+
+The **exact universal heralded theorem `N >= 2m` remains valid**. Exact normalized target equality on an interval of nonzero success gives the polynomial identity
+
+\[
+ f(t)=q(t)t^{2m}.
+\]
+
+For nonzero polynomial `q`, the right-hand side has degree `deg(q)+2m`, whereas `deg(f) <= N`. Hence `N >= 2m`, as argued in the frozen report. Bounded adaptive budgets still reduce to a fixed CP instrument; unbounded stopping times and expected-copy budgets remain outside that proof.
+
+This correction narrows the finite-error statement and leaves the exact deterministic/heralded lower bound, routing structure, estimator proof, and physical limitations unchanged. It records a proof-scope clarification identified by the independent adversarial review; no external correctness certification or priority claim is implied.

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Finite checks for the accompanying conditional-exchange information report.
+
+Only NumPy and the Python standard library are used. These checks are evidence
+for finite instances, not an external proof review or a hardware experiment.
+All output is written next to this script; no source packet or repository is
+modified.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import hashlib
+import itertools
+import json
+import math
+from fractions import Fraction
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import numpy as np
+
+OUT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+RNG = np.random.default_rng(202610150713)
+
+
+def tensor(*states):
+    result = np.array([[1.0]], dtype=complex)
+    for state in states:
+        result = np.kron(result, state)
+    return result
+
+
+def reorder(state, dims, order):
+    n = len(dims)
+    axes = list(order) + [n + i for i in order]
+    return state.reshape(tuple(dims) * 2).transpose(axes).reshape(state.shape)
+
+
+def reduce(state, dims, keep):
+    keep = list(keep)
+    drop = [i for i in range(len(dims)) if i not in keep]
+    perm = reorder(state, dims, keep + drop)
+    d_keep = math.prod(dims[i] for i in keep)
+    d_drop = math.prod(dims[i] for i in drop)
+    return np.einsum("abcb->ac", perm.reshape(d_keep, d_drop, d_keep, d_drop))
+
+
+def entropy(state):
+    values = np.linalg.eigvalsh((state + state.conj().T) / 2)
+    values = values[values > 1e-13]
+    return float(-np.sum(values * np.log2(values)))
+
+
+def random_state(d):
+    x = RNG.normal(size=(d, d)) + 1j * RNG.normal(size=(d, d))
+    x = x @ x.conj().T
+    return x / np.trace(x)
+
+
+def close(a, b, tol=2e-10):
+    error = float(np.max(np.abs(np.asarray(a) - np.asarray(b))))
+    assert error < tol, (error, tol)
+    return error
+
+
+def cycles(perm):
+    seen, result = set(), []
+    for start in range(len(perm)):
+        if start in seen:
+            continue
+        component, i = [], start
+        while i not in seen:
+            seen.add(i)
+            component.append(i)
+            i = perm[i]
+        result.append(component)
+    return result
+
+
+def pair_triple_route(labels):
+    # perm[i] is the donor whose A (logical R,S) appears at recipient i.
+    perm = list(range(len(labels)))
+    for c in set(labels):
+        group = [i for i, value in enumerate(labels) if value == c]
+        if len(group) <= 1:
+            continue
+        if len(group) % 2:
+            a, b, d = group[:3]
+            perm[a], perm[b], perm[d] = b, d, a
+            group = group[3:]
+        for a, b in zip(group[0::2], group[1::2]):
+            perm[a], perm[b] = b, a
+    return perm
+
+
+def correlation_graph_checks():
+    max_errors = {"tagged_product": 0.0, "global_mutual_information": 0.0,
+                  "output_multi_information": 0.0, "retained_mutual_information": 0.0,
+                  "disjoint_retained_product": 0.0}
+    cases = 0
+    # Includes non-derangements to check the number-moved correction.
+    configurations = [(2, [1, 0]), (3, [1, 2, 0]),
+                      (3, [1, 0, 2]), (4, [1, 0, 3, 2]),
+                      (4, [1, 2, 3, 0])]
+    for n, perm in configurations:
+        for _ in range(3):
+            rho = random_state(4)
+            rho_a, rho_e = reduce(rho, [2, 2], [0]), reduce(rho, [2, 2], [1])
+            info = entropy(rho_a) + entropy(rho_e) - entropy(rho)
+            original = tensor(*([rho] * n))
+            order = [item for i in range(n) for item in (2 * perm[i], 2 * i + 1)]
+            output = reorder(original, [2] * (2 * n), order)
+            local_entropies = []
+            for i in range(n):
+                marginal = reduce(output, [2] * (2 * n), [2 * i, 2 * i + 1])
+                target = rho if perm[i] == i else tensor(rho_a, rho_e)
+                error = close(marginal, target)
+                max_errors["tagged_product"] = max(max_errors["tagged_product"], error)
+                local_entropies.append(entropy(marginal))
+            all_a = reduce(output, [2] * (2 * n), list(range(0, 2 * n, 2)))
+            all_e = reduce(output, [2] * (2 * n), list(range(1, 2 * n, 2)))
+            global_info = entropy(all_a) + entropy(all_e) - entropy(output)
+            error = close(global_info, n * info)
+            max_errors["global_mutual_information"] = max(max_errors["global_mutual_information"], error)
+            moved = sum(perm[i] != i for i in range(n))
+            error = close(sum(local_entropies) - entropy(output), moved * info)
+            max_errors["output_multi_information"] = max(max_errors["output_multi_information"], error)
+            for bits in itertools.product((False, True), repeat=n):
+                retained = [i for i, flag in enumerate(bits) if flag]
+                if not retained:
+                    continue
+                marginal = reduce(output, [2] * (2 * n),
+                                  [item for i in retained for item in (2 * i, 2 * i + 1)])
+                a = reduce(marginal, [2] * (2 * len(retained)), list(range(0, 2 * len(retained), 2)))
+                e = reduce(marginal, [2] * (2 * len(retained)), list(range(1, 2 * len(retained), 2)))
+                overlap = len(set(retained).intersection(perm[i] for i in retained))
+                error = close(entropy(a) + entropy(e) - entropy(marginal), overlap * info)
+                max_errors["retained_mutual_information"] = max(max_errors["retained_mutual_information"], error)
+                if overlap == 0:
+                    error = close(marginal, tensor(*([tensor(rho_a, rho_e)] * len(retained))))
+                    max_errors["disjoint_retained_product"] = max(max_errors["disjoint_retained_product"], error)
+                cases += 1
+    return {"passed": True, "retained_subset_cases": cases, "max_errors": max_errors}
+
+
+def compilation_checks():
+    table = []
+    for n in range(2, 9):
+        best = n
+        tested = 0
+        for perm in itertools.permutations(range(n)):
+            if any(perm[i] == i for i in range(n)):
+                continue
+            best = min(best, n - len(cycles(perm)))
+            tested += 1
+        route = pair_triple_route([0] * n)
+        observed = n - len(cycles(route))
+        assert best == observed == math.ceil(n / 2)
+        table.append({"class_size": n, "derangements_enumerated": tested,
+                      "minimum_block_swaps": best, "checkpoint_cycle_swaps": n - 1})
+    return {"passed": True, "table": table}
+
+
+def polynomial_checks():
+    table = []
+    for m in range(1, 7):
+        n = 2 * m - 1
+        order = n + 1
+        diff = sum(Fraction((-1) ** (order - j) * math.comb(order, j))
+                   * Fraction(j, order) ** (2 * m) for j in range(order + 1))
+        target = Fraction(math.factorial(order), order ** order)
+        assert diff == target > 0
+        for degree in range(n + 1):
+            observed = sum(Fraction((-1) ** (order - j) * math.comb(order, j))
+                           * Fraction(j, order) ** degree for j in range(order + 1))
+            assert observed == 0
+        table.append({"N": n, "m": m, "target_finite_difference": str(diff),
+                      "uniform_trace_error_lower_bound": str(diff / (2 ** order))})
+    return {"passed": True, "note": "Finite differences certify the degree mismatch, not arbitrary channels by enumeration.",
+            "table": table}
+
+
+def label_lipschitz_checks():
+    # Extreme vertices suffice: every change is affine in the six scores.
+    maximum, witness, cases = 0, None, 0
+    for n in range(1, 8):
+        compositions = [(a, b, n - a - b) for a in range(n + 1) for b in range(n - a + 1)]
+        for scores in itertools.product((0, 1), repeat=6):
+            natural, dec = scores[:3], scores[3:]
+            def value(counts):
+                return sum(0 if k == 0 else natural[c] if k == 1 else k * dec[c]
+                           for c, k in enumerate(counts))
+            for counts in compositions:
+                for old in range(3):
+                    if counts[old] == 0:
+                        continue
+                    for new in range(3):
+                        if new == old:
+                            continue
+                        changed = list(counts)
+                        changed[old] -= 1
+                        changed[new] += 1
+                        delta = abs(value(changed) - value(counts))
+                        assert delta <= 3
+                        cases += 1
+                        if delta > maximum:
+                            maximum = delta
+                            witness = {"counts": counts, "old": old, "new": new,
+                                       "natural_scores": natural, "decorrelated_scores": dec}
+    assert maximum == 3
+    return {"passed": True, "cases": cases, "max_sum_change": maximum,
+            "bounded_score_witness": witness}
+
+
+def reference_pairing_countermodel():
+    psi = np.zeros(8, dtype=complex)
+    psi[0] = psi[5] = 1 / math.sqrt(2)  # (r,s,e)=(0,0,0),(1,0,1)
+    rho = np.outer(psi, psi.conj())
+    original = tensor(rho, rho)
+    routed = reorder(original, [2] * 6, [0, 4, 2, 3, 1, 5])
+    routing_error = close(routed, original)
+    future = reorder(routed, [2] * 6, [0, 2, 1, 3, 5, 4])
+    bell = np.array([1, 0, 0, 1], dtype=complex) / math.sqrt(2)
+    effect = np.outer(bell, bell.conj())
+    resident = float(np.trace(effect @ reduce(future, [2] * 6, [0, 1])).real)
+    donor = float(np.trace(effect @ reduce(future, [2] * 6, [3, 1])).real)
+    close(resident, 1)
+    close(donor, 0.25)
+    return {"passed": True, "physical_state_routing_change_max_entry": routing_error,
+            "resident_reference_Bell_score": resident, "donor_reference_Bell_score": donor,
+            "tracked_contrast": resident - donor}
+
+
+def bell_cycle_checks():
+    table = []
+    for n in range(2, 8):
+        perm = list(range(1, n)) + [0]
+        for u in (Fraction(1, 5), Fraction(1, 2)):
+            distribution = []
+            for bits in itertools.product((0, 1), repeat=n):
+                probability = math.prod(u if bit else 1 - u for bit in bits)
+                scores = [int(bits[perm[i]] == bits[i]) for i in range(n)]
+                assert sum(1 - score for score in scores) % 2 == 0
+                distribution.append((probability, scores))
+            q = (1 - u) ** 2 + u ** 2
+            mean = sum(p * sum(x) for p, x in distribution)
+            variance = sum(p * (sum(x) - mean) ** 2 for p, x in distribution)
+            v = u * (1 - u)
+            expected = 2 * n * q * (1 - q) if n == 2 else 4 * n * v * (1 - 3 * v)
+            assert mean == n * q and variance == expected
+            table.append({"cycle_length": n, "u": str(u), "mean_each": str(q),
+                          "sum_variance": str(variance), "iid_sum_variance": str(n * q * (1 - q)),
+                          "global_even_mismatch_constraint": True})
+    return {"passed": True, "table": table}
+
+
+def concentration_mgf_checks():
+    # Exact finite enumeration of a nontrivial condition-matched Bell phase assay.
+    n, p, u = 5, (Fraction(3, 5), Fraction(2, 5)), (Fraction(1, 5), Fraction(2, 5))
+    distribution = []
+    for labels in itertools.product((0, 1), repeat=n):
+        label_probability = math.prod(p[c] for c in labels)
+        perm = pair_triple_route(labels)
+        component_denominator = sum(len(component) ** 2 for component in cycles(perm))
+        assert component_denominator <= 3 * n
+        conditional = []
+        for bits in itertools.product((0, 1), repeat=n):
+            probability = math.prod(u[c] if bit else 1 - u[c] for c, bit in zip(labels, bits))
+            total = sum(int(bits[perm[i]] == bits[i]) for i in range(n))
+            conditional.append((float(probability), total))
+            distribution.append((float(label_probability * probability), total))
+        mean = sum(probability * total for probability, total in conditional)
+        for lam in np.linspace(-2, 2, 17):
+            mgf = sum(probability * math.exp(lam * (total - mean)) for probability, total in conditional)
+            assert mgf <= math.exp(component_denominator * lam ** 2 / 8) + 1e-10
+    mean = sum(probability * total for probability, total in distribution)
+    max_ratio = 0.0
+    for lam in np.linspace(-2, 2, 33):
+        mgf = sum(probability * math.exp(lam * (total - mean)) for probability, total in distribution)
+        bound = math.exp(12 * n * lam ** 2 / 8)
+        assert mgf <= bound + 1e-10
+        max_ratio = max(max_ratio, mgf / bound)
+    b, delta, batch_n = 4000, 0.05, 32
+    original_radius = math.sqrt(math.log(8 / delta) / (2 * b))
+    new_radius = math.sqrt(6 * math.log(8 / delta) / (b * batch_n))
+    return {"passed": True, "enumerated_label_and_phase_assignments": len(distribution),
+            "largest_unconditional_mgf_to_bound_ratio": max_ratio,
+            "example": {"B": b, "N": batch_n, "delta": delta,

+                        "new_four_arm_radius": new_radius,
+                        "new_two_arm_radius": 2 * new_radius,
+                        "complete_replica_preparations_four_arms": 4 * b * batch_n}}
+
+

+# An unconditional concentration bound for condition-matched local exchange scores
+
+Root derivation, 15 October 2026. The independent quantum-information worker
+derived the pair/triple compiler and conditional component bound; the root
+supplied the random-label bounded-difference step below. Both reconstructed the
+combined argument. This is same-team analytic work, not external validation.
+
+## Exact scope
+
+Each arm prepares B independent batches of N iid labeled modules. Conditional
+on the full label vector, modules are independent and their joint RSE state
+depends only on their observed condition c. All gate components, continuation
+channels and readouts act locally to their declared components and introduce
+no shared noise. Each endpoint score is in [0,1]. The bath-safe joint routing,
+reference tracking, matched continuation and readout assumptions of the source
+remain required. None is inferred from this sampling proof.
+
+Within a condition class of size k>=2, use disjoint swaps for even k and one
+3-cycle plus disjoint swaps for odd k. Singletons remain untouched. Every
+non-singleton moves and has exactly the source's conditional product marginal.
+For each condition, denote the native and routed local score means by o_c,d_c
+in [0,1]. These values need not be known to use the bound.
+
+The tested target is the actual unconditional *finite-batch* routing score,
+not the ideal infinite-reservoir score. Systematic errors and any inference
+from finite batch to ideal decorrelation are separate from sampling error.
+
+## Conditional measurement fluctuations
+
+For fixed labels the disjoint components are independent. A component of size
+g in {1,2,3} has total score in [0,g], even when its endpoints are correlated.
+Write S for the score averaged over all BN endpoints. Hoeffding's exponential
+bound, conditional on the labels, gives
+
+    E[exp(lambda (S-E[S|labels])) | labels]
+      <= exp(lambda^2 sum_components g^2 / (8 B^2 N^2))
+      <= exp(3 lambda^2/(8BN)).
+
+The second inequality uses g^2<=3g and sum g=BN. Independent endpoints are
+never assumed. More precise realized component counts improve this term.
+
+## Random-label fluctuations
+
+For one batch the conditional mean is
+
+    mu(labels)= (1/N) sum_c h_c(k_c),
+    h_c(0)=0, h_c(1)=o_c, h_c(k)=k d_c for k>=2.
+
+Its increment on adding one member to a class is
+
+    h_c(1)-h_c(0)=o_c in [0,1],
+    h_c(2)-h_c(1)=2d_c-o_c in [-1,2],
+    h_c(k+1)-h_c(k)=d_c in [0,1] for k>=2.
+
+Changing one label removes one member from a class and adds one to another.
+Therefore it changes the conditional batch mean by at most 3/N. This constant
+is attainable with two classes initially of sizes2 and1: take native/routed
+means (1,0) and (0,1), and move one member from the former to the latter.
+
+The B-batch conditional mean, as a function of BN independent labels, has
+bounded differences 3/(BN). The Doob-martingale exponential bound gives
+
+    E[exp(lambda(E[S|labels]-E S))] <= exp(9 lambda^2/(8BN)).
+
+For completeness, both exponential bounds use only the elementary bounded
+variable lemma log E exp(lambda(Z-E Z)) <=lambda^2(b-a)^2/8 for Z in[a,b].
+To prove it, twice differentiate the log moment-generating function; its
+second derivative is the variance under exponential tilting, at most
+(b-a)^2/4. Integrate twice from zero. The label bound applies that lemma to
+Doob increments, each of whose conditional range is at most the corresponding
+bounded difference. Thus no unexplained concentration theorem is a premise.
+
+## Combined result
+
+Condition first on labels and then average the two exponential bounds:
+
+    E exp(lambda(S-E S)) <= exp(12 lambda^2/(8BN)).
+
+Chernoff optimization for both signs yields
+
+    Pr(|S-E S|>=r) <= 2 exp(-BN r^2/6).
+
+For four predeclared arms, a union bound gives the simultaneous per-arm radius
+
+    r4 = sqrt(6 log(8/delta)/(BN)).
+
+Each two-arm contrast has radius2r4. One can use the smaller of this and the
+source's independent-batch radius sqrt(log(8/delta)/(2B)); the new bound is
+smaller when N>12. With B=4000,N=32,delta=.05, the new per-arm radius is about
+0.015424 versus .025187 for the batch-only bound. This is a sufficient analytic
+bound under stronger explicit local-component assumptions. It is neither a
+measured shot requirement nor a demonstrated advantage over other assays.
+
+The number of transpositions per class is ceil(k/2), minimal among
+derangements: a permutation with no fixed points has at most floor(k/2)
+cycles, and its minimum transposition count is k minus its cycle count.
+This reduces gate count relative to one long cycle without changing the
+source's tagged mean. Bath action, parallel hardware, resets, reference
+storage and acquisition costs remain charged.
+
+## Limits and falsifiers
+
+A joint cross-component continuation, common detector or gate noise, dependent
+source preparations, unmodeled adaptive policy selection, or nonlocal score
+can invalidate this factorization. Treat independent whole batches as the
+sampling units until the stronger locality/independence contract is justified.
+The actual tested score includes reference assignment and can change purely
+because reference partners changed; the separate reference-pairing
+counterexample must accompany any causal interpretation.

+# Exact retained-workload correlations under reference-tracked exchange
+
+Date: 15 October 2026 (Australia/Brisbane). Internally derived by the root
+researcher; historical originality and external review are UNKNOWN.
+
+## Contract
+
+Fix an observed condition c and let N independent, identically prepared modules
+have joint state rho_XE, where X=RS includes the donor's tracked reference R.
+The physical exchange permutes S; logical reference reassignment follows its
+donor, so the retained logical X includes R from the same original module.
+Environment registers remain in place. The joint physical implementation must
+be the intended exchange on the relevant joint states, within any separately
+justified error. Reduced gate characterization does not establish this premise.
+
+Let pi(i) be the donor delivered to recipient i. For a retained set T of k sites,
+put D=pi(T) and m=|T intersect D|. No independence assumption between X and E
+inside an original module is made. Finite-dimensional registers suffice below;
+the entropy conclusions extend when all displayed entropies are finite.
+
+## Theorem 1: exact state and information
+
+Up to relabeling tensor factors, the retained state is exactly
+
+    rho_T = (tensor over j in T intersect D of rho_(X_j E_j))
+            tensor (tensor over j in D minus T of rho_(X_j))
+            tensor (tensor over j in T minus D of rho_(E_j)).
+
+The X_j factor is placed in the logical output whose donor is j. Consequently,
+
+    I(X_D : E_T)_(rho_T) = m I(X:E)_rho.
+

+"""Finite corroboration of the analytic routing theorem, not hardware evidence."""
+from fractions import Fraction
+from itertools import permutations, product
+from pathlib import Path
+import json
+import numpy as np
+
+
+def partial_trace(rho, dims, keep):
+    rest = tuple(i for i in range(len(dims)) if i not in keep)
+    order = tuple(keep) + rest
+    dk = int(np.prod([dims[i] for i in keep]))
+    dr = int(np.prod([dims[i] for i in rest]))
+    a = rho.reshape(dims + dims).transpose(order + tuple(i+len(dims) for i in order))
+    return np.trace(a.reshape(dk, dr, dk, dr), axis1=1, axis2=3)
+
+
+def entropy(rho):
+    ev = np.linalg.eigvalsh((rho+rho.conj().T)/2)
+    ev = ev[ev > 1e-14]
+    return float(-np.dot(ev, np.log(ev)))
+
+
+def run():
+    cases = 0
+    for n in range(1, 6):
+        assignments = list(product((0, 1), repeat=n))
+        for pi in permutations(range(n)):
+            for mask in range(1 << n):
+                keep = [i for i in range(n) if mask >> i & 1]
+                donors = {pi[i] for i in keep}
+                m = len(donors.intersection(keep))
+                ea = Fraction(sum(sum(z[pi[i]] for i in keep) for z in assignments), 2**n)
+                eb = Fraction(sum(sum(z[i] for i in keep) for z in assignments), 2**n)
+                eab = Fraction(sum(sum(z[pi[i]] for i in keep)*sum(z[i] for i in keep)
+                                   for z in assignments), 2**n)
+                assert eab-ea*eb == Fraction(m, 4)
+                assert m >= max(0, 2*len(keep)-n)
+                cases += 1
+
+    rng = np.random.default_rng(20261015)
+    a = rng.normal(size=(4, 4))+1j*rng.normal(size=(4, 4))
+    rho = a@a.conj().T
+    rho /= np.trace(rho)
+    rx = partial_trace(rho, (2, 2), (0,))
+    re = partial_trace(rho, (2, 2), (1,))
+    mutual = entropy(rx)+entropy(re)-entropy(rho)
+    max_error = 0.0
+    quantum_cases = 0
+    for n, pi in ((2, (1, 0)), (3, (1, 2, 0)), (4, (1, 0, 3, 2)), (3, (0, 2, 1))):
+        full = np.array([[1.+0j]])
+        for _ in range(n):
+            full = np.kron(full, rho)
+        for mask in range(1, 1 << n):
+            keep = [i for i in range(n) if mask >> i & 1]
+            k = len(keep)
+            dims = (2, 2)*n
+            indices = tuple(j for i in keep for j in (2*pi[i], 2*i+1))
+            out = partial_trace(full, dims, indices)
+            m = len(set(keep).intersection(pi[i] for i in keep))
+            f = sum(pi[i] == i for i in keep)
+            sx = entropy(partial_trace(out, (2, 2)*k, tuple(range(0, 2*k, 2))))
+            se = entropy(partial_trace(out, (2, 2)*k, tuple(range(1, 2*k, 2))))
+            cross = sx+se-entropy(out)
+            local_sum = sum(entropy(partial_trace(out, (2, 2)*k, (2*j, 2*j+1))) for j in range(k))
+            total = local_sum-entropy(out)
+            errors = (abs(cross-m*mutual), abs(total-(m-f)*mutual))
+            max_error = max(max_error, *errors)
+            assert max(errors) < 3e-12, (n, pi, keep, errors)
+            quantum_cases += 1
+    return {"status": "passed", "classical_exhaustive_cases": cases,
+            "classical_scope": "all permutations and retained subsets, N=1..5, iid fair bits; exact Fraction covariance",
+            "quantum_cases": quantum_cases, "quantum_maximum_entropy_identity_error": max_error,
+            "quantum_scope": "selected N=2..4 permutations and all nonempty subsets, one seeded mixed qubit-pair state",
+            "evidence_limit": "finite mathematical checks only; analytic theorem proved in ROUTING_CORRELATION_THEOREM.md; no physical or novelty validation"}
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    result = run()
+    target = Path(__file__).with_name("ROUTING_CORRELATION_CHECK.json")
+    target.write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2)+"\n")
+    print(json.dumps(result, indent=2))
