# Selective primary-source proof receipts
+
+Read date: 15 October 2026. Reconstructed conclusions are in `HEAT_TO_CRITICAL_TRACE.md`; source claims below are not silently promoted to externally verified mathematics. Acquired source hashes are in `source_manifest.json`.
+
+## A. Bruno-Pasqualotto: actual planar quartic heat proof
+
+Primary source: Giuseppe Bruno and Federico Pasqualotto, [Quasiconvexity for the Dacorogna-Marcellini Energy, arXiv:2608.06367v1](https://arxiv.org/html/2608.06367v1).
+
+Read: Section 2, Lemma 3 and its proof; Section 3, exact-form construction and corrected quadratic blocks; Appendix A, the three-coefficient invariant cone and displayed square identity. In the web rendering these are approximately lines 132-190, 191-346, 347-422. The local HTML source is retained.
+
+The source proves the Dacorogna-Marcellini threshold and the distinct class with both left and right rotational invariance. Its mechanism adds the pullback of an exact matrix-space two-form to the integrated heat second variation. It does not state a theorem for all nine coefficients with left rotational invariance alone. N794 already applies this method to a different explicit energy. The current transfer uses N794's strict margin, not the three-coefficient theorem as a substitute for the full cone.
+
+## B. OpenAI Math: actual matrix heat proof, not a title analogy
+
+Repository primary source: [openai/math at 1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a](https://github.com/openai/math/tree/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a).
+
+Read actual proof files in `preprints/The-maximal-triangular-Hilbert-transform-at-the-symmetric-point-September-24-2026/build/sections/`:
+
+- [`matrix.tex`](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-maximal-triangular-Hilbert-transform-at-the-symmetric-point-September-24-2026/build/sections/matrix.tex), lines 1-170: supported matrix Hessian and operator-order proof.
+- [`heat.tex`](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-maximal-triangular-Hilbert-transform-at-the-symmetric-point-September-24-2026/build/sections/heat.tex), lines 1-291: Gaussian-weighted stars, support preservation, heat identities, neighbor comparison, integrated dissipation proof.
+
+The energy is `Phi(P)=tr(P^(3/2))` on PSD Grams. Its Hessian is the supported inverse of `L_sqrt(P)+R_sqrt(P)`. Neighbor costs are compared by PSD order, then Gaussian centers are integrated on `p0+p1+p2=d`. This is a specific finite-matrix entropy calculation, not a rank-one-convex-gradient theorem. The named positive-Gram representation transfer to `Fstar` is explicitly refuted by its negative value at the identity. No conclusion about the full triangular-Hilbert manuscript's external correctness is claimed from this selective read.
+
+The full `trace.tex` file was acquired but not used as a premise. Its complete mixed-trace theorem was not independently audited here.
+
+## C. OpenAI Math: actual recursive-potential proof
+
+Read [`Midpoint-convexity-from-two-recursive-potentials-September-27-2026/build/sections/energy.tex`](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Midpoint-convexity-from-two-recursive-potentials-September-27-2026/build/sections/energy.tex), lines 1-75.
+
+The two-field lemma uses nonnegative fields `P,Q,P',Q'` whose squares dominate child sums, a common nonnegative defect `d=P'-P=Q'-Q`, and one tight unprimed field at each internal node. Its proof sets a cubic-defect energy to the power `2/3`, applies Holder to two child sums, and telescopes to boundary leaves. These hypotheses were not constructed from arbitrary profile gradients. The lemma cannot be transferred merely because both problems use a word such as potential or compensation. The representation remains an incompatible interface, not a refutation of the source lemma.
+
+Related constrained/free-root/linear tree files and the foundations/obstruction files were acquired for navigation. Their full proofs were not used.
+
+## D. CLMS primary manuscript and the missing quartic closure
+
+Primary source: R. Coifman, P.-L. Lions, Y. Meyer and S. Semmes, [Compacite par compensation et espaces de Hardy](https://www.numdam.org/item/SEDP_1989-1990____A16_0/), Seminaire EDP, expose XIV (28 November 1989), especially Theorem 1 on printed page XIV-2 and the proof sketches on XIV-4--XIV-5. This is an early primary account; the later journal article is not falsely reported as fully read.
+
+Theorem 1 places the Jacobian in real Hardy space under Sobolev exponent summability. The scanned formula was visually checked on PDF page 5 (zero-based page 4), rather than trusting the incomplete OCR. The integration-by-parts/div-curl proof sketch was read. Section 10 of the report gives an independent scaled counterexample to the extra global `H^1`-BMO norm-product closure. It does not challenge the primary theorem.
+
+## E. Flow interchange: exact applicability premises
+
+Primary author manuscript: D. Matthes, R. J. McCann and G. Savare, [A family of nonlinear fourth order equations of gradient flow type](https://www.math.utoronto.ca/mccann/papers/MattesMcCannSavare.pdf), Theorem 3.2 and proof, printed page 17, equations (3.19)-(3.27).
+
+The formula and proof were visually checked on PDF page 17 (zero-based page 16). The key comparison uses an actual minimizing-movement minimizer and its competitor evolved by an auxiliary EVI flow. Those assumptions do not follow from convexity in profile velocity. The result is background on method, not a positive premise of the trace theorem here.
+
+## F. Trace topology
+
+Primary source: Anatole Gaudin, [Homogeneous Sobolev and Besov spaces on special Lipschitz domains and their traces, arXiv:2305.01441v2](https://arxiv.org/html/2305.01441v2), Theorem 1.1 and discussion of the bounded-domain case.
+
+The stated trace of `H^(1,4)=W^(1,4)` is `B^(3/4)_(4,4)=W^(3/4,4)` in the admitted bounded Lipschitz setting. Periodic cylinder charts give the same local trace scale. The report supplies its own elementary convolution-extension upper estimate, so it does not rely on a homogeneous whole-space quotient convention or on an unspecified Poisson calibration. No priority claim is made for this standard trace scale.
+
+## G. Repository status and acquisition scope
+
+The OpenAI repository README says its manuscripts have varying verification status. Its source descriptions and proof artifacts are not an independent correctness or novelty stamp. The complete acquired preprints tree and contents map provided navigation. Selective reading found no valid theorem that closes the full nine-coefficient destination obligation. That is a statement about the inspected transfers, not exhaustive absence of useful mathematics in the repository.
+
+The positive transfer is consequently stated with the strict certificate from the pinned Astra source, whose algebra was replayed, and an explicit analytic proof supplied in this worker's report. Other collected texts are not counted as proofs read. No remote messages, repository changes, or publication actions were taken.

+ torch.manual_seed(seed);obj=fc.Cycle(N,K)
+ par=torch.randn(K,2*N+1,2,requires_grad=True)
+ B=(.05*torch.randn(4)).requires_grad_(True)

+=
+-\frac{\epsilon_0s\chi_{\mathrm{eff}}^{(2)}}{3}E^3.
+\]
+Apply phase-locked fields at \(\omega\) and \(2\omega\):
+\[
+E(t)=E_1\cos\omega t+E_2\cos(2\omega t+\phi),
+\]
+where \(E_1,E_2\) are peak internal field amplitudes. Direct cycle averaging gives
+\[
+\overline{E^3}
+=
+\frac34E_1^2E_2\cos\phi.
+\]
+Consequently,
+\[
+\overline{u_{\mathrm{NL},s}}
+=
+-\frac{\epsilon_0s\chi_{\mathrm{eff}}^{(2)}}4
+E_1^2E_2\cos\phi.
+\]
+The energy-density difference between the polarities acts as a pressure on their boundary:
+\[
+\boxed{
+p_\phi
+=
+\frac{\epsilon_0\chi_{\mathrm{eff}}^{(2)}}2
+E_1^2E_2\cos\phi
+}
+\]
+with its sign defined relative to the chosen direction of boundary advance.
+Changing \(\phi\) by \(\pi\) reverses the preferred polarity without changing either individual beam intensity.
+This is the useful feature. In the model, the control does not merely multiply all transition rates by a common factor. It changes the relative energetic preference for different structural outcomes.
+What is—and is not—new here
+The underlying two-color hyperpolarizability interaction is established physics. Phase-locked fundamental and second-harmonic fields have already been used to orient molecules; theoretical work explicitly analyzes the phase-dependent orienting potential. I am not claiming invention of that interaction. Frontiers
+The narrower proposed operation is:
+Use the reactive three-wave interaction to drive retained relocation or removal of a nonferroelectric crystal’s inversion boundary.
+
+The sources reviewed do not establish that complete operation. They also do not constitute exhaustive novelty clearance. A publication claim would require a more complete search of nonlinear-optical forces, optical poling, domain engineering and relevant patents.
+Geometry can eliminate the effect entirely
+The scalar notation must not conceal a zero tensor contraction. In conventional cubic axes, the relevant GaAs bulk coupling involves the three distinct Cartesian components. Thus, a simplistic normal-incidence arrangement on a (001) surface with both fields entirely in-plane does not supply the assumed bulk cubic interaction.
+A nonzero geometry must be designed from the actual tensor, internal field directions and optical boundary conditions. For example, the idealized combination of propagation along \([1\bar10]\) and polarization along \([111]\) permits a nonzero contraction; realizing those fields in a particular film or waveguide remains an optical-design obligation. This conclusion follows from the published tensor structure, not from assigning a favorable scalar susceptibility. arXiv
+3. Quantitative screening: the attractive symmetry does not guarantee useful force
+I evaluated the pressure scale using the following normalizations, not measured hot-GaAs operating parameters:
+\[
+\chi_{\mathrm{eff}}^{(2)}=100\ \mathrm{pm/V},
+\qquad
+n_\omega=n_{2\omega}=3.3,
+\qquad E_1=E_2=E.
+\]
+For each color,
+\[
+I=\frac12n\epsilon_0cE^2.
+\]
+The resulting values are:
+Peak internal field, each color	Phase-selective on-state pressure	Internal intensity, each color
+\(10^7\ \mathrm{V/m}\)	\(0.443\ \mathrm{Pa}\)	\(0.0438\ \mathrm{GW/cm^2}\)
+\(10^8\ \mathrm{V/m}\)	\(443\ \mathrm{Pa}\)	\(4.38\ \mathrm{GW/cm^2}\)
+\(3\times10^8\ \mathrm{V/m}\)	\(11.95\ \mathrm{kPa}\)	\(39.4\ \mathrm{GW/cm^2}\)
+
+
+These are calculated scales under the stated approximation. The intensities are internal traveling-wave-equivalent intensities; they are not automatically equal to the external power required by a resonator.
+The important finding is nevertheless clear: substantial internal fields produce relatively modest mechanical pressures.
+The short-pulse implementation has a severe duty-cycle problem
+Consider rectangular 100 fs pulses at 1 MHz. Their duty fraction is
+\[
+D=10^{-7}.
+\]
+For an isothermal boundary with a linear overdamped response, the relevant average optical pressure at the middle field level is
+\[
+\overline p
+=
+Dp_{\mathrm{peak}}
+=
+4.43\times10^{-5}\ \mathrm{Pa}.
+\]
+The average internal intensity is still approximately \(438\ \mathrm{W/cm^2}\) per color.
+As a declared first target—not an achieved performance—suppose a boundary must traverse \(1\,\mu\mathrm m\) in 600 s. With \(v=Mp\), and optimistically neglecting opposing forces and pinning, the required mobility is
+\[
+M_{\mathrm{req}}
+=
+\frac{10^{-6}}{600\,p}.
+\]
+For continuous application of \(443\) Pa,
+\[
+M_{\mathrm{req}}
+=
+3.76\times10^{-12}\ \mathrm{m^4/(J\,s)}.
+\]
+For the specified pulsed exposure,
+\[
+M_{\mathrm{req,pulsed}}
+=
+3.76\times10^{-5}\ \mathrm{m^4/(J\,s)}.
+\]
+No measured boundary mobility has been supplied that validates either target. The seven-order-of-magnitude pulse penalty is an exact consequence of this particular linear, fixed-temperature model.
+I would reject the argument that a large femtosecond peak field, by itself, makes this a promising boundary-rewriting actuator. Nonlinear activated motion could change the conclusion, but it must be acquired rather than presumed.
+For example, in a simplified single-path Arrhenius model, doubling the time-averaged rate through a duty-\(D\) barrier reduction requires
+\[
+D\left[
+\exp\left(\frac{p\Delta V^\ddagger}{k_BT}\right)-1
+\right]\ge 1.
+\]
+At \(650\,^\circ\mathrm C\), \(p=443\) Pa and \(D=10^{-7}\), this requires
+\[
+\Delta V^\ddagger
+\gtrsim
+4.64\times10^{-22}\ \mathrm{m^3}.
+\]
+That is an unmeasured collective activation volume, not evidence that such a cooperative transition exists. It specifies how demanding the proposed kinetic rescue would be.
+“Below the bandgap” does not mean “negligible loss”
+Hurlbut and colleagues measured two- and three-photon absorption in GaAs across the mid-infrared using 100 fs pulses. Later measurements and modeling also explicitly include free-carrier absorption generated by multiphoton excitation. PubMed
+One useful warning comes from the tabulated GaAs three-photon coefficient at \(2.3\,\mu\mathrm m\):
+\[
+\alpha_3=0.35\ \mathrm{cm^3/GW^2},
+\]
+credited to Hurlbut’s measurements in the later comparison. At \(I=4.38\ \mathrm{GW/cm^2}\), this term alone corresponds to an effective on-state attenuation coefficient
+\[
+\alpha_3I^2\simeq6.71\ \mathrm{cm^{-1}}.
+\]
+Thus, even an optically thin layer can absorb substantial power at the required intensity. This is not a hot-material loss prediction; it is evidence against treating a sub-bandgap beam as lossless. arXiv
+The temperature mismatch is central. The demonstrated boundary dissolution uses hot GaAs. Published analysis shows that the two-photon and free-carrier absorption depend on temperature, wavelength and carrier state. A room-temperature optical coefficient cannot simply be paired with high-temperature structural mobility. AIP Publishing
+Moving to longer wavelengths may change the balance. It does not establish a solution without measuring the resulting nonlinear coupling, carrier absorption and both-beam losses in the same regime.
+4. The coupled physical model—not an independently optimized machine
+The scalar pressure formula is an explanatory limit. A frequency-dispersive implementation should instead be formulated through a calibrated interaction Hamiltonian.
+Let \(X\) describe boundary position, and let \(a,b\) be optical modes at \(\omega,2\omega\). A candidate conservative coupling is
+\[
+H_{\mathrm{int}}
+=
+\hbar\left[
+g(X)b^\dagger a^2+
+g^*(X)b(a^\dagger)^2
+\right].
+\]
+The boundary changes the spatial overlap of the sign-changing nonlinear response with the optical fields. For coherent amplitudes \(\alpha,\beta\),
+\[
+F_X
+=
+-2\hbar\operatorname{Re}
+\left[g'(X)\beta^*\alpha^2\right].
+\]
+This is the force expression to calibrate or derive microscopically. Substituting an arbitrary tabulated second-harmonic coefficient into the earlier scalar formula is not a substitute for that calculation.
+The optical amplitudes themselves respond to the interaction:
+\[
+\dot\alpha
+=
+(i\Delta_1-\kappa_1/2)\alpha
+-i2g^*\alpha^*\beta
++\sqrt{\kappa_{1e}}\,s_1,
+\]
+\[
+\dot\beta
+=
+(i\Delta_2-\kappa_2/2)\beta
+-ig\alpha^2
++\sqrt{\kappa_{2e}}\,s_2.
+\]
+Here \(\Delta_j\) are detunings, \(\kappa_j\) total loss rates, and \(s_j\) external drives. These quantities can depend on temperature, carriers and the evolving structure.
+The material evolution must simultaneously include a boundary law and heat/carrier balance. Schematically,
+\[
+\dot X
+=
+\mathcal V
+\left(
+p_\phi+p_{\mathrm{capillary}}+p_{\mathrm{stress}},
+T,n,\text{pinning and history}
+\right),
+\]
+\[
+C_V\dot T
+=
+\nabla\!\cdot(k\nabla T)
++
+q_{\mathrm{abs}}(\alpha,\beta,T,n)
++
+q_{\mathrm{diss}},
+\]
+\[
+\dot n
+=
+G_{\mathrm{abs}}(\alpha,\beta,T,n)-R(n,T).
+\]
+These equations expose the missing joint acquisition rather than filling it with favorable numbers.
+Several consequences follow.
+A cavity is not an absorption exemption. It can reduce external drive power for a given internal field, but the material still absorbs at that field. Its hot loaded quality factor, both-color resonance conditions and moving-boundary detuning must be included.
+Reactive interaction is not free work. Even at a phase where stationary frequency conversion is suppressed, the field phases and stored interaction energy respond to boundary motion. Mechanical work and losses must be supplied through the optical drive and other energy sources.
+The phase bias need not be spatially uniform. Propagation introduces a relative phase involving \(k_{2\omega}-2k_\omega\). The force can vary or reverse across the sample. A thin region or a properly measured mode-overlap design is required; uniform bulk pressure cannot be assumed.
+A useful conditional optimization result
+At fixed temperature, carrier state, wavelength and beam ratio, suppose the measured local behavior can be represented by
+\[
+p=A I^{3/2},
+\qquad
+q_{\mathrm{abs}}=aI+bI^2+cI^3,
+\]
+with nonnegative loss coefficients.
+Then
+\[
+\frac{p}{q_{\mathrm{abs}}}
+=
+\frac{A\sqrt I}{a+bI+cI^2}.
+\]
+For \(a>0\), an interior optimum satisfies
+\[
+\boxed{a-bI-3cI^2=0.}
+\]
+This is not a full process optimum: mobility, temperature, carriers and damage may change with intensity. It does show why “increase the field” is not an unlimited remedy once nonlinear absorption matters.
+The optimization must ultimately concern retained useful transformation per total input—not pressure alone.
+5. The strongest competitor is not necessarily optical
+There are two already serious practical baselines: optimized dark annealing and growth that prevents the boundaries. Both have published GaAs demonstrations. Springer
+There is also a less obvious physical comparator.
+GaAs is piezoelectric. Opposite polarities reverse the piezoelectric tensor, so a combined electric field and mechanical stress can also distinguish them. Interferometric measurements reported a GaAs \(d_{14}\) coefficient of approximately \(-2.7\) pm/V. figshare.mq.edu.au
+For an appropriately chosen tensor contraction, the mixed electromechanical interaction has the form
+\[
+g_s^{\mathrm{em}}
+=
+-sd_{\mathrm{eff}}E\sigma,
+\]
+giving a polarity pressure difference
+\[
+p_{\mathrm{em}}
+=
+2d_{\mathrm{eff}}E\sigma.
+\]
+Using \(|d_{\mathrm{eff}}|=2.7\) pm/V as an illustrative normalization,
+\[
+E=10^6\ \mathrm{V/m},
+\qquad
+\sigma=10^8\ \mathrm{Pa}
+\]
+gives
+\[
+p_{\mathrm{em}}\approx540\ \mathrm{Pa}.
+\]
+That is comparable to the middle optical-pressure example.
+This is not a validated alternative process either. The reported coefficient is not a hot-annealing measurement; electrical leakage, screening, stress-induced defects and the compatible field geometry must be assessed. Nevertheless, it invalidates the assumption that coherent light is the only available polarity-conjugate actuator.
+The optical route should advance only if it offers something this alternative cannot provide at acceptable cost—for example, genuinely useful contactless spatial control—not merely because its phase dependence is interesting.
+6. The decisive experiment: retained, phase-selected structure
+The experiment should be designed to distinguish two claims:
+1. A phase-dependent intervention changes boundary behavior.
+2. The proposed reactive optical pressure produces a retained useful transformation.
+The first is not sufficient evidence for the second.
+Establish the operating window before attempting a device
+Use a specimen with an independently mapped boundary and a physically available exit or annihilation path. Measure the two-color nonlinear response, absorbed power, local temperature, carrier response and boundary kinetics under the same conditions.
+A boundary anchored by its topology or interface registry cannot be treated as a freely translating wall. Nor can an overall decrease in boundary density be converted into a universal directional mobility.
+For the illustrative \(1\,\mu\mathrm m\)-in-600-s target, the measured response must support the required displacement while remaining within the sample’s thermal, optical and mechanical limits. If it does not, stop that implementation.
+Randomize phase and controls on comparable initial structures
+Use matched regions or specimens rather than assuming that reversing the phase on an irreversibly altered boundary reproduces the original initial condition.
+Compare phase settings separated by \(\pi\), a quadrature setting, loss of mutual coherence, each color separately and optimized dark annealing. Include the stress–electric-field comparator when experimentally compatible.
+The reactive-pressure model predicts a specific phase dependence, field-amplitude scaling and tensor dependence. Its coupling should be determined independently of the final boundary-displacement fit.
+Equal incident intensities do not establish equal heating or equal carrier excitation. A phase-dependent absorption pathway could mimic phase-selected motion. Temperature, absorption, carriers and strain must be measured sufficiently well to exclude that explanation—or the observed mechanism must be relabeled rather than claimed as confirmation of conservative optical pressure.
+Demand the complete endpoint after field removal
+The success criterion should be a predeclared region acquiring the selected polarity after illumination and annealing cease, with retention over a relevant time and temperature interval.
+Structural assessment must check for residual boundaries, unwanted faults, stoichiometric changes, cracks and displaced damage in a surrounding guard region. Optical polarity mapping can guide the assay, but an altered nonlinear optical signal alone does not establish atomic repair.
+The same region must then pass an application-relevant functional test. That might concern electrical transport, recombination or a deliberately specified optical response. The test must not assume that one favorable structural count guarantees all useful properties.
+Finally, report total electrical input to lasers, heating, cooling and stabilization, together with processing time, affected volume and yield. Compare equivalent final quality—not unequal intermediate signals.
+A successful experiment would therefore establish phase-selected, retained manufacturing control, not merely another pump–probe effect.
+7. Does this qualify as an Astra flagship direction?
+Not yet.
+The positive result is a concrete route from a measured symmetry-sensitive interaction to an outcome-selective force. Its direction is not an arbitrary fitted “repair selectivity.” The candidate also has a real structural precedent in its first proposed material.
+The negative results are equally consequential. The simple short-pulse implementation has a severe duty-cycle penalty. Strong internal fields need not provide strong boundary pressure. The hot structural regime and the optical-loss regime have not been qualified together. Existing growth and annealing methods already set a demanding baseline, and an electromechanical actuator could supply a comparable symmetry-selective bias.
+A successful GaAs experiment would establish a narrow physical capability. It would not establish a general atom assembler, arbitrary defect repair, an energy-generation technology or a path to civilization-scale manufacturing by itself.
+The broader hypothesis worth retaining is more precise:
+A structural distinction invisible to ordinary linear driving may become controllable through an externally imposed field product that couples to a sign-changing material response.
+
+For that to become a major manufacturing principle, the material must simultaneously possess a sufficiently strong response, an accessible structural pathway, tolerable losses and a useful retained endpoint. Transfer to another material requires reacquiring those conditions; shared symmetry is not enough.
+My present decision is to retain phase-directed polarity rewriting as a falsifiable mechanism, but not promote the GaAs optical implementation as a breakthrough or build a larger apparatus concept around it. The decisive missing result is a same-regime measurement showing that the available phase-selective bias can complete a useful retained transformation faster, more selectively or at lower total cost than the strongest compatible alternative.
+The literature establishes relevant ingredients and serious competitors. It does not establish their coexistence in that successful operation.

# Exact retained-workload correlations under reference-tracked exchange
+
+Date: 15 October 2026 (Australia/Brisbane). Internally derived by the root
+researcher; historical originality and external review are UNKNOWN.
+
+## Contract
+
+Fix an observed condition c and let N independent, identically prepared modules
+have joint state rho_XE, where X=RS includes the donor's tracked reference R.
+The physical exchange permutes S; logical reference reassignment follows its
+donor, so the retained logical X includes R from the same original module.
+Environment registers remain in place. The joint physical implementation must
+be the intended exchange on the relevant joint states, within any separately
+justified error. Reduced gate characterization does not establish this premise.
+
+Let pi(i) be the donor delivered to recipient i. For a retained set T of k sites,
+put D=pi(T) and m=|T intersect D|. No independence assumption between X and E
+inside an original module is made. Finite-dimensional registers suffice below;
+the entropy conclusions extend when all displayed entropies are finite.
+
+## Theorem 1: exact state and information
+
+Up to relabeling tensor factors, the retained state is exactly
+
+    rho_T = (tensor over j in T intersect D of rho_(X_j E_j))
+            tensor (tensor over j in D minus T of rho_(X_j))
+            tensor (tensor over j in T minus D of rho_(E_j)).
+
+The X_j factor is placed in the logical output whose donor is j. Consequently,
+
+    I(X_D : E_T)_(rho_T) = m I(X:E)_rho.
+
+In particular, all retained data jointly decorrelate from all retained
+environments exactly when m=0, unless rho was already a product. For a
+derangement pi, every individual retained site has state rho_X tensor rho_E,
+yet the total correlation among the k output *sites* is
+
+    sum_(i in T) S(X_pi(i) E_i) - S(rho_T) = m I(X:E)_rho.
+
+For T equal to all sites this is N I(X:E), and the global data/environment
+mutual information is unchanged. Exchange relocates these correlations.
+
+Proof. Each original module contributes either both its factors, only X, only
+E, or neither to the partial trace. Independence of original modules gives the
+displayed tensor factorization. Additivity of entropy gives
+
+    S(rho_T)=m S(XE)+(k-m)[S(X)+S(E)],
+    S(X_D)=k S(X),    S(E_T)=k S(E).
+
+Subtracting yields the mutual information identity. For a derangement each
+one-site marginal is a product, which proves the total-correlation identity.
+The tensor factorization, rather than a finite numerical check, is the proof.
+
+If fixed points are allowed, the cross-partition mutual information is still
+m I(X:E), but total correlation among sites is (m-f) I(X:E), where f is the
+number of fixed points in T. A fixed point keeps correlation inside its site.
+
+## Theorem 2: sharp routing reservoir overhead
+
+For fixed registers with dim X>=2 and dim E>=2, routing to produce k jointly
+independent product-marginal outputs for every unknown rho_XE requires
+N >= 2k, and that bound is sufficient. This statement also holds for randomized
+routing selected independently of all input modules, even when the route
+record is forgotten. If either register is one-dimensional, every input is
+already product and the necessity statement does not apply.
+
+Sufficiency: use k recipient modules and k disjoint donor modules, exchange
+each pair, and retain one endpoint of each pair. Reference tracking preserves
+each donor RS marginal, including its internal entanglement. The retained
+outputs are rho_X tensor rho_E independently. The other endpoints carry the
+complementary correlations and are discarded from the workload.
+
+Necessity: choose the classical state X_j=E_j=Z_j with independent fair bits
+Z_j. Define A=sum_(i in T) X_pi(i), B=sum_(i in T) E_i. Then exactly
+
+    Cov(A,B)=|T intersect pi(T)|/4.
+
+Averaging over independently randomized routing gives E[m]/4 because both
+conditional means equal k/2. The ideal product target has covariance zero, so
+m must vanish almost surely. Disjoint k-element T and pi(T) require N>=2k.
+For fixed retained sets the pigeonhole lower bound m>=max(0,2k-N) also gives
+
+    Cov(A,B) >= max(0,2k-N)/4.
+
+This proof is a routing-class impossibility. A separate worker supplies a
+stronger polynomial-degree bound for arbitrary fixed quantum instruments.
+Independent same-team review identified the explicit nontrivial-dimension and
+input-independent-routing qualifications above. The initial authored draft is
+retained as ROUTING_CORRELATION_THEOREM_v0001.txt; the current statement includes
+these qualifications. Neither draft is externally certified.
+
+## Workload interpretation and conditional matching
+
+One X or E can contain an entire internally correlated workload. Swapping
+between two independent condition-matched workload modules preserves the
+donor's full data/reference state and replaces its associated environment.
+The theorem does not require independent qubits or a microscopic bath model
+inside a workload. It does require independent whole workload preparations,
+matched continuation, and a bound on collateral environmental action.
+
+Conditional matching applies separately for each c. Retaining floor(N_c/2)
+outputs per condition can change the condition distribution. Thus neither this
+construction nor postselection silently preserves the population p_c. Use
+predeclared strata with correct target weights, or report the actual routed
+intervention and its weights. Acquisition of rare conditions, buffers,
+reference storage, reset and all discarded modules must be charged.
+
+This result clarifies the distinction between a one-site causal assay and a
+joint workload. It does not establish a new laboratory operation or advantage
+over direct randomized controller testing. Local continuation/readout permits
+less conservative estimation than a general joint workload; that is a distinct
+dependency-graph question, investigated separately.
+
+## Prior art and verification boundary
+
+Two-copy subsystem recombination is established prior art, including the
+experimental cavity-QED study by Coeuret Cauquil et al. (2026):
+https://arxiv.org/html/2601.07011v2 . Its existence precludes a claim to have
+invented product-marginal recombination. The result here is an explicit
+retained-subset accounting and operational resource boundary for the supplied
+reference-tracked construction. Historical priority for these formulations has
+not been established.
+
+The checker verify_routing_correlations.py exhaustively enumerates small
+classical routing cases and tests quantum entropy identities for selected mixed
+states. Those checks corroborate formulas; they do not establish physical
+obtainability, independent correctness or novelty.
+

# An unconditional concentration bound for condition-matched local exchange scores
+
+Root derivation, 15 October 2026. The independent quantum-information worker
+derived the pair/triple compiler and conditional component bound; the root
+supplied the random-label bounded-difference step below. Both reconstructed the
+combined argument. This is same-team analytic work, not external validation.
+
+## Exact scope
+
+Each arm prepares B independent batches of N iid labeled modules. Conditional
+on the full label vector, modules are independent and their joint RSE state
+depends only on their observed condition c. All gate components, continuation
+channels and readouts act locally to their declared components and introduce
+no shared noise. Each endpoint score is in [0,1]. The bath-safe joint routing,
+reference tracking, matched continuation and readout assumptions of the source
+remain required. None is inferred from this sampling proof.
+
+Within a condition class of size k>=2, use disjoint swaps for even k and one
+3-cycle plus disjoint swaps for odd k. Singletons remain untouched. Every
+non-singleton moves and has exactly the source's conditional product marginal.
+For each condition, denote the native and routed local score means by o_c,d_c
+in [0,1]. These values need not be known to use the bound.
+
+The tested target is the actual unconditional *finite-batch* routing score,
+not the ideal infinite-reservoir score. Systematic errors and any inference
+from finite batch to ideal decorrelation are separate from sampling error.
+
+## Conditional measurement fluctuations
+
+For fixed labels the disjoint components are independent. A component of size
+g in {1,2,3} has total score in [0,g], even when its endpoints are correlated.
+Write S for the score averaged over all BN endpoints. Hoeffding's exponential
+bound, conditional on the labels, gives
+
+    E[exp(lambda (S-E[S|labels])) | labels]
+      <= exp(lambda^2 sum_components g^2 / (8 B^2 N^2))
+      <= exp(3 lambda^2/(8BN)).
+
+The second inequality uses g^2<=3g and sum g=BN. Independent endpoints are
+never assumed. More precise realized component counts improve this term.
+
+## Random-label fluctuations
+
+For one batch the conditional mean is
+
+    mu(labels)= (1/N) sum_c h_c(k_c),
+    h_c(0)=0, h_c(1)=o_c, h_c(k)=k d_c for k>=2.
+
+Its increment on adding one member to a class is
+
+    h_c(1)-h_c(0)=o_c in [0,1],
+    h_c(2)-h_c(1)=2d_c-o_c in [-1,2],
+    h_c(k+1)-h_c(k)=d_c in [0,1] for k>=2.
+
+Changing one label removes one member from a class and adds one to another.
+Therefore it changes the conditional batch mean by at most 3/N. This constant
+is attainable with two classes initially of sizes2 and1: take native/routed
+means (1,0) and (0,1), and move one member from the former to the latter.
+
+The B-batch conditional mean, as a function of BN independent labels, has
+bounded differences 3/(BN). The Doob-martingale exponential bound gives
+
+    E[exp(lambda(E[S|labels]-E S))] <= exp(9 lambda^2/(8BN)).
+
+For completeness, both exponential bounds use only the elementary bounded
+variable lemma log E exp(lambda(Z-E Z)) <=lambda^2(b-a)^2/8 for Z in[a,b].
+To prove it, twice differentiate the log moment-generating function; its
+second derivative is the variance under exponential tilting, at most
+(b-a)^2/4. Integrate twice from zero. The label bound applies that lemma to
+Doob increments, each of whose conditional range is at most the corresponding
+bounded difference. Thus no unexplained concentration theorem is a premise.
+
+## Combined result
+
+Condition first on labels and then average the two exponential bounds:
+
+    E exp(lambda(S-E S)) <= exp(12 lambda^2/(8BN)).
+
+Chernoff optimization for both signs yields
+
+    Pr(|S-E S|>=r) <= 2 exp(-BN r^2/6).
+
+For four predeclared arms, a union bound gives the simultaneous per-arm radius
+
+    r4 = sqrt(6 log(8/delta)/(BN)).
+
+Each two-arm contrast has radius2r4. One can use the smaller of this and the
+source's independent-batch radius sqrt(log(8/delta)/(2B)); the new bound is
+smaller when N>12. With B=4000,N=32,delta=.05, the new per-arm radius is about
+0.015424 versus .025187 for the batch-only bound. This is a sufficient analytic
+bound under stronger explicit local-component assumptions. It is neither a
+measured shot requirement nor a demonstrated advantage over other assays.
+
+The number of transpositions per class is ceil(k/2), minimal among
+derangements: a permutation with no fixed points has at most floor(k/2)
+cycles, and its minimum transposition count is k minus its cycle count.
+This reduces gate count relative to one long cycle without changing the
+source's tagged mean. Bath action, parallel hardware, resets, reference
+storage and acquisition costs remain charged.
+
+## Limits and falsifiers
+
+A joint cross-component continuation, common detector or gate noise, dependent
+source preparations, unmodeled adaptive policy selection, or nonlocal score
+can invalidate this factorization. Treat independent whole batches as the
+sampling units until the stronger locality/independence contract is justified.
+The actual tested score includes reference assignment and can change purely
+because reference partners changed; the separate reference-pairing
+counterexample must accompany any causal interpretation.
+

# Scoped proofs for conditional exchange robustness
+
+Worker: exchange_robustness. Date: 2026-10-15. Repository pin:
+`00631610750c708263d5cf6d812ebbb8edc77335`.
+
+These are internal finite-dimensional derivations. No independent external
+mathematical or physical validation and no historical novelty claim is made.
+The wire-cutting identity in Section 5 is established prior art, reconstructed
+here to give an explicit comparator/resource tradeoff.
+
+## 1. Exact reconstruction of the incoming operation
+
+Write the native cq state as
+
+\[
+ \rho_{CRSE}=\sum_c p_c|c\rangle\langle c|\otimes\rho^c_{RSE},
+ \quad \sigma_c=\rho^c_{RS},\quad \tau_c=\rho^c_E.
+\]
+
+For independent joint copies i,j, a local permutation of their S registers
+gives tagged marginal \(\sigma_c\otimes\tau_c\) on donor reference R_j,
+recipient data S_i, recipient environment E_i. This is just the original
+cross marginal \(\rho_{R_jS_jE_i}\), with S_j moved to S_i. Independence
+factorizes that marginal. The donor, rather than recipient, C label follows
+the job and reference.
+
+For N iid copies, cyclically route each condition group of size at least two;
+leave singleton groups native. A tagged condition-c copy is unmatched iff
+the other N-1 records avoid c. Thus exactly
+
+\[
+ \rho_N=\sum_c p_c |c\rangle\langle c|\otimes
+ [ (1-p_c)^{N-1}\rho^c_{RSE}
+  +(1-(1-p_c)^{N-1})\sigma_c\otimes\tau_c].
+\]
+
+With trace distance normalized by 1/2, its distance from complete conditional
+grafting is at most \(s_N(C)=\sum_cp_c(1-p_c)^{N-1}\). Every [0,1] task score
+inherits this bound; a two-policy difference inherits twice the bound.
+None of these statements makes the whole output batch independent.
+
+The source's phase model with hidden bit X~Bernoulli(u), RS Bell phase X,
+and future controlled-Z has native echo success 1 and independent graft
+success \((1-u)^2+u^2\). Sharing X between copies leaves echo success 1.
+An extra bath X gate is invisible to reduced SWAP characterization but can
+change future success from 1 to 0 even on an initially product input.
+
+## 2. Matching on the task-relevant quotient of the record
+
+Let Z=f(C) be a declared deterministic coarsening; \(q_z=\Pr(Z=z)\) and
+\(\bar\tau_z=\sum_{c:f(c)=z}p(c|z)\tau_c\). Draw N iid joint preparations.
+Route S within Z groups by a fixed index-based derangement (e.g. a cycle),
+leaving singleton groups native. Selection may depend on Z and independent
+routing randomness, but not on the fine C values within a group or on any
+unrecorded variable. Attach the full donor C and original donor R to the
+transferred job. Sites and continuation operations are interchangeable.
+
+**Exact finite-batch theorem.** The tagged output is
+
+\[
+ \rho_N^Z=\sum_c p_c|c\rangle\langle c|\otimes
+ [a_{f(c)}\rho^c_{RSE}+(1-a_{f(c)})\sigma_c\otimes\bar\tau_{f(c)}],
+ \qquad a_z=(1-q_z)^{N-1}.                                      \tag{1}
+\]
+
+**Proof.** Condition on the tagged donor's fine record c and all coarse
+records. If its coarse group is a singleton, its joint state is unchanged.
+Otherwise its recipient is a distinct index selected without inspecting
+the fine records. The recipient's fine record has distribution p(c'|z),
+independent of the donor's joint state. The recipient environment marginal
+is therefore \(\bar\tau_z\). Averaging the singleton event proves (1).
+The argument works for any fixed cycle length, and does not require product
+states inside a replica. QED.
+
+If \(\tau_c=\bar\tau_{f(c)}\) for every c, the only difference from complete
+fine-C grafting is singleton mass \(s_N(Z)=\sum_zq_z(1-q_z)^{N-1}\). Both the
+fine CRS and fine CE marginals are then preserved. The condition does not
+require the donor RS states to agree within a coarse group.
+
+There is a weaker, task-only version. Let \(\Lambda_a^\tau\) denote the
+continuation channel S->S' with initial independent environment state tau.
+R is idle; its dimension and its entanglement with S are unrestricted. The
+policy a may include a full predeclared continuation sequence. A finite
+menu may contain the fine-record-dependent policies used in scoring.
+Suppose, for every scored policy and each relevant c,
+
+\[
+ \Lambda_a^{\tau_c}=\Lambda_a^{\bar\tau_{f(c)}}.                 \tag{2}
+\]
+
+Then every tagged reference-inclusive task score equals the full fine-C
+graft score, apart from singleton mass \(s_N(Z)\). Equation (2) follows from
+equality of normalized Choi states, so it can in principle be tested using
+system-only causal-break channel probes on a fixed finite policy menu;
+full bath-state tomography is unnecessary. Such testing still requires
+certified local replacement operations and enough support/precision in C.
+Infinitely many or unique fine records do not come with a free certificate.
+
+For approximate matching put
+\(\eta_{a,c}=\frac12\|\Lambda_a^{\tau_c}-
+\Lambda_a^{\bar\tau_{f(c)}}\|_\diamond\). Then, for a [0,1] effect on RS',
+
+\[
+ |F_a(\rho_N^Z)-F_a(\mathcal G_C(\rho))|
+ \le s_N(Z)+\sum_c p_c(1-a_{f(c)})\eta_{a,c}.                  \tag{3}
+\]
+
+**Proof.** Apply (1). On singleton branches use the [0,1] range. On matched
+branches the diamond definition applies to the arbitrary reference-bearing
+input \(\sigma_c\). Average the bounds. QED.
+
+For d-dimensional S and normalized Choi states J, the sufficient bound
+\(\eta_{a,c}\le(d/2)\|J_a^{\tau_c}-J_a^{\bar\tau_z}\|_1\) gives one finite
+acquisition interface; uncertainty of the Choi estimates must be included.
+Its tomography cost depends on d and output dimension and the policy menu,
+not on a declared bath Hilbert-space size. It is not generally cheap.
+
+Equation (2) preserves selected task response, not the full fine CE
+marginal. If two conditional baths differ only on a spectator that never
+couples during the selected future, they may be task-equivalent and remain
+different physical states. A null task response is not global memorylessness.
+
+**Explicit removal of the rare-record obstruction.** Let C=(Z,U), with Z
+fair and U an independently generated 128-bit nonce. Suppose E's conditional
+marginal depends only on Z. U may select arbitrary genuinely local unitaries
+on S, so the RS states need not coincide. For N=32,
+
+\[
+ s_N(C)=(1-2^{-129})^{31}\ge1-31\,2^{-129},\qquad
+ s_N(Z)=2^{-31}\simeq4.657\times10^{-10}.                       \tag{4}
+\]
+
+Fine-record matching is almost inert; coarse routing realizes the desired
+tagged fine-record graft to the small bound in (4). The nonce's independence
+can be supplied by the actual generation/causal design, rather than guessed
+from bath measurements. With genuinely informative fine records, condition
+coarsening is allowed only when (2) or an explicit error budget is acquired.
+
+### Approximate matching with continuous informative records
+
+The response certificate can be used without coarse bins. Suppose a known
+observed scalar t(c) lies in [a,b], and, uniformly over the scored policy
+menu and all relevant c,c', an acquired bound gives
+
+\[
+ \tfrac12\|\Lambda_a^{\tau_c}-\Lambda_a^{\tau_{c'}}\|_\diamond
+ \le L|t(c)-t(c')|.                                         \tag{4a}
+\]
+
+For even N, sort the batch by t and exchange adjacent pairs. Conditional on
+the complete fine record list, the copies remain independent under the iid
+joint preparation contract. Donor j then sees its recipient's tau rather
+than its own. By the diamond bound, the batch-mean expected score differs
+from the sample average of the ideal fine-C graft scores by at most
+
+\[
+ \frac{2L}{N}\sum_{k=1}^{N/2}(t_{(2k)}-t_{(2k-1)})
+ \le \frac{2L(b-a)}{N}.                                    \tag{4b}
+\]
+
+The paired intervals are disjoint subsets of [a,b], proving the second
+inequality. Averaging over the records gives the same bias bound against
+the population fine-C graft score. Every fine C may be unique almost surely;
+exact matching would be inert, whereas this protocol gives O(1/N) worst-case
+task bias and uses N/2 block SWAPs. For donor-specific policies a(c), the
+Lipschitz certificate must hold for each such policy with both compared bath
+states. For odd N, keeping one singleton adds at most 1/N to the stated
+even-batch upper bound; discarding it changes the target and is not assumed.
+
+The same proof covers simultaneous upper confidence edge costs and a
+minimum-cost permutation, provided the edge certificate is valid for all
+candidate matches and route selection does not inspect hidden replica
+states. This is ordinary assignment optimization, not an algorithmic
+novelty claim. A selected task may admit tighter costs than a full-channel
+diamond certificate.
+
+Equation (4a), its scope/support and its calibration uncertainty are paid
+inputs. A smooth recorded scalar by itself does not establish a smooth
+conditional bath response. Fine CE preservation is not claimed. This is a
+conditional removal of exact-record collision cost, not removal of the
+correlation-safe router or cross-independence premises.
+
+## 3. The exact partial-independence requirement
+
+Let Omega be an arbitrary joint N-replica state with a measured label/routing
+transcript T. On a branch t, donor j(t) routes to recipient i(t). An ideal
+data permutation has tagged state exactly
+
+\[
+ \Omega_{R_jS_jE_i|t}.                                       \tag{5}
+\]
+
+Consequently full N-copy independence can be replaced by the selection-stable
+cross-marginal condition
+
+\[
+ \Omega_{R_jS_jE_i|t}
+ =\Omega_{R_jS_j|t}\otimes\Omega_{E_i|t}.                     \tag{6}
+\]
+
+This is sufficient, and is necessary if equality is required for all future
+channels and all effects. If (6) fails, the difference of the two states has
+a positive spectral projector that separates them by their trace distance.
+For a limited task menu only indistinguishability under that menu is needed.
+For comparison with a specified unselected cq ensemble, the two conditional
+marginals in (6) must additionally equal the intended sigma_c and tau_c (or
+the declared coarse bath mixture). Otherwise selection changes the target
+marginals even when the conditional cross state factorizes. The iid
+finite-singleton formula is not inferred from (6) alone.
+
+With discrepancy epsilon_t equal to that trace distance, the average
+tagged task-score error is at most \(\sum_t\Pr(t)\epsilon_t\). This statement
+includes conditioning on the entire selection transcript: pairwise
+independence before adaptive matching does not automatically survive its
+selection events. Nor do one-copy statistics certify (6).
+
+**Non-iid success example.** Three fair hidden phase bits conditioned on even
+parity are globally dependent but every pair is independent. Constant C and
+a deterministic 3-cycle satisfy (6), so tagged grafting works exactly. This
+strictly weakens the source's full-iid requirement for the mean. It does not
+supply independent endpoints or a free concentration bound.
+
+## 4. A bath-marginal and reset-probe certificate is insufficient
+
+Take two independent copies of any correlated state \(\rho_{RSE}\), with
+identical bath marginal tau. Compare ideal \(U_0=SWAP_{S_1S_2}\) with
+
+\[
+ U_1=SWAP_{S_1S_2}\otimes SWAP_{E_1E_2}.                     \tag{7}
+\]
+
+Both have exactly the same reduced action on every accessible-register
+input, including arbitrary initial correlations. Both square to identity.
+The complete bath marginal is tau tensor tau before and after (7); even
+complete bath-state tomography sees no change in this marginal.
+
+More strongly, prepare ANY accessible-register probe state xi, possibly
+entangled across the copies and with external references, independently of
+the baths. Because bath SWAP fixes tau tensor tau,
+
+\[
+ U_0(\xi\otimes\tau\otimes\tau)U_0^\dagger
+ =U_1(\xi\otimes\tau\otimes\tau)U_1^\dagger.                 \tag{8}
+\]
+
+Thus every subsequent probe, even a joint bath-and-system measurement,
+has identical calibration data on this reset-input class. Arbitrarily many
+such product-probe process tomographies cannot resolve the ambiguity.
+
+Nevertheless on the native correlated input, U_1 delivers the donor bath
+with the donor state, so the intended conditional decorrelation fails. In
+the u=0.2 phase model the ideal tagged echo score is 0.68; U_1's score is 1.
+The unmatched mass is zero, all local and joint bath marginals agree, and
+the reset-probe certificate is perfect. The error is still 0.32.
+
+This falsifies a proposed acquisition shortcut, not every system-only
+certification protocol. A router audit must constrain action on relevant
+correlations, or use justified locality/no-cross-bath-transfer premises, or
+an adequate family of independently auditable correlated calibration
+states. Merely showing that the bath's state or its product-input channel
+is unchanged cannot furnish that contract.
+
+**Reference-pairing boundary, invented by quantum_information_operation,
+relayed by root and independently checked here.** Let
+\(\rho_{RSE}=|0\rangle\langle0|_S\otimes\Phi_{RE}\). Data SWAP between two
+copies leaves the entire physical state unchanged. A later local SWAP_SE
+returns a Bell pair to each resident reference, scoring 1. Pairing each
+output with the other, donor-tracked reference instead scores 1/4. The
+tagged acquisition identity remains correct: the operational estimand
+includes routing/job/reference assignment. It is not by itself a measure
+of changed resident processor dynamics. Any held-out decision must specify
+this assignment and justify its relevance to the physical job.
+
+## 5. A known virtual alternative trades routing for sampling
+
+Suppose actual local measurement and replacement primitives at the cut are
+certified to act on S alone. Take two independent same-condition copies.
+Measure donor S; send its classical outcome to the recipient; discard the
+recipient S nonselectively and prepare a state determined by that outcome.
+Retain donor R. The recipient environment marginal is tau, independently of
+the donor's conditional reference state. No data-register transport or
+coherent intermodule SWAP is required. This is a score estimator, not an
+entanglement-preserving physical output state.
+
+For d-dimensional S choose a Haar-random orthonormal basis or an appropriate
+finite 2-design/MUB implementation. Define D+ by measuring and preparing
+the observed basis vector. Define D- by measuring and preparing a uniformly
+chosen orthogonal vector in that basis. Averaging gives
+
+\[
+ D_+(A)=\frac{A+I\operatorname{Tr}A}{d+1},\qquad
+ D_-(A)=\frac{dI\operatorname{Tr}A-A}{d^2-1},
+ \qquad \operatorname{id}=dD_+-(d-1)D_-.                     \tag{9}
+\]
+
+For a qubit only the X,Y,Z measurement bases are needed: prepare the same
+eigenstate for D+, the opposite eigenstate for D-. Each branch is a physical
+measure-and-prepare channel. Equation (9), including its extension by an
+arbitrary untouched reference, follows directly by substitution. Its signed
+combination reconstructs \(\sigma_{RS}\otimes\tau_E\) before continuation.
+
+Let gamma=2d-1. Sample + with probability d/gamma and - with probability
+(d-1)/gamma. For an available raw score m in [0,1], the centered estimator
+
+\[
+ Y=\frac12+\gamma\operatorname{sign}(t)(m-\tfrac12)           \tag{10}
+\]
+
+has mean equal to the ideal tagged graft score. Its range has length gamma,
+so independent trials/batches need gamma squared times the ordinary bounded
+score Hoeffding budget. For one qubit the multiplier is 9. For m qubits
+collectively it is \((2^{m+1}-1)^2\), in addition to local basis synthesis,
+reference measurement, full-history preparation, record matching, feedforward,
+readout calibration and bath-safe local-operation costs. Measuring Bell
+fidelity by separate Pauli correlators gives raw range [-1/2,1], whose width
+1.5 must also be charged if comparing with a direct binary Bell projection.
+
+The coefficient norm gamma is optimal among signed decompositions of the
+identity into deterministic entanglement-breaking channels. Indeed, their
+normalized Choi states are separable, with overlap with the maximally
+entangled state at most 1/d. If positive coefficients total a and negative
+coefficients total b, trace preservation gives a-b=1. Unit Choi overlap
+requires 1<=a/d, so a>=d and a+b>=2d-1. Equation (9) attains this. This is
+not a universal lower bound for a particular easy task functional, and it is
+not a new wire-cutting result.
+
+The conditional/coarse matching and selection-stable cross-independence
+conditions of Sections 2-3 apply unchanged to this estimator. Local
+measure-and-prepare bath disturbance does NOT disappear by algebra; a real
+local-operation certificate is still required. System-only benchmarking of
+those primitives does not automatically supply such a certificate.

# Exact oriented free-time actions for the convex complex-tilt family
+
+Date: 15 October 2026. Supplement to NO_LINEAR_SELECTOR.md.
+
+## Result and scope
+
+For real t and rho>0, consider the convex, left-SO(2)-invariant quartic
+
+    C_(t,rho)(X|Y)=|X+(t+i rho)Y|^4.
+
+Let k be any integer and a any complex number. Minimize the action on a strip of width T>0 joining zero to the profile U(y)=a exp(iky), allowing arbitrary smooth multi-frequency strip interiors. Define lambda=rho k and
+
+    I_(lambda,T)=integral_0^T exp((4lambda/3)(T-s)) ds
+      =3(exp(4lambda T/3)-1)/(4lambda),  lambda !=0,
+      =T,                                      lambda =0.
+
+Then the exact fixed-width minimum is
+
+    Incoming_T(0,U)=|a|^4 I_(lambda,T)^(-3).             (1)
+
+The exact return minimum, with the same arbitrary-interior allowance, is
+
+    Return_T(U,0)=exp(4lambda T)|a|^4 I_(lambda,T)^(-3). (2)
+
+Taking the infimum over all positive widths gives
+
+    Incoming(0,U)=(64/27)rho^3(-k)_+^3 |a|^4,
+    Return(U,0)  =(64/27)rho^3( k)_+^3 |a|^4.           (3)
+
+The shear t changes only an optimal phase, not the value. For nonzero a, every fixed-width minimum is attained by a smooth strip. None of the free-width infima in (3) is attained at a finite width: all are limits as T tends to infinity. The trivial profile a=0 has zero action attained at any width.
+
+This is an exact convex-family value calculation, including all compatible interior frequencies. It is not a quasiconvexity advance for negative-valued energies, a solution of the universal left-invariant problem, or a historical novelty claim. Originality remains UNKNOWN.
+
+## 1. Averaging eliminates all interior frequencies except k
+
+Let Phi(x,y) be any smooth competitor with the stated boundary profiles. For theta in the transverse circle, set
+
+    (G_theta Phi)(x,y)=exp(-ik theta) Phi(x,y+theta).
+
+Both boundary profiles are fixed by G_theta. The complex multiplier is a constant output rotation, and the shift is a transverse translation. Therefore C_(t,rho) has the same action on every G_theta Phi.
+
+Average these competitors:
+
+    Psi(x,y)=(1/(2pi))integral_0^(2pi) G_theta Phi(x,y) dtheta
+            =r(x)exp(iky).
+
+Convexity of C_(t,rho), applied pointwise to the gradient and then integrated, gives action(Psi)<=action(Phi). Thus restricting to this single transverse mode does not change the global fixed-width infimum. The reverse inequality holds because single-mode strips are admissible competitors.
+
+This is an energy-decreasing symmetry projection justified by convexity. The same argument cannot be imported for a general rank-one-convex nonconvex quartic.
+
+## 2. Phase gauge and exact Holder bound
+
+For Psi=r(x)exp(iky), the complex quantity inside the fourth power is
+
+    (r'+ikt r-rho k r)exp(iky).
+
+Write r(x)=exp(-ikt x)z(x). The action becomes
+
+    integral_0^T |z'-lambda z|^4 dx,
+    z(0)=0, z(T)=exp(ikt T)a
+
+for an incoming path. Put v=z'-lambda z and A=exp(ikt T)a. The endpoint equation is
+
+    A=integral_0^T exp(lambda(T-s))v(s) ds.
+
+Holder's inequality with exponents 4 and 4/3 gives
+
+    |A| <= (integral_0^T |v|^4 ds)^(1/4)
+             I_(lambda,T)^(3/4).
+
+Therefore the action is at least |a|^4 I_(lambda,T)^(-3).
+
+Equality is achieved by the explicit smooth control
+
+    v(s)=A exp(lambda(T-s)/3)/I_(lambda,T).              (4)
+
+Indeed its endpoint integral equals A and its fourth-power integral equals |A|^4 I^(-3). Solving z'=lambda z+v with z(0)=0 produces a smooth minimizer with exactly the prescribed endpoint. This proves (1).
+
+For a return path z(0)=a and z(T)=0, the endpoint equation instead requires
+
+    integral_0^T exp(lambda(T-s))v(s) ds=-exp(lambda T)a.
+
+The same Holder bound and equality control give (2).
+
+## 3. Free-width limits and attainment
+
+If lambda>0, I increases without bound, so the incoming infimum is zero. For the return value,
+
+    exp(4lambda T) I^(-3)
+      =(4lambda/3)^3(1-exp(-4lambda T/3))^(-3),
+
+which decreases strictly to (4lambda/3)^3.
+
+If lambda<0, I increases strictly to 3/(4|lambda|), so the incoming value decreases strictly to (4|lambda|/3)^3. The return value tends to zero.
+
+If lambda=0, both values are |a|^4/T^3 and tend to zero.
+
+For nonzero a the relevant fixed-width formulas are strictly above their limiting values at every finite T. This proves the nonattainment assertion and (3). The formal controls on an infinite strip explain the limits, but finite-strip limiting sequences suffice for the proof.
+
+## 4. An actual nonlocal nonlinear model, and its limitation
+
+For this convex family define the required supply on an arbitrary smooth profile U by the infimum of incoming actions over all finite widths and compatible strips from zero to U. Pointwise nonnegativity gives a lower bound zero. A unit-width straight strip gives a finite upper bound. Thus the value is finite without invoking quasiconvexity.
+
+Concatenating an almost minimizing incoming strip with any prescribed transition proves that this value is a dominating profile functional. Piecewise smooth concatenations can be smoothed near their joins while keeping the outer traces fixed and approximating the quartic action in W^(1,4). This is the established required-supply construction; its existence here is independently secured by pointwise nonnegativity.
+
+Equation (3) computes its value on every individual circular Fourier mode even though its definition allows arbitrary-frequency interiors. It has quartic amplitude scaling, cubic frequency scaling, orientation sensitivity and cubic dependence on the ellipticity parameter rho.
+
+This is a useful exact model for a genuinely nonlocal, nonlinearly coefficient-dependent construction. It does not solve the hard part of extending it to negative-valued rank-one-convex energies: there the required-supply lower bound is not automatic. The supplement is not offered as a renamed no-negative-cycle solution.
+
+Any normalized dominating functional for C_(t,rho) must lie between negative return cost and incoming cost. Therefore on a mode,
+
+    -(64/27)rho^3(k)_+^3|a|^4
+       <= P_C(a exp(iky))
+       <= (64/27)rho^3(-k)_+^3|a|^4.                    (5)
+
+Both sides are the sharp extremal-storage bounds: incoming required supply dominates, and negative return cost also dominates by concatenation. They give an exact calibration test for nonlinear proposals.
+
+## Verification and provenance
+
+The proof is analytic, based on convex group averaging, a scalar linear ODE and Holder equality. The accompanying verify_no_linear_selector.py additionally checks the finite-T equality-control integrals and free-width constants by exact symbolic calculation. It does not sample all competing fields.
+
+The general storage/required-supply framework is prior:
+
+[J. C. Willems, Dissipative Dynamical Systems, Part I: General Theory (1972)](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF00276493).
+
+Convex averaging, linear controllability and Holder duality are standard ingredients. No comprehensive priority search for the present explicit family formula was performed. Originality is UNKNOWN.
+

# Electrodynamic and structural derivations
+
+15 October 2026. Independent internal audit, not external validation. Historical originality UNKNOWN. These are conditional results with explicitly specified optical and structural models. No laboratory response, hot material parameters, useful transformation, or industrial advantage was acquired.
+
+## 1. What the source pressure actually assumes
+
+Let true inversion-related variants have bulk response `chi_s^(2)=s chi_0^(2)`, `s=±1`, in the same laboratory axes. This relation must be checked for the actual APB; the name “antiphase domain” alone does not establish it. The linear responses can agree while the third-rank response changes sign. Let a scalar contraction of that tensor be real, local, instantaneous and weak enough for perturbation theory. At a prescribed electric field the nonlinear contribution to the effective material potential is
+
+\[
+f_s(E)=-\epsilon_0s\chi_{\rm eff}^{(2)}E^3/3.
+\]
+
+This is a fixed-field effective potential, not the complete stored electromagnetic/material energy of a driven dispersive system. With peak fields `E1,E2`,
+
+\[
+E(t)=E_1\cos\omega t+E_2\cos(2\omega t+\phi),\qquad
+\overline{E^3}=\tfrac34E_1^2E_2\cos\phi,
+\]
+
+so
+
+\[
+f_s=-s h\cos\phi,\quad h=\epsilon_0\chi_{\rm eff}^{(2)}E_1^2E_2/4,
+\quad p_0=2h.
+\]
+
+Positive pressure is defined to expand `s=+1`. The source's prefactor is consistent with these assumptions; this audit does **not** identify an algebraic error in it. An absorption/injection coefficient alone does not supply this conservative potential. Nor does an arbitrarily chosen real room-temperature SHG coefficient certify a hot, carrier-loaded, moving-wall force.
+
+For dispersive transparent normal modes the safe reduced model is a calibrated Hermitian interaction
+
+\[
+H_{\rm int}=\hbar[g(X)b^\dagger a^2+g(X)^*b(a^\dagger)^2],\qquad
+F_X=-2\hbar\operatorname{Re}[g'(X)\beta^*\alpha^2].
+\]
+
+The modes must be normalized by their full dispersive field-plus-material energy, with their actual hot optical boundary conditions. The force is a partial derivative at fixed canonical optical state; it is not the total derivative of the energy after replacing the amplitudes by arbitrary steady-state functions of `X`. Driving, damping and changes of the optical state must then be evolved separately. If linear mode frequencies also depend on wall position, the ordinary term `-hbar sum_j omega_j'(X) Nj` and any dissipative-coordinate forces must be included; equality of the ideal bulk variants' linear response does not remove an APB's own localized response. Quesada–Sipe's nonlinear quantization analysis is a relevant warning about canonical variables, not a proof that this fixed-field source formula is wrong. [Primary paper](https://opg.optica.org/ol/abstract.cfm?uri=ol-42-17-3443).
+
+## 2. Exact wall-overlap pressure and thickness cancellation
+
+Assume prescribed, undepleted forward fields. Absorb the real tensor contraction and amplitude product into `h(r)≥0`; write the relative phase as `Phi+q·r`, with `q=2k_omega-k_2omega` (changing this convention only reverses phase signs). The interaction is

+\[
+U[s]=-\int s(\mathbf r)h(\mathbf r)
+       \cos(\Phi+\mathbf q\!\cdot\!\mathbf r)\,dV.
+\]
+
+For a wall whose positive-variant side expands with normal displacement `delta X`, its virtual-work pressure is
+
+\[
+p(\mathbf r)=2h(\mathbf r)\cos(\Phi+\mathbf q\!\cdot\!\mathbf r).
+\]
+
+The generalized force on **rigid translation of the entire wall** is the surface integral of this pressure. For a rectangular uniform wall of tangent lengths `L1,L2` and normal position `X`,
+
+\[
+\frac{F_X}{A}=p_0\prod_{j=1}^2
+\operatorname{sinc}(q_{tj}L_j/2)
+\cos(\Phi+q_nX+\mathbf q_t\!\cdot\!\mathbf r_c),
+\quad \operatorname{sinc}x=\sin x/x.
+\]
+
+**Consequences.** A tangent direction spanning an integer beat length `2pi/|q_t|` has exactly zero net force in this uniform lossless model, for every externally set phase. An infinite flat wall has zero mean pressure if there is any nonzero tangent mismatch. A finite thin wall can survive this restriction. Net-force cancellation does not imply every patch of a flexible wall is stationary: opposite local pressures can bow it or write different polarities at different depths.
+
+In a film, if the wall spans `0<z<d`, the two internal intensity attenuation coefficients are `alpha1,alpha2`, and no reflections or depletion occur, the normalized overlap is
+
+\[
+W(d)=\frac1d\int_0^d e^{-az+iq_zz}dz
+=\frac{1-e^{-(a-iq_z)d}}{d(a-iq_z)},\qquad
+a=\alpha_1+\alpha_2/2,
+\]
+
+\[
+\bar p=p_0\operatorname{Re}[e^{i\Phi}W(d)],\qquad
+|\bar p|\le p_0|W(d)|\le p_0\frac{1-e^{-ad}}{ad}\le p_0.
+\]
+
+At `a=0`, `W=exp(i q_z d/2) sinc(q_z d/2)`. At nonzero attenuation the exact sinc zeros generally lift; that does not restore a uniformly driven thick volume. Standing waves, multiple reflections, changing tensor projections and pump depletion require their measured complex overlap instead of this forward-wave formula.
+
+Using **only** Skauli et al.'s original 22 °C dispersion fit, the fundamental/SH pair 2.3/1.15 µm has `Lc=pi/|q|≈5.01 µm`, while 4.6/2.3 µm has `Lc≈40.97 µm`. The corresponding uniform 400 nm overlap magnitudes are 0.99738 and 0.99996. Therefore this propagation theorem is **not** a demonstrated cancellation of the proposed 400 nm film. The fit's temperature measurements extend only to 95 °C; no 650 °C refractive index is extrapolated here. [Original author-uploaded paper, Eq.13/Table II](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/241151797_Improved_dispersion_relations_for_GaAs_and_applications_to_nonlinear_optics).

+For common external propagation directions on a planar film, tangential wavevector conservation can make the in-plane components of `q` zero even when the internal normal components differ. A lateral wall can then see position-independent average pressure while the phase varies through its thickness. The theorem must be applied using the wall orientation, not simply the optical path length.
+
+## 3. Fixed-phase drift obstruction and a conditional moving-phase alternative
+
+If mismatch projects onto the direction of wall motion, `q_n!=0`, and the tangent overlap remains fixed, write
+
+\[
+p(X)=P\cos(q_nX+\Phi),\qquad
+U(X)/A=-P\sin(q_nX+\Phi)/q_n.
+\]
+
+Then
+
+\[
+\int_X^{X+2\pi/|q_n|}p(x)dx=0.
+\]
+
+A static optical phase thus creates a periodic potential, not an indefinitely directed bulk pressure. Under deterministic isothermal gradient motion `Xdot=M p(X)`, with positive mobility and no other force, the wall approaches a stable zero of the force rather than traversing repeated cells. Thermal detailed balance in this static periodic potential likewise gives no stationary directed current. Depletion, spatial temperature variation, nonthermal carriers, radiation recoil or moving phases can escape this narrow result and must be accounted for as different driven mechanisms.

+A useful mechanism mutation is to translate the phase pattern: `Phi(t)=-q_n v t`. With `eta=q_n(X-vt)`,

+\[

+For positive `q_n`, a stable locked solution exists if `|v|<MP`; choose the root with `sin eta>0`. It advances a **freely moving** wall at the programmed speed. The input sources supply power `F v` and all loss. The experiment would compare positive/negative phase-ramp velocity and zero-ramp controls, with independently measured optical overlap and temperature/carriers. This is a conditional optical conveyor interpretation; moving optical potentials are established physics and historical originality of this APB application is UNKNOWN. It removes the static-phase travel restriction, not pinning, absorption, tensor zeros, duty-cycle limits or retention obligations. It is unnecessary when `q_n=0` and a uniform pressure is already available.
+
+For an ideal thick one-dimensional system with `f=-h s(z) cos(qz)`, minimizing local optical energy instead favors `s(z)=sign cos(qz)`. Over an integer number of periods this pattern gains `2h/pi` energy per volume but introduces `|q|/pi` walls per length. With constant wall energy `gamma`, it beats a uniform variant only when

+\[
+p_0=2h>\gamma |q|.
+\]
+
+Hence domain inversion used to quasi-phase-match the optical coupling is not an independent free resource while those same domains are being removed. This comparison assumes sharp freely creatable walls, fixed field and isotropic wall energy; it is not a hot-GaAs nucleation prediction.

+## 4. SHG backaction, no-seed symmetry and energy balance
+
+For the closed resonant three-wave interaction,
+
+\[
+\dot\alpha=-i2g^*\alpha^*\beta,\qquad
+\dot\beta=-ig\alpha^2.
+\]
+
+Set `Z=g beta* alpha^2`. Direct calculation yields
+
+\[
+\dot N_a=-4\operatorname{Im}Z,\qquad
+\dot N_b=2\operatorname{Im}Z,\qquad
+\frac d{dt}(N_a+2N_b)=0.
+\]
+
+Conservative force samples a real quadrature; frequency conversion samples an imaginary quadrature. Zero **instantaneous** conversion is therefore compatible with nonzero force. It does not provide sustained uncharged work: amplitudes/phases or coupling energy change, and a driven steady state must supply mechanical work and dissipation. For a stationary apparatus a complete energy boundary is
+
+\[
+\frac d{dt}(U_{\rm optical+material}+E_{\rm mechanical})
+=P_{\rm drive}-P_{\rm outgoing}-P_{\rm absorbed}.
+\]
+
+For a closed cycle returning both mechanics and all optical/material states, net delivered work is bounded by supplied work minus losses. There is no new energy source.
+
+For a cavity with an undepleted fundamental and **no independent SH seed**,
+
+\[
+\beta=-ig\alpha^2/(K-i\Delta_2),\qquad K=\kappa_2/2.
+\]
+
+For real `g,g'`,
+
+\[
+F_X^{\rm self}=-\frac{\hbar|\alpha|^4\Delta_2}
+{K^2+\Delta_2^2}\,\partial_X|g|^2.
+\]
+

Complex overlaps can carry recoil forces, but the same global parity remains. A target crystal's **own** generated harmonic cannot by itself supply an independently chosen polarity reference. A separately phase-locked injected SH field can do so; its cross term is odd under seed phase reversal while the self-generated contribution is even. This is a design restriction, not a falsifier of the source, which explicitly supplies both colors.
+

+## 6. Root topology, capillarity and why surface disappearance can mislead
+
+Suppose a film-spanning wall has fixed substrate root `X(0)=0`, free top at `z=d`, isotropic positive wall tension `gamma`, uniform pressure `p`, and no interface registry change. Its energy per transverse length is
+
+\[
+\mathcal E[X]=\gamma\int_0^d\sqrt{1+X'(z)^2}\,dz
+-p\int_0^d X(z)\,dz.
+\]
+
+The Euler–Lagrange equation and natural free-top condition give
+
+\[
+\frac{X'}{\sqrt{1+X'^2}}=\frac p\gamma(d-z),\quad X'(d)=0.
+\]
+
+For `r=|p|d/gamma<1`,
+
+\[
+X(d)=\frac\gamma p[1-\sqrt{1-(pd/\gamma)^2}]
+=\frac{pd^2/\gamma}{1+\sqrt{1-r^2}}
+\simeq\frac{pd^2}{2\gamma}.
+\]
+
+The last rationalized form is numerically stable. The root remains present regardless of apparent surface progress. At `|p|d/gamma>=1` this graph-equilibrium solution fails; that failure alone neither proves depinning nor authorizes an interface reconstruction. A rooted APB cannot be erased through the whole film while its root boundary condition is held fixed. Contact-line motion, root release or an annihilation path is an additional structural process.
+
+Rubel–Baranovskii's relaxed static DFT result `gamma_{110}=28 meV/Å²≈0.44861 J/m²` supplies a **normalization**, not a measured 650 °C wall tension/stiffness. +

+\[
+\mathcal E(R)=2\pi R d\gamma-\pi R^2d p,\qquad
+\dot R=M(p-\gamma/R).
+\]
+
+Phase reversal cannot reverse the direction of radius drift if `|p|<gamma/R`; both phases still shrink the island. This is not an acquired hot critical radius; the exact same-regime falsifier is the **measured** inequality `p_max R < gamma_hot` in this model. A flat unrooted wall avoids this capillary threshold but still needs acquired mobility/pinning and retained exit behavior.

+## 7. Coupled loss, carriers, timing and a constrained beam ratio

+At a fixed measured state, the phase-even channel contributions can be organized as

+\[

+The full loss can additionally contain coherent interference terms such as `q_Phi=2 Re[D E2* E1²]`, plus propagation-mediated changes of absorption. Coefficients depend on temperature, carrier populations, optical polarization, spectrum, defect state and the boundary. +def mon(z,w):
+ z,w=torch.broadcast_tensors(z,w)
+ u=z.abs()**2;v=w.abs()**2;prod=z.conj()*w;q=prod.imag;dot=prod.real
+ return torch.stack([u*u,v*v,u*v,dot*dot,u*dot,v*dot,q*u,q*v,q*dot],dim=-1)
+class Full(Basis):
+ def tensor_storage(self,cr):
+  c=torch.view_as_complex(cr.contiguous())
+  vx=((self.E*self.ns.abs()[None,:])*c[None,:])@self.B
+  py=((self.E*(1j*self.ns)[None,:])*c[None,:])@self.B
+  return .5*(mon(vx,py).mean(-2)*self.wt[:,None]).sum(0)
+ def deficit(self,cr,vr,pc,coef):
+  c=torch.view_as_complex(cr.contiguous());v=torch.view_as_complex(vr.contiguous())
+  py=(1j*self.ns*c)@self.B;vx=v@self.Bv
+  p=torch.tensor(pc)
+  st=self.tensor_storage(cr)
+  P=coef*(st[6:]*p[6:]).sum()
+  g=torch.autograd.grad(P,cr,create_graph=True)[0]
+  dp=(g*vr[[i for i,n in enumerate(self.nv.tolist()) if n]]).sum()
+  n4=((vx.abs()**2+py.abs()**2)**2).mean()
+  L=(mon(vx,py)*p).sum(-1).mean()

+ def dvec(self,cr,vr,coef):
+  c=torch.view_as_complex(cr.contiguous());v=torch.view_as_complex(vr.contiguous())
+  py=(1j*self.ns*c)@self.B;vx=v@self.Bv
+  d=mon(vx,py).mean(0)
+  st=self.tensor_storage(cr)
+  ids=[i for i,n in enumerate(self.nv.tolist()) if n]
+  corr=[]
+  for i in range(6,9):
+   g=torch.autograd.grad(st[i],cr,retain_graph=True)[0]
+   corr.append((g*vr[ids]).sum())
+  d=d-torch.cat([torch.zeros(6),coef*torch.stack(corr)])
+  n4=((vx.abs()**2+py.abs()**2)**2).mean()

+

+Requires Python 3.10+ and NumPy. Run: python verify.py
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+import json
+from fractions import Fraction
+from itertools import product
+from pathlib import Path
+import numpy as np
+
+TOL = 2e-12
+RNG = np.random.default_rng(20261015)
+
+
+def density(v: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
+    return np.outer(v, v.conj())
+
+
+def tensor(*ops: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
+    out = np.array([[1.0 + 0j]])
+    for op in ops:
+        out = np.kron(out, op)
+    return out
+
+
+def marginal(rho: np.ndarray, dims: tuple[int, ...], keep: tuple[int, ...]) -> np.ndarray:
+    """Partial trace, preserving the requested order of retained subsystems."""
+    if len(set(keep)) != len(keep) or any(k < 0 or k >= len(dims) for k in keep):
+        raise ValueError("Invalid retained-subsystem indices")
+    dim = int(np.prod(dims))
+    if rho.shape != (dim, dim):
+        raise ValueError("Density matrix shape does not match subsystem dimensions")
+    rest = tuple(k for k in range(len(dims)) if k not in keep)
+    order = keep + rest
+    kdim = int(np.prod([dims[k] for k in keep]))
+    rdim = int(np.prod([dims[k] for k in rest]))
+    arr = rho.reshape(dims + dims).transpose(order + tuple(k + len(dims) for k in order))
+    return np.trace(arr.reshape(kdim, rdim, kdim, rdim), axis1=1, axis2=3)
+
+
+def swap_matrix(dims: tuple[int, ...], a: int, b: int) -> np.ndarray:
+    if dims[a] != dims[b]:
+        raise ValueError("Swapped subsystems must have equal dimensions")
+    dim = int(np.prod(dims))
+    result = np.zeros((dim, dim), dtype=complex)
+    for i in range(dim):
+        coord = list(np.unravel_index(i, dims))
+        coord[a], coord[b] = coord[b], coord[a]
+        result[np.ravel_multi_index(tuple(coord), dims), i] = 1
+    return result
+
+
+def apply_permutation(rho: np.ndarray, unitary: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
+    # All unitaries passed here are computational-basis permutation matrices.
+    order = np.argmax(unitary, axis=1)
+    return rho[np.ix_(order, order)]
+
+
+def td(a: np.ndarray, b: np.ndarray) -> float:
+    delta = (a-b + (a-b).conj().T)/2
+    return float(np.abs(np.linalg.eigvalsh(delta)).sum()/2)
+
+
+def random_state(dim: int) -> np.ndarray:
+    m = RNG.normal(size=(dim, dim)) + 1j*RNG.normal(size=(dim, dim))
+    rho = m @ m.conj().T
+    return rho / np.trace(rho)
+
+
+I2 = np.eye(2, dtype=complex)
+X = np.array([[0,1],[1,0]], dtype=complex)
+P0, P1 = np.diag([1.,0.]), np.diag([0.,1.])
+PLUS = np.array([1,0,0,1], dtype=complex)/np.sqrt(2)
+MINUS = np.array([1,0,0,-1], dtype=complex)/np.sqrt(2)
+BELL = density(PLUS)
+BELL_MINUS = density(MINUS)
+CZ = np.diag([1.,1.,1.,-1.])
+ECHO = tensor(I2, CZ)  # subsystem order R,S,E
+BELL_READ = tensor(BELL, I2)
+
+
+def memory_state(u: float) -> np.ndarray:
+    return (1-u)*tensor(BELL, P0) + u*tensor(BELL_MINUS, P1)
+
+
+def bell_success(rho: np.ndarray, echo: bool) -> float:
+    state = ECHO @ rho @ ECHO.conj().T if echo else rho
+    return float(np.trace(BELL_READ @ state).real)
+
+
+def run() -> dict:
+    results: dict = {
+        "scope": "Synthetic finite checks; no experimental data and no novelty/advantage certification",
+        "seed": 20261015,
+    }
+    # 1. An arbitrary mixed RSE state, including quantum correlations, not only a classical toy.
+    max_error = 0.0
+    max_rs_error = 0.0
+    for _ in range(32):
+        dims = (2,2,3)
+        rho = random_state(12)
+        pair = tensor(rho, rho)
+        sw = swap_matrix(dims+dims, 1, 4)
+        exchanged = apply_permutation(pair, sw)
+        # Recipient site 1 now contains donor S2: follow donor reference R2.
+        graft = marginal(exchanged, dims+dims, (3,1,2))
+        target = tensor(marginal(rho, dims, (0,1)), marginal(rho, dims, (2,)))
+        max_error = max(max_error, td(graft, target))
+        max_rs_error = max(max_rs_error, td(marginal(graft, dims, (0,1)), marginal(rho,dims,(0,1))))
+    assert max_error < TOL and max_rs_error < TOL
+    results["random_quantum_identity"] = {
+        "instances":32, "dimensions_R_S_E":[2,2,3],
+        "maximum_trace_distance": max_error,
+        "maximum_reference_system_marginal_error":max_rs_error,

+    u = [Fraction(1,5), Fraction(2,5)]

+    rows = []
+    for n in [2,4,8,16,32,64]:

+        assert abs(f-ideal_echo) <= singleton_mass

+                     "echo_fidelity":float(f),"isolate_fidelity":float(isolate),
+                     "echo_fidelity_exact":str(f)})

+    max_enum_error = 0.0
+    for n in range(2,9):

+f=t*cs(1)-S.Rational(1,5)*t*t*sn(2)-S.Rational(1,6)*t**3*cs(3)

+    u=z.abs()**2;v=w.abs()**2;q=(z.conj()*w).imag

+    return -14.5*q*u-12*q*v
